events.title: THE KNIGHT WHO WON BY ACCIDENT
events.text: {{other}} boasts of never losing a duel. You discover the previous opponents were paid to surrender. Unfortunately, the next challenge has just been addressed to you.

choices.label: Ask the champion what surrender pays

outcome.text: {{other}} gives you six gold to preserve the legend. You fall over after a magnificently unconvincing blow and spend the walk home rehearsing a better groan.

choices.label: Invite the previous opponents to demonstrate

outcome.text: Three former victims demonstrate the same fatal stagger. {{other}} objects that you have organised a very unfair rehearsal.

choices.label: Insist on a real practice bout (injury risk)

outcome.text: {{other}} has to lift a sword without paying anyone first. The spectators become attentive for entirely new reasons.

stakes.summary: A real bout can injure either opponent.

events.title: THE LOVE LETTER THAT ESCAPED
events.text: Your private love letter has reached the wrong hearth. Three neighbours consider the description flattering. {{spouse}} would like to know which of them resembles a summer orchard.

choices.label: Read the original aloud, including the intended name

outcome.text: {{spouse}} hears the name before the unfortunate fruit comparison. The misunderstanding ends; the orchard will take longer to live down.

choices.label: Claim it was an exercise for a travelling poet

outcome.text: {{spouse}} asks you to recite another verse. Your sudden objection to poetry is much less convincing than the first letter.

choices.label: Dedicate the entire disastrous poem to your spouse

outcome.text: You recite it under your own window. {{spouse}} pulls you inside before the orchard can acquire another harvest.

events.title: THE NOBLE’S BRILLIANT DISGUISE
events.text: {{other}} arrives in a sack with a coronet underneath and insists the name is “Ordinary John”. Ordinary John would like to hear an honest opinion of the local nobility.

choices.label: Give Ordinary John an ordinary load to carry

outcome.text: {{other}} carries it three steps before requesting the sort of assistance usually reserved for important people. You praise the remarkable speed of the promotion.

choices.label: Describe exactly what the households complain about

outcome.text: {{other}} forgets to disguise the voice halfway through defending the lord. The argument becomes considerably more useful after that.

choices.label: Remark how handsome the disguised lord must be

outcome.text: {{other}} agrees before remembering not to know. You are both obliged to admire the sack for a moment.

events.title: THE WEDDING SPEECH THAT WILL NOT END
events.text: {{other}} asks you to toast a newly married couple. A hiccup arrives after the first name and appears determined to marry it to every sentence.

choices.label: Offer the shortest possible blessing

outcome.text: You say “Happiness”, hiccup once and sit. {{other}} calls it the most efficient speech of the feast.

choices.label: Make the interruption part of a song

outcome.text: The guests join in at the wrong places. {{other}} has to explain to the bride’s aunt that this was not a family custom until five minutes ago.

choices.label: Refuse to surrender the rest of your magnificent speech

outcome.text: The couple finish eating before you finish the introduction. {{other}} moves the candle farther from your sleeve without interrupting the hiccups.

events.title: THE LADDER AT THE WRONG WINDOW
events.text: {{other}} waits below a dark window with flowers. You know the room belongs to an elderly wool sorter who has already opened a bucket.

choices.label: Move the admirer before the bucket tips

outcome.text: {{other}} escapes with dry flowers and a much wetter opinion of the address supplied by a friend.

choices.label: Announce the serenade to its actual audience

outcome.text: The wool sorter demands a second verse. {{other}} receives the bucket only after failing to supply one.

choices.label: Take the first verse yourself

outcome.text: The bucket finds you instead. {{other}} helps wring out your cloak and promises never to praise your voice again.

events.title: THE SLEEVES THAT ARRIVED BEFORE YOU
events.text: {{other}} lends you fashionable sleeves for an important supper. They reach the soup before your hands and the candle before your judgement.

choices.label: Roll them up and admit the loan

outcome.text: You eat with both hands visible. {{other}} asks why nobody told the tailor this was an available arrangement.

choices.label: Continue the magnificent gestures

outcome.text: The left sleeve extinguishes a candle and the right acquires somebody else’s sauce. {{other}} retrieves the sleeves before they can accept a third invitation.

choices.label: Ask your neighbour to hold the spare fabric

outcome.text: The two of you conduct supper like an awkward sail. {{other}} is delighted until asked to steer the pudding.

events.title: THE HERO WITH A RHYME MISSING
events.text: {{other}} commissions a song about your courage. The minstrel has found rhymes for your name, but all of them involve a cowardly act or a skin complaint.

choices.label: Become the hero under a less musical name

outcome.text: The song praises a stranger with your deeds. {{other}} enjoys it until the stranger is credited with paying for supper.

choices.label: Suggest the embarrassing incident yourself

outcome.text: The audience laughs where you intended. {{other}} has to surrender the much worse version prepared for later.

choices.label: Demand that courage rhyme with your name

outcome.text: The minstrel stretches the word across three notes. {{other}} starts coughing at every repetition and finally leaves the room to recover.

events.title: THE CHAMPION’S VERY SMALL WEAPON
events.text: {{other}} challenges you to spit a cherry stone farther than the village champion. The champion is the baker’s grandmother and has removed her good shoes.

choices.label: Compete with suitable respect

success.text: Your stone passes hers. {{other}} congratulates you at a careful distance from the grandmother’s second attempt.

failure.text: Your stone lands in your own collar. {{other}} declares this an entirely different achievement.

choices.label: Judge the distances instead

outcome.text: {{other}} disputes half a thumb’s length until the grandmother offers to demonstrate it against a nearby target. The dispute ends.

choices.label: Kick your stone farther while everyone watches hers

outcome.text: The grandmother has been watching your feet. {{other}} awards you a special prize for having apparently misunderstood the sport.

events.title: THE DANCE WITH ONE INSTRUCTION TOO MANY
events.text: {{other}} teaches a fashionable dance before the lord’s supper. Every step has a name. Your feet know none of them.

choices.label: Offer a simpler village measure

outcome.text: The servants recognise the tune and the nobles borrow their timing. {{other}} calls this the rustic portion of an increasingly successful evening.

choices.label: Invent names for the mistakes

outcome.text: The audience follows the second mistake willingly. {{other}} is obliged to explain why the dance now contains “Avoid the Chair”.

choices.label: Stop before taking anyone else with you

outcome.text: You leave the floor with a bow that requires no assistance. {{other}} praises your judgement in the voice usually used for the injured.

events.title: THE MERCHANT’S FABULOUSLY EMPTY FEAST
events.text: {{other}} invites the important buyers to admire a new fortune. The dishes are magnificent, the portions are tiny and the cook has begun serving the decorations.

choices.label: Turn it into a shared supper

outcome.text: You bring bread and invite everyone to add what they have. {{other}} acquires a warm evening at the cost of a rather cold pretence.

choices.label: Praise the remarkable lightness of every course

outcome.text: The buyers repeat the compliment until {{other}} orders the cook to make something heavy. The cook brings the pot.

choices.label: Leave hungry without exposing the host

outcome.text: {{other}} follows you to the door with an apology wrapped round the last piece of cheese.

events.title: THE HAT THAT FRIGHTENS ITS OWNER
events.text: {{other}} acquires a plumed hat to make an impression at court. A gust makes the plume brush the back of the neck. The resulting leap makes a different impression.

choices.label: Catch the hat before the second attack

outcome.text: {{other}} thanks you and holds the hat at arm’s length for the rest of the introduction.

choices.label: Bow solemnly to the victorious feather

outcome.text: The servants copy the bow. {{other}} removes the plume with the expression of someone dismissing a dangerous officer.

choices.label: Offer to tame the creature yourself

outcome.text: You wear the hat backwards. {{other}} is forced to choose between gratitude and explaining why this looks better.

events.title: THE HERMIT WHO ENJOYS VISITORS
events.text: {{other}} invites you to meet a famous hermit. The hermit offers three courses, asks who else is coming and complains that solitude has been slow this season.

choices.label: Let the lonely host talk

outcome.text: The hermit tells you about the winter. {{other}} quietly stops explaining the advantages of never needing anybody.

choices.label: Invite the hermit to your next supper

outcome.text: The invitation is accepted before you have named a date. {{other}} wonders whether a hermit may bring a companion.

choices.label: Ask whether the wilderness requires a waiting room

outcome.text: The hermit finds an excellent view for you outside. {{other}} remains for the second course.

events.title: THE NOBLE’S PROOF OF COURAGE
events.text: {{other}} offers to demonstrate courage by approaching an allegedly savage pig. The pig is asleep. Its owner recommends leaving both facts undisturbed.

choices.label: Declare the beast subdued before waking it

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts the triumph in a whisper. The pig sleeps through its own defeat.

choices.label: Wake the pig and let courage take its course

outcome.text: The pig rises, sniffs and follows the smell of the feast. {{other}} retreats faster than anyone expected a victory to travel.

choices.label: Show how its owner actually handles it

outcome.text: You lead it away with food. {{other}} asks whether anyone needs to mention the food in the account of your bravery.

events.title: THE RIVAL WHO ARRIVED SIDEWAYS
events.text: {{other}} rides into the square rehearsing a splendid greeting. The saddle begins to turn halfway through it.

choices.label: Hold the reins before the speech falls off

outcome.text: {{other}} completes the greeting from the ground. Thanks follows considerably later, but it does follow.

choices.label: Ask the crowd to admire the new riding style

outcome.text: {{other}} spends the evening explaining how little the incident mattered. By nightfall, even the stable boy knows which side landed first.

choices.label: Offer a private lesson in checking the girth

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts after making it clear that the lesson concerns the saddle’s conduct.

events.title: THE PERSON YOUR SPOUSE KEEPS PRAISING
events.text: {{spouse}} has praised a stranger’s looks three times. You discover the portrait being admired is a very flattering picture of you.

choices.label: Admit the resemblance before demanding an apology

outcome.text: {{spouse}} studies you, then the picture, then asks whether the painter can also improve your hearing.

choices.label: Agree that the stranger seems delightful

outcome.text: You compliment the painted face until {{spouse}} turns it round. Supper includes a surprisingly detailed discussion of modesty.

choices.label: Insist this proves something suspicious anyway

outcome.text: {{spouse}} puts the portrait away. The room becomes less handsome and much less willing to explain itself.

events.title: THE PROPOSAL THAT STUCK
events.text: You plan a graceful greeting for {{other}} and take one last bite of pear. The greeting arrives as an urgent request for help with the pear.

choices.label: Start again after you can speak

outcome.text: {{other}} hears the real greeting between two small laughs. The second attempt has fewer ornaments and a better answer.

choices.label: Pretend the coughing was an elaborate bow

outcome.text: {{other}} returns the bow while trying not to laugh. You have introduced an unfortunate new custom between you.

choices.label: Retreat with what remains of your dignity

outcome.text: {{other}} offers water for the retreat. Your dignity has to accept it before leaving.

events.title: THE ROMANCE WITH VERY CLEAR FOOTPRINTS
events.text: {{spouse}} points to two sets of muddy footprints outside a neighbour’s window. Yours lead there and back. You were returning a borrowed kettle; the kettle has not stayed to testify.

choices.label: Fetch the kettle and its owner

outcome.text: The owner arrives carrying the kettle and an excellent memory for the handle you broke. {{spouse}} forgives the supposed romance before discussing the handle.

choices.label: Explain that many people own feet

outcome.text: {{spouse}} agrees, then asks how many of them wear your patched left shoe. The argument acquires a very specific shape.

choices.label: Admit the broken handle before anything else

outcome.text: {{spouse}} asks why a kettle was worth such an impressive effort to appear unfaithful. The two of you finish laughing before supper.

events.title: THE BABY WHO CHOSE THE IMPORTANT GUEST
events.text: {{other}} brings a visiting dignitary to admire a new baby. The baby reaches for the grand chain and immediately decides it is worth tasting.

choices.label: Offer a wooden toy in exchange

outcome.text: The baby releases the chain. {{other}} watches the dignitary thank a piece of wood for succeeding where rank had failed.

choices.label: Congratulate the baby on excellent judgement

outcome.text: {{other}} has to hold the baby while the guest removes the chain. Neither appears willing to be the first to apologise.

choices.label: Take the baby and the responsibility

outcome.text: The baby releases the chain and grips your sleeve. {{other}} calls this a happy transfer of government.

events.title: THE HERO HIDING BEHIND THE RIGHT DOOR
events.text: {{other}} hides from a noisy quarrel behind a cellar door. Opening it lets out the household’s enormous dog, which ends the quarrel immediately. Witnesses are cheering the courage.

choices.label: Praise the dog’s contribution

outcome.text: The owner feeds the actual hero. {{other}} accepts a smaller share of the applause without having to re-enter the cellar.

choices.label: Help improve the story

outcome.text: {{other}} becomes increasingly brave with each telling and increasingly dependent on your silence.

choices.label: Get the frightened neighbour away from the crowd

outcome.text: {{other}} stops shaking once the cheering is two streets away. You let the dog have the rest of the story.

events.title: THE BED MADE FOR A MUCH BETTER PERSON
events.text: {{other}} has raised a bed to show the household’s importance. Getting into it now requires a servant, a stool and a willingness to be seen needing both.

choices.label: Build a small step and name nobody in particular

outcome.text: {{other}} tests the step after everyone has been asked to leave. The furniture finally becomes suitable for sleeping.

choices.label: Admire the view from the floor

outcome.text: {{other}} descends to explain that height is not the point. This takes both the stool and most of the explanation.

choices.label: Suggest returning the legs to ordinary length

outcome.text: The carpenter lowers the bed while {{other}} is away. You are thanked for the comfort and blamed for the lost elevation.

events.title: THE FAMILY FEUD LEARNS A TUNE
events.text: {{other}} whistles a tune associated with an old family insult. Half the lane recognises the insult; the other half keeps asking for the next verse.

choices.label: Supply an embarrassingly affectionate new verse

outcome.text: The tune survives as a love song nobody wants to claim. {{other}} finds it much harder to whistle threateningly.

choices.label: Sing the insulting verse back (family feud)

outcome.text: The lane learns both versions. Your households now possess a quarrel that can be performed without either of you being present.

familyFeud.reason: Public exchange of a family insult

choices.label: Ask what the quarrel is actually about

outcome.text: {{other}} begins with a grandfather, loses track of a cousin and finally admits to never having met either. You agree to leave them out of supper.

events.title: THE COMPLIMENT YOUR RIVAL BELIEVED
events.text: {{other}} mistakes your sarcastic praise for a sincere recommendation. The resulting bow is so grateful that the audience has stopped laughing.

choices.label: Let the compliment become true

outcome.text: You help finish the task you had intended to mock. {{other}} thanks you a second time. Resenting the first was much easier.

choices.label: Explain the joke at full volume

outcome.text: The crowd understands. {{other}} understands more than you meant to teach.

choices.label: Suggest a more modest first attempt

outcome.text: {{other}} tries it and succeeds. You are left in the awkward position of having given useful advice.

events.title: THE SUITOR WHO BROUGHT A PROPMAN
events.text: {{other}} rehearses a flattering speech to you. A friend behind the hedge supplies the forgotten words and, on one occasion, the wrong beloved’s name.

choices.label: Ask the hedge whether it wishes to join the conversation

outcome.text: The prompter crawls out. {{other}} delivers the remaining sentence without help, and it is much better for being short.

choices.label: Teach the suitor to ask a real question

outcome.text: {{other}} asks what you would actually enjoy doing. The hedge, having no prepared answer, is finally quiet.

choices.label: Leave before the hedge proposes marriage

outcome.text: {{other}} bows alone. The prompter supplies an ending to somebody who is already walking home.

events.title: THE TRIUMPH THAT REACHED THE WRONG HOUSE
events.text: {{other}} returns from a modest errand beneath a garland and two borrowed banners. The procession stops at your house because nobody thought to ask where the hero lived.

choices.label: Offer the hero a seat and water

outcome.text: {{other}} sits among the abandoned banners and admits the errand concerned a missing shoe. You ask whether it has returned in triumph too.

choices.label: Lead the procession to the actual destination

outcome.text: The neighbours cheer when the right door finally opens. {{other}} has to acknowledge your contribution to the navigation.

choices.label: Accept the applause yourself

outcome.text: You bow until somebody asks what you did. {{other}} supplies the answer with the joy of someone finally useful to the ceremony.

events.title: THE WAKE THAT STARTED TOO EARLY
events.text: {{parent}} falls asleep during preparations for an elderly neighbour’s wake. A visiting mourner begins praising the wrong person’s virtues. {{parent}} opens one eye at the first exaggeration.

choices.label: Make the introduction before the speech improves

outcome.text: The mourner is relieved to discover a living critic. {{parent}} asks to keep the part about generosity for another occasion.

choices.label: Let your parent hear the affectionate part

outcome.text: {{parent}} waits until the kind words are finished before asking for tea. The mourner laughs and stays to share it.

choices.label: Correct the praise as well as the identity

outcome.text: {{parent}} sits up to defend virtues nobody had questioned until you arrived. The actual wake proceeds with rather less help from you.

events.title: THE SPOON GOES DOWN AGAIN
events.text: You drop your spoon. {{carer.intro}} picks it up. By the fifth time, the smile has gone and the spoon is being held very firmly.

choices.label: Drop it once more

outcome.text: {{carer}} catches the spoon before it lands. You squeal with delight. This was meant to discourage you.

choices.label: Give it back with your sweetest smile

outcome.text: {{carer}} kisses your sticky forehead and lets you try feeding yourself. Most of supper reaches your mouth.

events.title: EVERYONE SHOULD BE AWAKE
events.text: {{carer.intro}} has just fallen asleep in the chair beside you. One eye is still open. You would like the other one open too.

choices.label: Shout until both eyes open

outcome.text: {{carer}} lurches upright and bumps the table. You laugh so hard that a tired laugh comes back.

choices.label: Curl up and let them sleep

outcome.text: The chair creaks. {{carer}} sleeps with one hand on your blanket, and you drift off too.

events.title: NO SPOONS ALLOWED
events.text: {{carer.intro}} brings your soup. You have built a wall of bread around the bowl and will not allow the spoon through.

choices.label: Slap away the invading spoon

outcome.text: Soup splashes down your sleeve. {{carer}} wipes you clean while you inspect the hole in your bread wall.

choices.label: Open a little gap

outcome.text: {{carer}} gets a spoonful past the bread. You eat it, look surprised, and allow another.

events.title: THE BOOT WITH A PASSENGER
events.text: A wooden duck fits neatly into {{carer.intro}}’s boot. You push it right down to the toe and wait to see what happens.

choices.label: Fetch your duck when the hopping starts

outcome.text: {{carer}} holds out the boot. You fish out the duck and get a grateful squeeze, though the hopping has stopped.

choices.label: Look as surprised as possible

outcome.text: {{carer}} shakes out the duck. You stare at it in amazement. It is the best acting you have managed so far.

events.title: THE CAT’S NEW NAME
events.text: You give the household cat a new name. {{carer}} asks what happened to its old one.

choices.label: Explain at great length

outcome.text: {{carer}} understands none of the explanation and all of the importance. The cat responds to neither name.

choices.label: Call the cat to demonstrate

outcome.text: The cat leaves. {{carer}} praises your accurate imitation of an adult being ignored.

events.title: THAT IS MY DIRT
events.text: {{carer.intro}} approaches with a wet cloth. You clamp both hands over the patch of mud you have been saving on your cheek.

choices.label: Wriggle like an eel

outcome.text: {{carer}} catches one cheek, then the other. You get muddy fingerprints on the clean one and earn a helpless laugh.

choices.label: Take a corner of the cloth

outcome.text: You scrub your chin while {{carer}} does the difficult parts. Water runs down your neck, but the dirt comes off.

events.title: THE UNRECOGNISED ANIMAL
events.text: You shape a piece of dough and insist it is an animal. {{carer}} guesses carefully.

choices.label: Correct every guess

outcome.text: {{carer}} finally names a creature nobody has seen. You accept the answer and eat its head.

choices.label: Give the creature to your carer

outcome.text: {{carer}} leaves it beside the hearth where it can become bread without ceasing to be important.

events.title: THE BLANKET EXCHANGE
events.text: {{carer}} offers a clean blanket for the old one. The old one knows how to be yours.

choices.label: Hold on to the familiar corner

outcome.text: {{carer}} washes the other end first. The compromise leaves you holding a small but recognised country.

choices.label: Accept the warm replacement

outcome.text: The new blanket smells different. {{carer}} stays until different has stopped meaning alone.

events.title: THE EXTRA PERSON ON THE WALL
events.text: A candle makes a stranger out of {{carer}}’s shadow. The stranger appears to possess a very long nose.

choices.label: Point out the suspicious nose

outcome.text: {{carer}} bows and makes the nose longer. The stranger becomes less frightening and less dignified.

choices.label: Watch from beneath the blanket

outcome.text: {{carer}} moves the candle. The stranger goes home without requiring you to be brave for an audience.

events.title: ONE VERY IMPORTANT THREAD
events.text: {{carer.intro}} gives you the thread to hold while a torn sleeve is mended. You watch the needle as though it might bite.

choices.label: Keep your fist still

outcome.text: {{carer}} finishes the sleeve and pulls it on to show you. You pat the new stitches and are thanked for helping.

choices.label: See how far the thread goes

outcome.text: Much farther than expected. {{carer}} catches the sleeve before it falls apart and gives you a spare length to tug.

events.title: THE NEW HEADMASTER
events.text: A goat eats the lesson sheet. {{peer}} puts a cap on it and seats it in {{teacher.intro}}’s chair. The goat immediately eats the cap.

choices.label: Help {{teacher}} get the goat outside

outcome.text: {{teacher}} holds out a carrot. The goat abandons its chair, while {{peer}} finds you a clean lesson sheet.

choices.label: Let the goat teach the lesson

outcome.text: {{teacher}} waits for a sensible answer. The goat swallows the last bit of cap, and {{peer}} snorts so loudly that you start laughing too.

choices.label: Replace the register with generous new names

outcome.text: You add three absent children and a pig. {{teacher}} asks the pig to read aloud, then takes the pencil away from you.

events.title: THE HAND BEHIND YOUR BACK
events.text: {{teacher.intro}} finds an open inkpot. {{peer}} looks at your blackened hand, then at your face. “Put it in your pocket,” comes the whispered advice.

choices.label: Hold up the inky hand

outcome.text: {{teacher}} hands you a rag. You clean the spill together, and next time the inkpot is left within your reach.

choices.label: Hide it behind your back

outcome.text: You press a perfect black handprint onto your tunic. {{peer}} stuffs a sleeve into their mouth to stop laughing.

events.title: WHO GETS THE STOOL?
events.text: {{peer.intro}} gets the only stool and decides that means choosing every game. The rest of you have a plate of biscuits.

choices.label: Insist everyone gets a turn

outcome.text: {{peer}} listens to each child in turn. By the time a game is chosen, the biscuits are gone.

choices.label: Offer a biscuit for a turn on the stool

outcome.text: {{peer}} takes the biscuit and climbs down. You sit for a minute before sharing it out again.

events.title: THE BOAT THAT HAS NO INTEREST IN COMMAND
events.text: You and {{peer.intro}} launch a wooden boat in the ditch. It shoots under a bridge that neither of you can crawl beneath.

choices.label: Fish it out with a stick

outcome.text: You hook the boat and soak your sleeve. {{peer}} holds your belt so you do not follow it into the ditch.

choices.label: Make the other children pay to watch

outcome.text: The boat vanishes before your grand demonstration. {{peer}} has to return the pebbles while you explain the invisible ship.

events.title: THE CAKE RESERVED FOR A SAINT
events.text: {{peer.intro}} lifts the cloth over a cake saved for the parish feast. There is a great deal of cake and nobody in the room but you.

choices.label: Cover it and wait for the feast

outcome.text: You both wait. The first slices reach you warm, and {{peer}} nudges yours across with the larger corner.

choices.label: Try a little from the far side

outcome.text: You and {{peer}} keep cutting it straight. When the cloth goes back, it sags into a hole big enough to hide a kitten.

events.title: THE BUTTON AT THE CENTRE OF THE WORLD
events.text: {{peer.intro}} has lost a shiny button in the rushes. They are trying very hard not to cry, which makes finding it much more urgent.

choices.label: Get down and search together

outcome.text: You find a bead, a nail and the button. {{peer}} presses the bead into your hand and keeps checking that the button is still there.

choices.label: Promise to find it for a reward

outcome.text: {{peer}} reaches into another pocket and finds it. You pretend you were about to suggest looking there.

events.title: THE APPLE THAT DISPROVES THE SUM
events.text: {{teacher.intro}} lays out apples for a lesson. At the far end of the bench, {{peer}} quietly makes one of the numbers smaller.

choices.label: Point out the missing apple

outcome.text: {{teacher}} asks {{peer}} to count aloud. A mouth full of apple makes this a difficult exercise.

choices.label: Help eat the difficult numbers

outcome.text: {{peer}} slips you a piece. {{teacher}} takes away the apples and gives you both more sums, which are much harder to swallow.

events.title: THE WORD YOU WERE NOT MEANT TO LEARN
events.text: {{carer.intro}} drops a pot and shouts a word you have never heard. {{peer}} leans close. “Say it again.”

choices.label: Ask what it means, quietly

outcome.text: {{carer}} tells you what it means and asks you not to repeat it at chapel. {{peer}} looks as though chapel has just become interesting.

choices.label: Try the new word at full volume

outcome.text: A neighbour drops a spoon. {{carer}} covers your mouth too late, while {{peer}} bends double laughing.

events.title: THE CROWN MADE OF THE WRONG HEDGE
events.text: {{peer}} makes a crown from a hedge nobody has first tested for thorns.

choices.label: Make a safer crown from rushes

outcome.text: {{peer}} accepts the replacement with the dignity of a ruler whose ears have recently been defeated.

choices.label: Prove it is perfectly suitable for royalty

outcome.text: You remove it quickly. {{peer}} agrees that a shorter reign can still be historic.

events.title: ONE PEBBLE TO CROSS
events.text: {{peer.intro}} wants a pebble from anyone crossing a plank over a puddle. You can get around the entire puddle in one step.

choices.label: Step around it

outcome.text: {{peer}} drags the plank to block you. You go around the other end. This continues until both of you are laughing.

choices.label: Help collect the pebbles

outcome.text: You collect six before an adult takes back the plank. {{peer}} lets you keep half the pebbles and blames the adult.

events.title: THE BELL THAT RINGS FOR BISCUITS
events.text: {{peer.intro}} finds a small bell. One ring could bring the whole household running to supper, if anybody had cooked it yet.

choices.label: Put it back before trouble comes

outcome.text: {{peer}} sighs, but helps you return it. The adults finish their work without being dragged away from it.

choices.label: Ring for a splendid imaginary supper

outcome.text: Three hungry adults arrive. {{peer}} looks into an empty bowl and whispers, “Ring it again. Perhaps that makes the food.”

events.title: DO NOT WASH MY POCKET
events.text: {{carer.intro}} empties your pocket before washing your clothes. Out come a stone, a bent nail and something with far too many legs.

choices.label: Explain which things you need

outcome.text: {{carer}} lets you keep the stone. The nail goes on a high shelf and the many-legged treasure goes outside on a shovel.

choices.label: Grab the many-legged treasure

outcome.text: It scuttles up your sleeve. {{carer}} helps shake it out while you discover how quickly you can dance.

events.title: THE LOAF WITH A JOURNEY MISSING
events.text: {{carer}} sends you home from the baker with a loaf. By the time you reach the door, a small section of the journey has been eaten.

choices.label: Explain where the missing piece went

outcome.text: {{carer}} cuts the loaf at the bite. Your share becomes remarkably easy to identify.

choices.label: Describe an unusually precise attack by birds

outcome.text: {{carer}} asks why the birds left teeth marks. Your evidence is returned for further preparation.

events.title: THE DOOR THAT RECORDS YOUR HEIGHT
events.text: {{carer}} marks your height on a doorpost. The previous mark is disappointingly close, considering how much work growing has been.

choices.label: Stand flat and accept the new mark

outcome.text: {{carer}} dates it carefully. There is still room above for years you cannot yet imagine.

choices.label: Improve the measurement with your heels

outcome.text: {{carer}} marks the extra height with a tiny drawing of your feet. The record is accurate in a particularly inconvenient way.

events.title: THE ERRAND THAT NEEDS A RECEIPT
events.text: {{other}} offers you a coin to carry a parcel across the square. The parcel is light; the instructions about not looking inside are unusually heavy.

choices.label: Ask who will receive it before agreeing

outcome.text: {{other}} points to the cobbler. The parcel contains a repaired shoe, and the elaborate secrecy concerns a very large hole in the other one.

choices.label: Decline the mysterious employment

outcome.text: {{other}} crosses the square carrying the parcel. The strange limping walk supplies an explanation you did not have to purchase.

events.title: THE VISITOR WHO GETS THE WARM PLACE
events.text: {{carer}} gives a tired visitor your favourite place by the hearth. {{peer}} suggests testing how long hospitality lasts.

choices.label: Bring your stool alongside

outcome.text: {{carer}} makes room for both. The visitor tells a story worth more than the lost foot of warmth.

choices.label: Explain whose place it really is

outcome.text: {{carer}} hears the explanation and gives the visitor another blanket. {{peer}} suggests your case lacked witnesses.

events.title: THE SIGNATURE BIGGER THAN THE RENT
events.text: {{other}} asks you to witness a rent mark. The tenant cannot read; you can read just enough to see the amount has grown.

choices.label: Read the amount aloud before marking

outcome.text: {{other}} blames a tired clerk and fetches the smaller tally. The tenant watches you finish the word.

choices.label: Mark it and avoid the argument

outcome.text: {{other}} thanks you for being sensible. The tenant pays for the compliment.

events.title: THE MASTERPIECE SMALL ENOUGH TO HIDE
events.text: {{peer}} has made a model of the master’s best work and accidentally improved it. The master is approaching.

choices.label: Name the actual maker

outcome.text: The master inspects the joint twice before asking how it was done. {{peer}} stops hiding the model beneath the bench.

choices.label: Present the model as your work

outcome.text: The master asks you to repeat the joint. {{peer}} watches your second, much less successful masterpiece.

events.title: THE ANSWER IN THE WRONG MARGIN
events.text: {{peer}} has a copy of a test with the answers written in the margin. The scholar’s name is also written there.

choices.label: Return the copy before the test

outcome.text: {{peer}} calls you unreasonable until the scholar starts collecting names as well as papers.

choices.label: Copy the impressive answers

outcome.text: You reproduce the scholar’s name under your own. {{peer}} admires the completeness of your borrowing.

events.title: THE HEN HAS TWO OWNERS AND NO ALLEGIANCE
events.text: {{peer}} catches a hen claimed by two households. It lays an egg during the argument.

choices.label: Compare the owners’ marks

outcome.text: The mark settles ownership. {{peer}} asks whether the egg can remain neutral.

choices.label: Sell the egg while they debate

outcome.text: You gain one gold. {{peer}} has to explain why the hen has suddenly become less productive under joint ownership.

events.title: THE MESSAGE THAT SOUNDS BETTER SHORTENED
events.text: {{other}} entrusts you with a message that contains an apology. {{peer}} says removing that part would make you sound much more important.

choices.label: Deliver the apology exactly

outcome.text: {{other}} hears that you kept the difficult part. The reply is shorter because it no longer has to be angry.

choices.label: Improve the sender’s dignity

outcome.text: Your version reaches the wrong sort of audience. {{other}} asks to hear the exact improvement, without the audience this time.

events.title: THE SWORD THAT REQUIRES TWO HANDS AND PERMISSION
events.text: {{peer}} finds a practice sword and suggests testing it before anyone can ask why you have it.

choices.label: Ask for a safe lesson

outcome.text: The instructor gives you a blunt exercise and a stance that does not involve the nearest wall. {{peer}} has to learn it too.

choices.label: Demonstrate your natural command

outcome.text: The sword strikes a bucket. {{peer}} concedes that the bucket has surrendered, though your wrist disputes the victory.

events.title: THE TRANSLATION THAT IMPROVES THE COOK
events.text: {{teacher.intro}} sets a Latin sentence. {{peer}} reads it as “give the children more pudding” and waits hopefully.

choices.label: Check the word for pudding

outcome.text: The word means patience. {{teacher}} makes you find the right passage, while {{peer}} keeps a finger on the wrong one.

choices.label: Explain why pudding fits the meaning

outcome.text: {{teacher}} asks for the grammar. {{peer}} rubs an empty stomach. It is a strong argument for lunch, but a poor one for Latin.

events.title: THE EXTRA COIN NOBODY HAS CLAIMED
events.text: {{other}} gives you too much change. {{peer}} calculates how long it would take an honest person to notice.

choices.label: Return the extra coin

outcome.text: {{other}} checks the sum and thanks you without making a sermon of it. {{peer}} revises the calculation.

choices.label: Keep the advantage

outcome.text: You pocket the extra coins. {{peer}} asks whether your arithmetic always improves when someone else is paying.

events.title: THE DARE WITH A WITNESS IN EVERY WINDOW
events.text: {{peer}} dares you over a forbidden fence. Every house overlooking it appears empty, except at the curtains.

choices.label: Refuse the audience its entertainment

outcome.text: {{peer}} calls you cautious. The curtains remain disappointed and your coat remains whole.

choices.label: Climb before the witnesses get comfortable

success.text: You cross and return with a leaf caught in your collar. {{peer}} declares the leaf proof of a great expedition.

failure.text: You tear your coat and scrape a knee. {{peer}} offers a version of events in which the fence attacked first.

events.title: THE NICKNAME THAT HAS OUTLIVED THE JOKE
events.text: {{peer.intro}} gives you an unkind nickname. Younger children start repeating it, even when you are close enough to hear every word.

choices.label: Tell them it hurts and ask them to stop

outcome.text: {{peer}} glances at your face and drops the grin. The next time somebody repeats it, they change the subject.

choices.label: Find a crueler name for them

outcome.text: The younger children learn both names. {{peer}} stops laughing and starts using yours whenever an adult turns away.

events.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S FIRST REAL ACCOUNT
events.text: {{carer.intro}} asks you to count the grain sacks. There are fewer than the tally says, and the empty shelf is hard to argue with.

choices.label: Show where the grain is missing

outcome.text: {{carer}} checks the shelf and changes the supper plan. Your careful count leaves a little more grain for the lean week ahead.

choices.label: Write down the reassuring number

outcome.text: {{carer}} finds the bare shelf later and recounts everything. Next time, you have to count with someone watching.

events.title: THE BRIDGE PLAN DRAWN AFTER THE RAIN
events.text: {{peer.intro}} draws a bridge to build from spare boards. There is room for a hero in a cloak, but nothing holding up the middle.

choices.label: Make room for the supports

outcome.text: {{peer}} rubs out the cloak. With two extra supports, your little model stays upright and the bridge might be useful.

choices.label: Test the heroic version

outcome.text: One pebble folds the bridge in half. {{peer}} redraws the hero on the bank, well away from the water.

events.title: THE LETTER THAT HAS MET ITS READER
events.text: {{peer.intro}} has your note. They point to the line about their eyes and wait for you to stop staring at your shoes.

choices.label: Ask the question you meant to ask

outcome.text: You get the words out without a borrowed verse. {{peer}} answers quietly, and neither of you has to involve the whole lane.

choices.label: Say it was a handwriting exercise

outcome.text: {{peer}} reads the line about their eyes again. You decide to become very interested in the weather.

events.title: THE WAGE WITH AN INVISIBLE DEDUCTION
events.text: {{other.intro}} offers to pay you for an errand, then takes back half the wage as a fee for learning how to do it.

choices.label: Ask for the whole wage before you start

outcome.text: {{other}} grumbles, but pays four gold. You do the errand carefully; you would like to be paid again.

choices.label: Take the two gold and get it done

outcome.text: You carry the sack and collect two gold. {{other}} pats your shoulder and asks whether the free instructions made it a fair bargain.

events.title: THE BOOK THAT SHOULD NOT BE THIS INTERESTING
events.text: {{peer.intro}} opens a respectable book at a forbidden page. Somebody has underlined all the exciting parts in red.

choices.label: Read the argument and check it

outcome.text: You find a flaw in the passage and point it out. {{peer}} groans; you have somehow made forbidden reading into more work.

choices.label: Copy the red bits for everyone

outcome.text: The copies are traced to your enormous red initials. {{peer}} quietly turns your name face down.

events.title: THE SHORT WAY PAST THE QUARRY
events.text: {{peer}} knows a quicker path beneath loose quarry stone. The chief recommendation is that nobody responsible has approved it.

choices.label: Take the ordinary road

outcome.text: {{peer}} complains until you arrive with both ankles functioning. The longer story is much less impressive.

choices.label: Take the unstable shortcut

success.text: You cross safely and gain a poor example you can now defend from experience.

failure.text: Loose stone catches your leg. The broken bone ends the outing and begins a real recovery.

events.title: THE REFERENCE WRITTEN BY ITS BENEFICIARY
events.text: {{peer.intro}} writes you a glowing reference. It lists three skills you do not have and one that neither of you can pronounce.

choices.label: Leave in the things you can actually do

outcome.text: {{peer}} keeps one warm compliment and crosses out the rest. The shorter reference gives you something you can build on.

choices.label: Hand over the magnificent version

outcome.text: You are asked to demonstrate the unpronounceable skill. {{peer}} takes a sudden interest in a very distant part of the yard.

events.title: THE BAG FOR THE LIFE BEYOND HOME
events.text: {{carer}} helps pack what you will need for work away from the household. Every practical object seems to carry a longer conversation.

choices.label: Pack slowly and hear the advice

outcome.text: {{carer}} stops pretending the extra bread is merely efficient. You leave the bag by the door and stay for the meal.

choices.label: Pack quickly to prove you are ready

outcome.text: {{carer}} adds the bread after you have finished explaining your independence. You notice it later.

events.title: THE SEED THAT IS ALSO SUPPER
events.text: {{carer}} divides the household’s seed grain. It looks uncomfortably like the food everyone could eat tonight.

choices.label: Keep the sowing reserve and find other work

outcome.text: {{carer}} marks the sack. The evening is lean, but the spring has not been eaten to make it easier.

choices.label: Use the reserve now

outcome.text: The meal is better. {{carer}} counts the missing seed before putting the empty sack away.

events.title: THE SAMPLE BETTER THAN THE GOODS
events.text: {{carer}} shows you a perfect cloth sample and the less perfect consignment. The lesson is about which one customers are allowed to touch.

choices.label: Label the goods by what they are

outcome.text: The lower price earns fewer coins and fewer angry visits. {{carer}} lets you write the next honest description.

choices.label: Sell from the perfect sample alone

outcome.text: You receive four gold. {{carer}} makes you keep the sample for the complaints, where perfection becomes less helpful.

events.title: THE RATION RETURN COUNTS YOU TWICE
events.text: {{carer}} finds two ration entries in your name. The quartermaster describes the second as an administrative child.

choices.label: Correct the duplicate before collecting

outcome.text: The quartermaster crosses out the child. {{carer}} praises your first successful reduction of an army.

choices.label: Collect for both children

outcome.text: The extra food reaches supper before your explanation. {{carer}} puts both signatures beside your bowl and waits for you to discover which one you wrote.

events.title: THE CHAIR THAT OUTRANKS ITS OWNER
events.text: {{carer}} asks you to yield a chair to an important cousin. The cousin has brought a diagram establishing the chair’s ancestors.

choices.label: Move the chair and keep your wit private

outcome.text: {{carer}} sees the concession. The cousin spends supper defending the pedigree to a chair that cannot contradict it.

choices.label: Ask to hear the chair’s whole pedigree

outcome.text: The explanation lasts until the food cools. {{carer}} admires your question less than the audience does.

events.title: THE PRICE OF THE FIRE
events.text: {{other}} offers a healing stone for one fee and its warmth for another. The brazier is plainly visible.

choices.label: Decline the heating fee

outcome.text: You point to the brazier. {{other}} moves it behind a cloth, making the science harder to inspect.

choices.label: Show the customers how it is warmed

outcome.text: The customers warm their own stones. {{other}} has never disliked public education quite so much.

events.title: SILENCE AT THE MARKET RATE
events.text: {{other.intro}} offers to stop repeating a rumour about you. The price is shouted across the market. So is the rumour.

choices.label: Refuse to buy the silence

outcome.text: {{other}} shouts a higher price. Several listeners ask whether shouting costs extra.

choices.label: Repeat the offer to everyone listening

outcome.text: You quote the demand word for word. {{other}} discovers how embarrassing it is to have an exact price put on their discretion.

events.title: THE ANCESTOR WITH TWO EXCLUSIVE FAMILIES
events.text: {{other.intro}} tries to sell you an exclusive pedigree. Two stalls away, the same ancestor has six different descendants and a cheaper frame.

choices.label: Drop the doubtful claim

outcome.text: {{other}} offers a smaller ancestor at half the price. You leave before the family shrinks any further.

choices.label: Swear the pedigree is true

outcome.text: The clerk asks how you met the witness from 1180. {{other}} suddenly has another customer to serve.

charge.offence: Defending an invented pedigree under oath

events.title: THE MEASURE AT THE HEARING
events.text: {{other}} brings a milling measure to a dispute. Its outside is larger than its inside, a distinction the miller would prefer described less clearly.

choices.label: Describe only what you can inspect

outcome.text: The clerk records its capacity. {{other}} objects to a vessel being judged by what it holds.

choices.label: Keep out of the dispute

outcome.text: The measure returns unchanged. {{other}} thanks you for an unusually spacious interpretation of silence.

events.title: QUILLS WITH AN HONEST PARENTAGE
events.text: {{other}} sells ordinary quills with a plain description. The prices are the only part claiming celestial distinction.

choices.label: Welcome the honest description

outcome.text: {{other}} sells a bird’s feather as a bird’s feather. Nobody is asked to kneel.

choices.label: Mock the expensive claims

outcome.text: The buyers laugh and {{other}} closes the box. Accuracy has become personal rather than profitable.

events.title: THE INFORMANT’S WELL-KEPT COPY
events.text: You have a known secret. {{other}} offers to suppress a political accusation already circulating in the market. The offer is the fresh part.

choices.label: Refuse another secret bargain

outcome.text: You state your position publicly. {{other}} discovers that information loses value when its owner can say it aloud.

choices.label: Buy one copy, without trusting it is unique (12g)

outcome.text: {{other}} promises exactly one sheet, which is the most honest part of the interview.

events.title: THE MIRACLE’S EXPENSE ACCOUNT
events.text: {{other}} asks whether shrine donations should buy food or a larger sign describing the shrine’s generosity.

choices.label: Fund food for distribution (8g)

outcome.text: The money becomes bread. {{other}} agrees the sign would have been harder to divide between households.

choices.label: Argue that collecting is enough

outcome.text: {{other}} opens the empty bread basket beside the full account. The distinction needs no Latin.

events.title: THE LUNCH COLLECTOR HAS LOST THE BADGE
events.text: {{other.intro}} takes the other children’s lunches while wearing a leaf as a badge. The oldest children deny sending anyone with a leaf.

choices.label: Stop taking lunches together

outcome.text: {{other}} pulls off the leaf. You both leave the food where its owners can reach it.

choices.label: Demand a lunch as repayment

outcome.text: {{other}} hands it over and looks at you with weary recognition. The leaf is gone, but the children are still losing their lunch.

events.title: THE CARE THAT IS NOT AN INVOICE
events.text: Your mother {{other}} asks whether accepting help means hearing the cost repeated at every meal.

choices.label: Say care is not a debt between you

outcome.text: {{other}} puts away the tally. You talk about the meal while it is warm.

choices.label: Explain every sacrifice you have made

outcome.text: The tally stays on the table. Repetition has not made the sum kinder.

events.title: THE GRIEVANCE WITHOUT THE GLOVE
events.text: {{other.intro}} arrives to tell you exactly what he thinks of you. He says he left his duelling glove at home and shows you both empty hands.

choices.label: Hear Roderick without an audience

outcome.text: Roderick gets through the complaint without reaching for a weapon. Once you answer quietly, he finds rather less to shout about.

choices.label: Give your finest answer in public

outcome.text: Roderick produces the glove. It was in the other pocket. Your audience takes a quick, interested step backward.

events.title: THE LIVING PERSON ON THE DEAD LIST
events.text: {{other}} finds their name on a death assessment and asks whether correcting it will also restore the ordinary taxes.

choices.label: Explain without inventing an exemption

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts that being alive is an expensive legal position, but preferable to the alternative.

choices.label: Help with the assessment (6g)

outcome.text: {{other}} insists the receipt mention that the payer is still breathing.

events.title: THE FEE FOR NOT HAVING DIED
events.text: {{other}} offers to withdraw a doubtful death claim and charge for storing it. The dead are apparently expected to rent parchment.

choices.label: Reject the storage demand

outcome.text: {{other}} calls this unprecedented, then puts the form in a box full of precedents.

choices.label: Read the demand publicly

outcome.text: {{other}} starts searching for a clerk young enough to blame for inventing it.

events.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S EMERGENCY RESERVE
events.text: {{other}} weighs the reserve before hiding it beneath the salt. The weighing is partly arithmetic and partly a question about trust.

choices.label: Add to the reserve (12g)

outcome.text: Your contribution goes under the salt. {{other}} gives you the box instead of watching your hands.

choices.label: Ask to count it together

outcome.text: You count openly. {{other}} stops treating the lid as something that needs a guard.

events.title: THE SIGNATURE YOU DID NOT WRITE
events.text: {{other}} has put your name beneath a loan guarantee. It is a handsome signature for a hand you do not recognise.

choices.label: Refuse the false guarantee publicly

outcome.text: The lender asks {{other}} for their own security. The sudden interest in spelling is unwelcome.

choices.label: Help without endorsing the forgery (8g)

outcome.text: You pay and cross out the supposed signature. {{other}} thanks you more quietly than the money deserves.

events.title: THE CHILD WHO SAW THE HIDDEN GOODS
events.text: Your child {{other}} has found goods hidden from a collector and asks how old a person must be before lying becomes lawful.

choices.label: Answer honestly

outcome.text: You explain the wrong rather than the advantage. {{other}} asks another question; the first answer mattered.

choices.label: Threaten the child into silence

outcome.text: {{other}} stops asking. This is much less reassuring than you expected.

events.title: THE FAMILY SEAL SMELLS OF SOAP
events.text: {{other}} has cut a family seal in soap. The impression is convincing; the basin is full of evidence.

choices.label: Correct the false impression

outcome.text: The document is corrected and the soap used for washing. {{other}} finds both applications disappointing.

choices.label: Use the impression on another paper

outcome.text: The clerk recognises the same bubbles on both. {{other}} has made a very washable conspiracy.

charge.offence: Creating false evidence for the soap-seal advance

events.title: TWO PEOPLE, ONE HOUSEHOLD LIST
events.text: {{other}} wants the household goods counted fairly. The difficult contributions have never fitted on a list.

choices.label: Divide the goods together

outcome.text: {{other}} stops adding the small corrections designed merely to make you listen.

choices.label: Claim every advantage on the list

outcome.text: You keep the better goods. {{other}} keeps a copy that now resembles a description of you.

events.title: THE JOKE YOUR SPOUSE DID NOT ENJOY
events.text: {{other}} asks about your public joke concerning the marriage. The audience has gone, taking most of its persuasive force.

choices.label: Apologise without repeating the punchline

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts before you can improve the apology into another performance.

choices.label: Explain that everybody else laughed

outcome.text: {{other}} asks whether you intend to live with everybody else.

events.title: THE UNCOUNTED WEDDING EXPENSE
events.text: {{other}} brings a wedding bill for an extra musician, borrowed benches and a creditor nobody invited.

choices.label: Help settle the bill (10g)

outcome.text: {{other}} dismisses the extra musician, who had been charging to wait.

choices.label: Refuse to finance the display

outcome.text: The feast shrinks. The creditor is the only guest pleased to see a smaller table.

events.title: THE SINGER AND THE NUMBERED WINDOWS
events.text: {{other}} has hired a serenade below the wrong window. The actual listener is pricing an encore.

choices.label: Correct the mistake quietly

outcome.text: The singer moves a window along. Only one household has learned the entire verse.

choices.label: Tell the street what happened

outcome.text: The street joins the refrain. {{other}} hears their own name more clearly than the lover’s.

events.title: THE RENT ON YOUR OWN SHADE
events.text: Your feuding households disagree again. {{other}} claims rent for a wall’s shade, making the afternoon unusually expensive.

choices.label: Offer a witnessed settlement (11g)

outcome.text: {{other}} hears a concession rather than a threat. The feud remains, but this conversation has not enlarged it.

choices.label: Keep the quarrel public

outcome.text: The crowd laughs. {{other}} adds the audience to an account that was already long enough.

events.title: THE PARDON HAS LEFT ROOM FOR EVERYONE
events.text: You face legal suspicion. {{other}} offers a pardon with the offence left blank: an unusually broad mercy in an unsworn hand.

choices.label: Refuse the doubtful pardon

outcome.text: {{other}} offers a smaller offence at a lower price. The paper becomes less forgiving by the word.

choices.label: Show the blank to the clerk

outcome.text: The clerk fills the space with an inquiry into {{other}}. It is the first named matter the paper has covered.

events.title: THE PIE COMES WITH INSTRUCTIONS
events.text: {{other}} offers you a pie to deliver to a juror. The note inside the crust has not been written by a cook.

choices.label: Refuse to carry the suggestion

outcome.text: {{other}} removes the note and asks about the pie alone. Its innocence has survived less well than its pastry.

choices.label: Correct the approach openly (10g)

outcome.text: {{other}} gets the pie back without the private understanding it was meant to contain.

events.title: THE PRICE OFFERED FOR YOUR SKIN
events.text: {{other}} offers money if you take somebody else’s punishment. The payment is specified more carefully than the scar.

choices.label: Refuse and expose the bargain

outcome.text: The crowd hears the price. {{other}} discovers how cheaply an offer becomes a public description.

choices.label: Listen without accepting the injury

outcome.text: {{other}} explains it without accountancy. The bargain sounds considerably worse.

events.title: THE COFFIN NEEDS ANOTHER RECEIPT
events.text: {{other}} demands a toll from a funeral cart. The deceased must establish residence before being permitted to leave it.

choices.label: Demand the written authority

outcome.text: {{other}} finds no rate for the particular journey being proposed.

choices.label: Pay for the cart’s passage (6g)

outcome.text: {{other}} supplies a receipt that would embarrass any living person asked to present it.

events.title: THE OATH REHEARSED TOO WELL
events.text: {{other}} wants you to repeat a polished account before a clerk. Your current legal difficulties make the friendship unusually attentive.

choices.label: Refuse another doubtful statement

outcome.text: {{other}} folds the script and asks whether you have always been so difficult to assist.

choices.label: Disclose the proposed account

outcome.text: The clerk receives a script instead of an oath. {{other}} did not expect to be its main character.

events.title: THE BARREL HAS MOSTLY CARRIED AIR
events.text: {{other}} disputes a delivery with an excellent barrel mark and little inside. The mark cannot be poured into a cup.

choices.label: Correct the delivery account (10g)

outcome.text: {{other}} signs for what arrived and stops praising the beauty of the cooperage.

choices.label: Stand by the inflated account

outcome.text: {{other}} keeps the barrel as an exhibit. It is lighter than your explanation.

events.title: THE CUSTOMER KEPT THE BROKEN PART
events.text: {{other}} brings defective work and its receipt. The receipt has aged better than the joint.

choices.label: Replace the fault at your expense (10g)

outcome.text: {{other}} keeps the new receipt without requiring an apology to hold the work together.

choices.label: Blame the customer

outcome.text: {{other}} places the broken joint beside the untouched one. The comparison is shorter than your defence.

events.title: THE CREDITOR HAS NEVER BEEN TO SEA
events.text: You owe money. {{other}} explains that water damage is a matter between you and the goods.

choices.label: Review the terms without promising payment

outcome.text: {{other}} reads the terms with you. The loan remains a debt, but neither of you can now describe it differently.

choices.label: Borrow against another promise

outcome.text: The debt acquires a younger sibling. {{other}} has recorded the new promise as carefully as the first.

events.title: THE SILENT PARTNER HAS A SPEECH
events.text: {{other}} proposes a partnership. “Silent” appears to be a title rather than a restriction on giving orders.

choices.label: Agree clear limits before taking money

outcome.text: {{other}} reads the terms twice. Silence has become specific enough to price.

choices.label: Decline the partnership

outcome.text: {{other}} delivers the remaining speech to someone who has not already declined it.

events.title: THE WORD THAT CHANGES THE TESTIMONY
events.text: {{other}} presents a copied statement missing “not”. The clerk calls it a small word, as though size settled its effect.

choices.label: Correct the missing word

outcome.text: The clerk inserts “not” and discovers that the sentence has become more expensive to defend.

choices.label: Destroy the inconvenient original

outcome.text: {{other}} has kept a second copy. Your attempt to improve the evidence has become part of it.

charge.offence: Destroying evidence of a deliberately altered agreement

events.title: THE CERTIFICATE’S INCONVENIENT DATE
events.text: {{other}} queries a medical certificate dated when you were not present. Your profession makes the date more important than the handwriting.

choices.label: Acknowledge the false date

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts the correction and keeps the original. It records what you signed, not what you wish to have meant.

choices.label: Deny changing the date

outcome.text: {{other}} produces the dated envelope. Your memory has developed a very difficult relationship with the post.

events.title: THE PATRON’S ALMOST HARMLESS VERSE
events.text: {{other}} commissions a poem naming no victim until the last line. That line is underlined twice.

choices.label: Keep the point and remove the target

outcome.text: {{other}} complains that everybody could learn from it. You agree to regard this as a defect.

choices.label: Refuse the commission

outcome.text: {{other}} takes the underlined line to a poet with fewer objections and more hunger.

events.title: THE MEN WHO FIT THE MUSTER
events.text: {{other}} brings a muster smaller than the proposed parade. The flags have been ordered for the larger version.

choices.label: Support the true numbers

outcome.text: The spare flags become the only part of the company without duties. {{other}} signs the honest return.

choices.label: Mock the imaginary ranks

outcome.text: The company laughs. {{other}} must defend honesty and the size of the banners at once.

events.title: THE DINNER QUARREL BETWEEN TWO HOUSES
events.text: Your families maintain a feud. {{other}} brings a disputed dining account and a fresh opportunity to explain your relations.

choices.label: Admit your household’s mistake

outcome.text: {{other}} hears an admission rather than an inherited speech. The feud remains, but this meeting has not added to it.

choices.label: Repeat the family accusation

outcome.text: {{other}} writes it down exactly. Both houses now possess another version they will prefer not to correct.

events.title: THE RIVER REFUSES THE DRAWING
events.text: {{other}} maps the river on the profitable side of a boundary. The river is available outside for comparison.

choices.label: Accept a proper survey quietly

outcome.text: {{other}} puts the river where it is. The survey keeps enough dignity to be useful.

choices.label: Explain the first drawing’s advantages publicly

outcome.text: The audience laughs. {{other}} wishes the river had been less cooperative with the joke.

events.title: THE FACE IS SOUND, THE SILVER IS LIGHT
events.text: {{other}} brings coins bearing your royal face and less silver than required. The portrait has suffered no corresponding reduction.

choices.label: Fund an assay and correction (18g)

outcome.text: {{other}} leaves with a written standard rather than another promise about your nose.

choices.label: Blame the people weighing the coins

outcome.text: {{other}} weighs another. The missing silver continues to be absent without asking permission.

events.title: THE VERDICT ARRIVES BEFORE THE WITNESSES
events.text: {{other}} brings the ruler a petition with its conclusion already written. The witnesses have been invited to agree.

choices.label: Hear the evidence first

outcome.text: {{other}} removes the conclusion from the top. The witnesses acquire a purpose they were not promised.

choices.label: Require an ordinary hearing

outcome.text: The petition leaves by the public door. {{other}} has failed to purchase the convenience of your name.

events.title: THE SAINT HAS TWO CHILDHOODS
events.text: {{other}} displays two skulls of one saint, one adult and one child. The smaller is offered at a family price.

choices.label: Support an honest revised label

outcome.text: One skull loses a childhood and gains a description {{other}} can defend.

choices.label: Tell the crowd the original explanation

outcome.text: The crowd asks for the saint’s youth at a middling price. {{other}} closes the case.

events.title: THE OVEN’S EVIDENCE IS ON YOUR HAND
events.text: You live with chronic pain. {{other}} recommends an ordeal by heat, having found no other method of making your day more convincing.

choices.label: Explain what pain does not prove

outcome.text: {{other}} must explain why your existing pain has failed to supply sufficient evidence.

choices.label: Accept practical help instead

outcome.text: {{other}} brings a chair and stops discussing the oven. The day eases; the disability remains.

events.title: THE DONORS SPEAK BEFORE THE BREAD
events.text: {{other}} organises relief. Donors demand their names be read before the recipients eat.

choices.label: Serve food while reading the names

outcome.text: {{other}} reads over grateful chewing. The list finally provides a useful accompaniment.

choices.label: Make the hungry wait for important names

outcome.text: The list is magnificent. {{other}} looks at the cooling food and stops admiring its length.

events.title: THE BANDAGE AND THE SMALL REQUEST
events.text: You have a wound under care. {{other}} helps with the dressing and asks for practical help when you are able.

choices.label: Offer help you can safely give

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts a useful promise instead of an impossible display of gratitude.

choices.label: Reject the obligation

outcome.text: {{other}} finishes carefully. The knot receives more attention than the conversation.

events.title: THE SMALLEST PART OF THE SCAFFOLD
events.text: {{other}} calls a loose scaffold peg too small to matter. Everybody is preparing to stand above it.

choices.label: Explain and fit the support

outcome.text: {{other}} watches the platform stop moving and lowers the peg’s size on the list of objections.

choices.label: Explain mostly your own good sense

outcome.text: {{other}} fits the peg while you conclude. One contribution makes the scaffold safer.

events.title: THE GUARANTEE FITS IN THE BOTTLE
events.text: {{other.intro}} points to a tonic’s guarantee. It promises that the bottle contains tonic. The ingredients appear in much smaller writing.

choices.label: Accept a plain account of what is in it

outcome.text: {{other}} reads the ingredients without promising to restore your youth or rearrange your teeth. You can finally judge the offer itself.

choices.label: Decline it without another argument

outcome.text: {{other}} puts the bottle away. You leave with your coins and the teeth you arrived with.

events.title: THE FORTUNE CHARGES IN ADVANCE
events.text: You already owe money. {{other}} offers a foreign fortune whose estate is unnamed and whose fees are well documented.

choices.label: Refuse to finance the claim

outcome.text: {{other}} produces another seal. You retain the advantage of owing nothing to it.

choices.label: Take the demands to the clerk

outcome.text: The clerk asks for the estate’s name before its next fee. {{other}} dislikes this new order of business.

events.title: THE DEVIL WANTS AN HONEST WAGE
events.text: {{other}} accounts for a pageant whose devil has worked more than the angels and received less than the donkey.

choices.label: Help settle the accounts fairly

outcome.text: The devil is paid. {{other}} ends an infernal dispute without theology.

choices.label: Decline without insulting the work

outcome.text: The devil thanks you for not explaining that art should be its own reward.

events.title: THE BOUNDARY STONE HAS AN AUDIENCE
events.text: {{other}} asks where a family boundary belongs. The witnesses remember its position, unless somebody first suggests an advantage.

choices.label: Stand by the witnessed position

outcome.text: {{other}} helps put the stone back before bargaining can improve everyone’s memory.

choices.label: Keep out of the quarrel

outcome.text: {{other}} seeks another witness. The stone remains less evasive than its neighbours.

events.title: THE KEEPSAKE WITHOUT A NEW PRICE
events.text: {{other}} gives you a family keepsake. This one, the explanation goes, should not need another household account.

choices.label: Accept without making a debt of the gift

outcome.text: You listen to its story. {{other}} stops waiting for you to price the kindness.

choices.label: List what your help has cost

outcome.text: {{other}} sets the keepsake beside the tally. The two objects make an unkind comparison.

events.title: THE VICTORY BOW BEFORE THE RACE
events.text: {{other.intro}} draws a finish line and practises a victory bow. Then they invite you to race. Several people have stopped to see whether the bow was premature.

choices.label: Race for it

success.text: You finish first. {{other}} bows automatically, sees you beside them, and wishes they had not practised so thoroughly.

failure.text: {{other}} beats you to the line. You arrive breathless with a sore leg, and the grin waiting for you is larger than the crowd.

choices.label: Check the rules before agreeing

outcome.text: {{other}} has given themselves a shorter course and the good starting spot. You point this out, and the race is suddenly far less urgent.

choices.label: Carry the sack together instead

outcome.text: {{other}} takes the other handle after a little grumbling. Your shoulders ache, but the sack reaches its owner and you part on better terms.

events.title: THE BUSHEL WITH A SECOND PRICE
events.text: The harvest is poor. {{other}} has raised the price of grain while the parish is still thanking God for having any. The poor box is being asked to pay retail.

choices.label: Fund a shared grain reserve (12g)

outcome.text: You put grain in the household reserve and invite neighbours to draw against a written tally. {{other}} asks whether generosity has to be so well organised.

choices.label: Sell your stored grain at the new price

outcome.text: Your purse fills as the household shelves empty. {{other}} congratulates you in a voice intended to carry to the queue.

choices.label: Check the merchant’s measure in public

outcome.text: The scoop has an excellent appetite. You demonstrate it before the buyers; {{other}} produces a fuller measure and a considerably shorter greeting.

events.title: THE WILL WITH ROOM FOR ANOTHER SIGNATURE
events.text: {{other.intro}} wants your household’s inheritance. The proposed settlement leaves a blank beside the witness’s name. A fresh quill lies helpfully across it.

choices.label: Pay nine gold to contest the claim

outcome.text: The witnesses identify the disputed goods and your household keeps them. {{other}} leaves angry, while the clerk counts the nine-gold fee twice.

choices.label: Agree a smaller share now

outcome.text: You give up some goods and have the settlement witnessed. {{other}} helps carry the agreed share instead of returning with another demand.

choices.label: Fill in the helpful blank

outcome.text: You secure the larger share until {{other}} recognises your handwriting. The forgery gives the authorities something concrete to investigate.

choices.label: Give up the disputed goods

outcome.text: {{other}} carries the goods away. You hold the door, accept the quiet thanks and shut it on an emptier room.

events.title: THE CART THAT HAS ALREADY ENLISTED
events.text: {{other}} brings a levy writ for men, grain and carts. Your cart is listed as willing. The horse has expressed no view that the clerk is prepared to record.

choices.label: Pay for supplies in place of bodies (18g)

outcome.text: The official accepts supplies against your household’s obligation. The horse remains a civilian and looks deeply ungrateful.

choices.label: Help make the muster fair

outcome.text: You insist on a public list and exemptions read aloud. {{other}} objects to giving the levy quite so many opportunities to understand it.

choices.label: List a dead man in your household’s place

outcome.text: The dead man is exceptionally punctual on paper. His burial entry is equally punctual in reaching the clerk.

events.title: THE FUTURE THAT DOES NOT FIT THE HOUSE
events.text: {{child}} has a plan larger than the household can afford. The explanation includes a drawing of the future workshop and a very small space labelled “parents”.

choices.label: Fund a first practical lesson (10g)

outcome.text: You pay for tools and instruction. {{child}} redraws the parents’ space with a window.

choices.label: Help test the idea before promising money

outcome.text: You work through the first task together. {{child}} finds three problems and a fourth reason to keep trying.

choices.label: Order the child to take your place instead

outcome.text: {{child}} folds the drawing carefully and stops showing you the revisions. The household has gained obedience at the price of confidence.

events.title: THE LORD’S THREE DRIEST DAYS
events.text: {{other}} calls boon-work on the only dry days available for your hay. The notice describes this as a fortunate coincidence.

choices.label: Arrange a shared labour rota

outcome.text: You divide the service and harvest between households. Everybody complains about the rota, which has the unusual advantage of leaving time to complain.

choices.label: Buy out your service (8g)

outcome.text: The steward accepts eight gold and stops praising the spiritual value of labour. Your hay is gathered before the rain.

choices.label: Take a neighbour’s paid work instead

outcome.text: You return with a wage and find your own stores emptier. {{other}} congratulates you on being so industrious somewhere else.

events.title: THE PRICE CHANGED WHILE YOU WERE WORKING
events.text: {{other}} brings the new assize price just as your goods are ready. It has moved down. The cost of making them has displayed less religious humility.

choices.label: Correct the price and publish the weights

outcome.text: You accept the smaller margin. The wardens inspect your measure twice, disappointed to find nothing worth carrying away.

choices.label: Keep the old price and shorten the measure

outcome.text: The first buyers pay well. {{other}} brings the scoop to the wardens; your profit now has to attend a hearing.

charge.offence: Selling with a shortened assize measure

choices.label: Sell honestly at a loss to keep the customers

outcome.text: You swallow the loss before anyone has to swallow your explanation. {{other}} recommends the shop without being paid to do it.

events.title: THE CHILD BEFORE THE PEDIGREE
events.text: {{other}} brings a weak newborn to the chapel. Someone asks about the mother’s marriage. The child is having difficulty waiting for the answer.

choices.label: Attend to the child before the argument

outcome.text: You arrange warmth and immediate care. {{other}} thanks you; the questioner is left holding a pedigree nobody presently needs.

choices.label: Pay for the midwife’s attendance (7g)

outcome.text: The midwife enters, sends the debaters outside and asks for clean cloth. The room becomes much more useful.

choices.label: Insist the household settle the paperwork first

outcome.text: {{other}} leaves to find help elsewhere. The forms remain beautifully arranged on a table that is suddenly too quiet.

events.title: SIX ARCHERS SHORT OF AN ARMY
events.text: {{other}} needs six archers before the muster ends. One volunteer can draw a bow; the other five can draw their names with assistance.

choices.label: Train the volunteers and report their limits

outcome.text: You submit an honest muster and a useful drill. {{other}} has fewer imaginary archers and more actual ones.

choices.label: Supply six magnificent names on paper

outcome.text: The company pays for six archers who have achieved complete concealment. The muster clerk takes an interest in your handwriting.

choices.label: Pay a veteran to run the drill (8g)

outcome.text: The veteran teaches the company to hit the target and you to stop standing beside it.

events.title: THE CHARGE NOBODY HAS READ
events.text: {{other}} presents fourteen charges against tenants, four of whom cannot read them. The proposed procedure is to ask whether they understand and fine them for saying no.

choices.label: Read every charge and hear the answers

outcome.text: The hearing takes all afternoon. Two charges collapse, three improve dramatically when spoken aloud, and your tenants discover a use for your chair.

choices.label: Collect the proposed fines without a hearing

outcome.text: Twenty gold reaches the household. The tenants stop answering questions freely, having learned what an answer costs in your chair.

choices.label: Hire an independent clerk (10g)

outcome.text: The new clerk finds a hen charged twice and a man fined for being the hen’s owner. {{other}} disputes the hen’s legal personality.

events.title: THE ELEVENTH ITEM IS THE COINAGE
events.text: {{other}} places the currency proposal eleventh on a twenty-item agenda. The first ten concern ceremonial cushions. By the eleventh, the council will agree to almost any metal.

choices.label: Hear the coinage accounts first

outcome.text: The mint keeps its standard and the cushions endure neglect. {{other}} discovers that rearranging business can be a form of government.

choices.label: Sell exemptions before discussing the standard

outcome.text: Twenty gold reaches your purse. The exemptions reach the clerk’s book, where they are much less easily spent.

choices.label: Fund a public assay (15 treasury)

outcome.text: The assayer demonstrates the difference between the portrait and the silver. Nobody applauds until they know which one you meant to protect.

events.title: THE BAND’S LIST OF THINGS NOT TO STEAL
events.text: {{other}} proposes a rule against robbing poor households. The band asks how poor, how often, and whether the rule applies before supper.

choices.label: Keep the rule and divide your own supplies

outcome.text: You give up food and keep the band’s trust. {{other}} adds “including when hungry” in lettering large enough for everyone.

choices.label: Limit the plan to a wealthy target

outcome.text: The proposal acquires a richer victim and a proper robbery charge. {{other}} approves of your principles being so profitable.

choices.label: Sell the band’s intended route

outcome.text: The authorities pay twelve gold. {{other}} learns which part of the agreement you considered negotiable.

events.title: THE DEBT DISCUSSED IN A DOORWAY
events.text: {{other}} asks you to guarantee a loan. The request is made quietly in a doorway, as though a witness might add to the interest.

choices.label: Lend from your own purse instead (8g)

outcome.text: You put your own coins on the table and set down the terms. {{other}} accepts the help without having to borrow your name as well.

choices.label: Accept the debt openly

outcome.text: The loan is entered in your name. {{other}} promises gratitude; the lender prefers your signature.

choices.label: Refuse kindly and keep the friendship separate

outcome.text: {{other}} goes quiet, then asks whether you can help carry the goods instead. The friendship has survived acquiring a boundary.

events.title: HALF A FURROW, ALL OF YOUR ENEMITY
events.text: {{other}} has moved the boundary by half a furrow. The argument is now occupying more ground than the disputed field.

choices.label: Pay for a witnessed survey (7g)
