outcome.text: The survey proves both of you wrong by a little. {{other}} dislikes this result almost as much as losing.

choices.label: Trade the strip for an end to the personal quarrel

outcome.text: You give up a small claim. {{other}} takes your hand before either of you can turn it into another condition.

choices.label: Move the fence at night

outcome.text: Your household gains from the disputed use. {{other}} brings witnesses to the new fence, which has failed to make itself invisible.

events.title: THE SILENCE HAS JOINED YOU FOR SUPPER
events.text: {{spouse}} sets out two bowls and a list of household decisions made without consultation. The list needs more table than the bowls.

choices.label: Agree new terms and hear the whole list

outcome.text: You share the household accounts and the work. {{spouse}} finally eats before the soup becomes another grievance.

choices.label: Agree to end the marriage

outcome.text: You end the marriage by consent. The practical divisions are written down; neither of you tries to make the last conversation a victory.

choices.label: Insist the matter is already settled

outcome.text: {{spouse}} folds the list and stops discussing it. The quiet you wanted has become much less comfortable.

events.title: SEVEN NIGHTS YOU DID NOT SIT UP
events.text: {{sibling}} cared for your parent through the last illness. You were away. The account between you is not mainly about money, but money is the easiest part to say.

choices.label: Acknowledge the burden without an excuse

outcome.text: You say what you should have said before discussing the household goods. {{sibling}} sits down. The practical argument can finally begin.

choices.label: Contribute to the costs (10g)

outcome.text: You put ten gold toward the household costs. {{sibling}} accepts it without agreeing that the amount explains the nights.

choices.label: Describe the care as a duty owed anyway

outcome.text: {{sibling}} says that is an interesting use of the word “owed”. The household division becomes colder and much more exact.

events.title: THE LIFE YOU HAD ALREADY ARRANGED
events.text: {{child}} tells you the planned apprenticeship is not the life they want. The master is waiting outside with an agreement that leaves very little room for wanting.

choices.label: Hear the alternative before signing

outcome.text: You return the unsigned agreement and work through a different first step. {{child}} explains it twice, because this time you are listening.

choices.label: Pay for a short trial in the chosen work (8g)

outcome.text: You buy a trial rather than a future. {{child}} thanks you for the distinction and immediately starts asking practical questions.

choices.label: Insist on your plan

outcome.text: The paper remains unsigned while you argue. {{child}} learns exactly how much confidence to place in the next invitation to speak freely.

events.title: THREE SMALL THINGS AND A VERY LARGE QUESTION
events.text: You have three small reasons to distrust {{spouse}}. Each would be nothing on its own. You can ask a question, or spend a great deal of effort turning them into a verdict.

choices.label: Ask plainly without claiming proof

outcome.text: {{spouse}} answers and shows you the disputed letter. You discuss the real quarrel instead of the imaginary witness you were about to invent.

choices.label: Pay for private inquiries (9g)

outcome.text: The inquiry produces receipts, gossip and a bill. It produces no proof. {{spouse}} discovers the bill first.

choices.label: End a marriage you no longer trust

outcome.text: You agree to separate. The uncertainty remains uncertainty; neither of you puts an unproved accusation into the record.

events.title: THE ROAD BY THE FEVER HOUSES
events.text: {{other}} reports sickness beside the ford. The traders want the road kept open, preferably with the sick encouraged to describe it more quietly.

choices.label: Fund separate supplies and a temporary cordon (12g)

outcome.text: You send food to the affected houses and keep the gathering apart. {{other}} has to explain to the traders that a queue can carry more than baskets.

choices.label: Sell a reassuring account to the traders

outcome.text: The traders pay for an open road and a closed mouth. The parish’s sickness burden rises; {{other}} knows who supplied the reassurance.

choices.label: Organise bearers and food without inventing a cure

outcome.text: You spend your strength on practical care. {{other}} works beside you; neither of you wastes the breath on promises.

events.title: THE MARKET THAT FORGOT TO BE LAWFUL
events.text: Swineford has held a market for years without a charter. {{other}} brings a rival town’s complaint and a lawyer who has already found the fee schedule.

choices.label: Fund a proper petition (18g)

outcome.text: The petition is lodged with the market’s accounts and your payment. {{other}} signs beside you; the lawyer has to find an actual objection.

choices.label: Produce an impressively aged charter

outcome.text: The wax is old. The clerk recognises a witness who has been alive for only nineteen years, and takes a much livelier interest.

choices.label: Negotiate shared market rights

outcome.text: Both towns accept a smaller return and stop paying lawyers to describe the same stalls. {{other}} calls this a regrettable outbreak of arithmetic.

events.title: TWO GREAT SEALS, ONE TAX DEMAND
events.text: {{other}} presents two contradictory orders bearing rival seals. Both demand the same money. The messengers insist that obedience is a simple matter.

choices.label: Publish both orders and refuse duplicate payment

outcome.text: You pay the recorded obligation once and keep witnessed copies. {{other}} has to explain why loyalty should require a second receipt.

choices.label: Sell your support to the richer messenger

outcome.text: You accept fifteen gold for an endorsement. The rival claimant keeps the copy with your name; {{other}} keeps the original.

choices.label: Pay to verify the warrants (6g)

outcome.text: The verifier identifies the duplicate demand. One messenger objects to being described as a man with a very expensive stamp.

events.title: THE ACCUSATION ALREADY IN INK
events.text: {{other}} has entered a small accusation against you with magnificent certainty. The evidence consists of having heard it from someone who was also certain.

choices.label: Question the witnesses openly

outcome.text: The witnesses disagree about the day, the place and your hat. {{other}} withdraws the accusation in defence of the one detail they still like.

choices.label: Pay to settle the civil claim (8g)

outcome.text: The disputed claim is withdrawn with a receipt. {{other}} is pleased with your reasonableness, which appears to have been priced exactly.

choices.label: Commission an equally certain alibi

outcome.text: The alibi improves until the clerk asks for a date. You have supplied a real perjury charge in place of a doubtful accusation.

events.title: THIRTEEN DOORS, FOUR PAIRS OF HANDS
events.text: {{other}} has thirteen households asking for care and help for four. The richest house has sent a servant to explain how urgently wealth can suffer.

choices.label: Prioritise need and publish the list

outcome.text: The four places go to the most urgent cases. {{other}} helps explain the list to people who had hoped an explanation could be bought.

choices.label: Fund extra help (12g)

outcome.text: You pay for clean cloth, fuel and another pair of hands. {{other}} crosses two names off the waiting list before thanking you.

choices.label: Give priority to those who can pay you

outcome.text: You collect the fees. {{other}} has to deliver the refusal to the other doors and does not forgive the errand.

events.title: THE HOUSEHOLD THAT FITS IN THE YARD
events.text: Your family is safe outside a damaged home. {{other}} offers rebuilding credit while the timbers are still warm enough to make the interest seem reasonable.

choices.label: Borrow for the repair

outcome.text: The loan is recorded and the work is paid for. You get a weatherproof room and a creditor whose memory is much better than the thatch.

choices.label: Patch a smaller room together

outcome.text: You save the usable timber and accept less space. {{other}} lends a hand after discovering that you intend to sleep under this work yourself.

choices.label: Pay for the repair outright (24g)

outcome.text: You pay, count the spars and decline the loan. {{other}} looks disappointed by a roof that will not send them money.

events.title: THE NAVE HAS ACQUIRED A BORDER
events.text: Two priests have divided the parish over obedience and poverty. {{other}} asks where you sit. The draughtiest pew is now a declaration of belief.

choices.label: Make both sides state the practical complaint

outcome.text: The argument shrinks to a disputed charge for candles. {{other}} produces the account; the nave loses a frontier and gains an embarrassing sum.

choices.label: Sell a useful account to the richer side

outcome.text: You receive twelve gold and provide the quarrel with respectable language. {{other}} recognises the price even where the parish cannot read it.

choices.label: Fund parish food instead of another sermon (8g)

outcome.text: The food crosses the aisle without difficulty. {{other}} admits that hunger has been a rather efficient ecumenist.

events.title: THE CELLAR WITH A CANDIDATE ATTACHED
events.text: {{other}} seeks your vote against a rival with better wine. The election has reached the stage at which principles are being judged by the jug.

choices.label: Demand a written, witnessed vote

outcome.text: The voters must supply names rather than noises from the cellar. {{other}} accepts the result and blames the handwriting only once.

choices.label: Sell your vote and keep the cup

outcome.text: You receive ten gold. {{other}} keeps an exact account of the principle you sold and the much smaller cup you stole.

choices.label: Put forward an honest working candidate

outcome.text: You argue for skill rather than the cellar. {{other}} respects the argument while becoming much less fond of its author.

events.title: THE PRIORY’S NAMELESS PAYMENT
events.text: {{other}} brings a priory account for a child’s keep. The donor’s name is hidden; the expense is not. Someone has paid a great deal to be described as nobody.

choices.label: Pay the child’s immediate board without claiming a pedigree (12g)

outcome.text: The priory takes the money and serves supper. {{other}} puts away the royal speculation long enough to count the bowls.

choices.label: Publish the account as evidence, not proof of parentage

outcome.text: The payment becomes public. {{other}} finds that the missing name attracts more attention than any name you could safely invent.

choices.label: Accept payment to hide the account

outcome.text: You pocket fifteen gold and keep a secret. The unknown donor remains unknown; {{other}} is now quite certain about you.

events.title: FIFTEEN MISSING HOLY OBJECTS
events.text: {{other}} has an abbey inventory naming fifteen lost treasures. Four are on display in other churches. One is being used to keep a door open.

choices.label: Record where the objects actually are

outcome.text: You copy the marks and locations. {{other}} rescues the doorstop’s description before anyone can improve its provenance.

choices.label: Pay to return the disputed object (10g)

outcome.text: The abbey receives its object and the parish receives an ordinary stone for the door. Both are asked to acknowledge the substitution in writing.

choices.label: Sell the object to a discreet collector

outcome.text: You collect eighteen gold. The inventory becomes the evidence against you, with unusually helpful illustrations.

events.title: THE FRATERNITY’S LOCKED POOR BOX
events.text: {{other}} invites you to a fraternity that feeds its sick and buries its dead. The accounts are sound; the door is locked; the treasurer would prefer not to discuss the combination.

choices.label: Pay this year’s dues after reading the accounts (8g)

outcome.text: The fraternity records your contribution and opens the relief box. {{other}} welcomes the only new member who asked to see the bottom of it.

choices.label: Challenge the missing relief money publicly

outcome.text: The missing sum is entered beside the treasurer’s name. {{other}} loses your confidence and gains an audience for the explanation.

choices.label: Take a share for keeping quiet

outcome.text: You receive twelve gold from a box meant for sick neighbours. {{other}} considers this admission sufficiently binding without an oath.

events.title: THE MATCH WITH FOUR COPIES AND NO AGREEMENT
events.text: {{other}} brings a marriage settlement that promises more than either household owns. The clerk recommends signing before anyone counts.

choices.label: Count the goods and renegotiate

outcome.text: The promised ox becomes a cart, then half a cart, then an apology. {{other}} agrees to a smaller honest settlement; nobody is married by arithmetic alone.

choices.label: Withdraw the promise openly

outcome.text: The proposed match ends before anybody has to live inside it. {{other}} returns your token with the air of a creditor cancelling a very small kingdom.

choices.label: Add your own imaginary livestock

outcome.text: The settlement now contains enough cattle to feed both families until the clerk asks where they are. {{other}} supplies the false document to the court.

events.title: THE CHILD AT THE THRESHOLD
events.text: {{other}} brings a child needing a home. The parish offers a blessing and asks whether you can provide the less portable necessities.

choices.label: Register a placement and set aside food

outcome.text: The placement is entered through the parish and food is reserved. {{other}} carries away a practical answer instead of another prayer to translate into supper.

choices.label: Fund the child’s immediate care (8g)

outcome.text: The parish receives eight gold for food and bedding. {{other}} puts the blessing aside long enough to buy both.

choices.label: Admit that your household cannot provide care

outcome.text: You help {{other}} ask elsewhere without promising a bed you do not have. The answer hurts less than a welcome that cannot be kept.

events.title: THE BED THAT HAS BECOME A PEDIGREE
events.text: {{sibling.intro}} lies across the best bed and will not move. You are trying to divide the household goods. They suggest beginning with something they are not lying on.

choices.label: Agree a division with witnesses

outcome.text: You take fewer goods and get the division witnessed. {{sibling}} finally sits up, trusts the agreement and helps carry your share.

choices.label: Let them have the bed

outcome.text: {{sibling}} smooths the blanket, then notices you still standing. They make room for you to sit and ask you to stay for supper.

choices.label: Invent a better inventory for yourself

outcome.text: You get the larger share until {{sibling}} recognises the chest they carved last winter. They take the false list to the authorities.

events.title: THE MILLRACE’S BAD AIR
events.text: {{other}} has fever after clearing the millrace. The miller insists the work cannot be responsible because it was not paid well enough to be important.

choices.label: Fund rest and clean supplies (9g)

outcome.text: You pay for food, water and a dry place to rest. {{other}} is spared the miller’s proposed cure of another shift.

choices.label: Take the dangerous shift yourself

outcome.text: You clear enough of the race to stop the immediate flooding. {{other}} thanks you; your own strength pays the part the miller omitted.

choices.label: Sell a reassuring report to keep the mill open

outcome.text: The miller pays you to call it a rumour. {{other}} supplies a less convenient account, between bouts of coughing.

events.title: THE MIDWIFE’S INCONVENIENT HAND
events.text: {{other}} is helping an experienced midwife whose hand locks in the cold. A family wants the famous name; the apprentice has the steadier fingers.

choices.label: Pay for skilled assistance (8g)

outcome.text: The midwife directs and the apprentice works. {{other}} marvels that two people can be useful without one of them being declared a fraud.

choices.label: Ask the midwife to choose the safest arrangement

outcome.text: The master gives the practical tasks to the apprentice and keeps the difficult decisions. {{other}} finally stops arguing about the name on the door.

choices.label: Insist on the name you were promised

outcome.text: The midwife attempts too much and the care becomes less safe. {{other}} remembers your contribution to a problem you did not have to solve with your hands.

events.title: THE BELL FOUNDER CANNOT READ HIS MARK
events.text: {{other}} cannot see the tuning marks on a new bell. The wardens want the famous founder to work alone, preferably without describing what “alone” now requires.

choices.label: Read the marks without taking the credit

outcome.text: You call the marks and {{other}} makes the corrections. The bell rings true, under the name that knew what to do with the numbers.

choices.label: Take the credit for the whole casting

outcome.text: You collect a fee and the applause. {{other}} keeps the mould and the knowledge of who actually knew how to use it.

choices.label: Pay for an assistant named on the commission (10g)

outcome.text: The wardens allow a second name after discovering it does not make the bell twice as expensive. {{other}} can keep working without pretending to see.

events.title: THE CHALICE AND THE VERY ORDINARY METAL
events.text: A chalice is missing. {{other}} has found a gilt shaving, a fresh roof and several hens belonging to a suspiciously prosperous witness.

choices.label: Have the metal tested before accusing anyone (5g)

outcome.text: The gold is gilt over pewter. {{other}} looks at the new roof and realises that someone has stolen twice: first the chalice, then the parish’s idea of its value.

choices.label: Place the evidence before the proper court

outcome.text: You lodge the shaving and the account of the payment. {{other}} signs as witness; a rumour becomes evidence without becoming a conviction by lunch.

choices.label: Sell your silence about the witness’s new hens

outcome.text: You receive fourteen gold. {{other}} retains the shaving and a particularly good description of the transaction.

charge.offence: Taking money to conceal church theft

events.title: THE SNARE HAS CAUGHT A FORESTER
events.text: {{other}} has trapped the forester’s leg in a snare meant for deer. The forester promises to be reasonable as soon as somebody stops being so criminally helpful.

choices.label: Cut the snare and give an honest account

outcome.text: The forester is freed and the trap is surrendered. {{other}} loses a valuable wire and gains a chance to explain it without a man screaming over the answer.

choices.label: Take the catch and leave the evidence

outcome.text: You carry away the meat. {{other}} can describe both your kindness and the direction in which it departed.

charge.offence: Taking game and abandoning a trapped forester

choices.label: Pay for help and surrender the poaching gear (8g)

outcome.text: You pay for care and the gear is taken as evidence. {{other}} discovers an unusually expensive method of catching no deer.

events.title: THE ALIBI WITH TOO MUCH DETAIL
events.text: {{other}} offers an alibi that includes the weather, the candles and what everyone ate. You remember only that you were not there for half of it.

choices.label: Give the part you actually know

outcome.text: The clerk crosses out an impressive meal and two useful hours. {{other}} has a weaker alibi and a witness who can survive a second question.

choices.label: Swear to the whole polished account

outcome.text: The first draft is still on the clerk’s desk. He puts it beside your oath and asks which version you would prefer to defend.

choices.label: Refuse to give evidence you cannot support

outcome.text: The court seeks another witness. {{other}} stops treating your presence as a thing that can be borrowed after the event.

events.title: THE COPE-CHEST HAS ACQUIRED A DEADLINE
events.text: {{other.intro}} wants an oak chest finished by tomorrow. Their purse contains next week’s price. An apprentice shows you a better joint as the old sample splits on the bench.

choices.label: Use the sound joint and credit the apprentice

outcome.text: The lid closes neatly. {{other}} tries to lift the chest by one corner, fails to break it, and pays eight gold with obvious reluctance.

choices.label: Hide a split in cheap timber

outcome.text: You pocket eighteen gold. {{other}} lifts the chest, sees daylight through the split, and carries the receipt straight to the guild.

choices.label: Give back the eight-gold advance

outcome.text: {{other}} takes the money back and complains about the delay. You keep your tools, your unbroken timber and one fewer impossible promise.

events.title: FOUR CARTS, ONE QUESTIONABLE GUARANTEE
events.text: {{other}} offers a place in a four-cart convoy. The safe-passage letter covers the road, the bridge and everything except the people collecting the toll.

choices.label: Pay for a clear shared contract (9g)

outcome.text: The hauliers sign the loss-sharing terms. {{other}} stops calling the profits guaranteed once somebody writes down who pays for a missing cart.

choices.label: Borrow for the unguarded shipment (30g debt)

success.text: The carts arrive and your return is paid. The loan also arrives, requiring rather less unloading.

failure.text: The goods are lost. Your creditor has stayed home and suffered no such misfortune.

choices.label: Keep your goods and refuse the guarantee

outcome.text: {{other}} offers three adjectives and no better security. You take your goods home before a fourth can be found.

events.title: THE WORKDAY THAT RAN INTO TOMORROW
events.text: {{other}} brings a contract requiring apprentices to work after the permitted hours. The master has solved the problem by describing midnight as late afternoon.

choices.label: Uphold the hours and take the smaller commission

outcome.text: You refuse the work that depends on the extra hours. {{other}} loses a commission and gains an example the apprentices can quote.

choices.label: Take the cheap work and break the agreed hours

outcome.text: Twelve gold reaches your purse. The apprentices reach the clerk before dawn, for once making excellent use of the hours you insisted were still afternoon.

choices.label: Pay for food while the dispute is settled (8g)

outcome.text: The apprentices eat while the master finds a clock that agrees with the ordinance. {{other}} keeps the bread account separately from the speeches.

events.title: THE BUSHEL WITH LESS INSIDE THAN OUT
events.text: {{other}} presents a tithe measure with a handsome outside and a remarkably high bottom. The steward calls the difference ecclesiastical space.

choices.label: Compare the measure before witnesses

outcome.text: You fill both measures from the same sack. {{other}} replaces the false one while explaining that certainty has become unpleasantly heavy.

choices.label: Pay to exempt your household alone (9g)

outcome.text: Your grain is spared and your neighbours’ grain is not. {{other}} keeps the payment in a box with a very accurate memory.

choices.label: Pay for an independent standard (6g)

outcome.text: The new standard is kept in public. {{other}} dislikes the inconvenience of a bushel that does not improve when unattended.

events.title: THE LOTS ARE DRAWN BEFORE THE DRAWING
events.text: {{other}} brings a levy list containing the names of fourteen men. You were told there would be a drawing. The ink appears to have attended early.

choices.label: Demand a public drawing with exemptions read aloud

outcome.text: The list is remade before witnesses. {{other}} complains about delay while hiding the pen that predicted the first result.

choices.label: Pay for a lawful household exemption (14g)

outcome.text: The exemption is recorded and the levy continues. {{other}} gives you a receipt too large to hide in a sleeve.

choices.label: Remove your household’s name secretly

outcome.text: The erased name leaves a fine white scar. {{other}} has the first copy, complete with a date that is not your friend.

events.title: TWO SEALS, NO CONFIDENCE
events.text: {{other}} brings two impressions of the guild seal. Both claim exclusive authority, and both smell of the same workshop.

choices.label: Compare the charter and lodge one public standard

outcome.text: You establish the authorised impression before the merchants. {{other}} must retire a very profitable second thumb.

choices.label: Pay for a proper verification (12g)

outcome.text: The verification arrives with enough witnesses to outnumber the seals. {{other}} remarks that honesty is becoming expensive to counterfeit.

choices.label: Sell a third impression

outcome.text: You collect sixteen gold and provide the guild with the only claim neither side wishes to defend.

events.title: THE THATCH HAS LEARNED THE WEATHER
events.text: {{other}} finds rot beneath your recently repaired roof. The repairer says it is not a leak if the water can also get out.

choices.label: Pay for sound timber (14g)

outcome.text: The rotten pieces come down and dry ones go up. {{other}} lets you count them before anybody describes the house as improved.

choices.label: Patch it with your own labour

outcome.text: You finish the patch with a stiff back and a dry bed. {{other}} tests the beam before congratulating you.

choices.label: Move the bowls and leave the repair

outcome.text: The bowls catch less than the rain brings. The household loses food and shelter while the repairer preserves a perfect record of having been paid.

events.title: THE RATS HAVE ACQUIRED A KEY
events.text: The granary sacks are light. {{other}} blames rats. You catch nine and find that the missing grain is still far too heavy for their combined ambition.

choices.label: Count the sacks and change the lock (5g)

outcome.text: The new lock excludes both the rats and the person who kept forgetting to report them. {{other}} loses the spare key with visible regret.

choices.label: Record an honest food allowance instead

outcome.text: The hungry household receives a proper ration. {{other}} signs for it; the sacks stop having to develop holes to feed somebody.

choices.label: Sell your silence about the missing sacks

outcome.text: You take eight gold from a theft that is still costing your household grain. {{other}} finds your arithmetic delightfully incurious.

charge.offence: Concealing theft from a communal granary

events.title: THE FIRE HAS NO RESPECT FOR BOUNDARIES
events.text: A neighbour’s roof burns and sparks reach your own thatch. {{other}} has a ladder, two buckets and an urgent theory about whose property matters first.

choices.label: Help the people before the property

success.text: You get the trapped household into the yard. {{other}} pours the last bucket on your sleeve and apologises for the part that was still warm.

failure.text: A falling spar burns your arm. You reach the yard alive, with pain that requires proper care.

choices.label: Protect your household’s roof first

outcome.text: Your roof survives. {{other}} watches where you pour the water and stops calling you neighbour quite so comfortably.

choices.label: Pay for a bucket crew (10g)

outcome.text: The crew passes water rather than opinions. {{other}} discovers how much quicker the work goes without deciding who deserves to be wet.

events.title: THE TREASURE MAP ENDS UNDER A BED
events.text: {{other}} sells a map to buried wealth. The last mark lies under a living neighbour’s bed. The map provides no advice about the neighbour.

choices.label: Ask permission and share any proceeds

outcome.text: The neighbour admits there is an old cellar and lets you inspect it. {{other}} looks disappointed that the first tool you used was a question.

choices.label: Pay to inspect the survey (4g)

outcome.text: The survey is genuine and the treasure annotation is newer. {{other}} lowers the price of the annotation without offering to improve the cellar.

choices.label: Dig without permission

outcome.text: You find a sound foundation and a furious owner. {{other}} declines to explain why you are under somebody’s floor.

charge.offence: Breaking into a dwelling to dig for treasure

events.title: THE BONE BOTH CHURCHES REMEMBER
events.text: {{other}} presents a relic claimed by two churches. Each can describe its miracles; neither can produce the receipt. The armed escort can produce several swords.

choices.label: Require provenance before public claims

outcome.text: The inventory identifies the bone as a sheep’s. {{other}} asks whether that proves the sheep was not unusually devout.

choices.label: Sell the shrine’s display rights to both churches

outcome.text: You take sixteen gold and issue two incompatible promises. {{other}} places the contracts beside the bone, creating a rather better exhibit.

charge.offence: Selling conflicting rights to a disputed relic

choices.label: Fund a quiet public inventory (8g)

outcome.text: The bone is catalogued without a procession. {{other}} laments the loss of a very profitable misunderstanding.

events.title: THE PROPHECY THAT HAS MET THE RENT
events.text: A child has made a striking prediction. {{other}} is charging to hear the next one and has begun suggesting that the heavens might be interested in this month’s rent.

choices.label: Stop the paying audience and hear the child quietly

outcome.text: Without the crowd, the prediction becomes a frightened child’s account of a flooded ditch. {{other}} has to find a different way to make it pay.

choices.label: Take a share of the prophecy takings

outcome.text: You receive fifteen gold. {{other}} adds another stool for paying customers, and the child learns which sort of answer brings supper.

choices.label: Pay for quiet care and food (8g)

outcome.text: The child gets food, a quiet room and an afternoon without questions. {{other}} receives a receipt instead of a revelation.

events.title: THE CHRISTENING SPOON IN THE WRONG SLEEVE
events.text: {{sibling}} has the household’s silver spoon and an explanation that grows more ancestral every time you ask.

choices.label: Ask for its return without an audience

outcome.text: The spoon comes home. {{sibling}} keeps the explanation, which is now too elaborate to throw away.

choices.label: Sell your claim for a fair payment

outcome.text: {{sibling}} pays five gold for the spoon and the right to stop describing your grandmother.

events.title: THE CARE AGREEMENT EVERYONE HAS HEARD ABOUT
events.text: {{other}} challenges a household care agreement. The dispute has attracted several people who have never provided any of the care.

choices.label: Read the actual terms before witnesses

outcome.text: The audience loses interest when the food, beds and responsibilities are counted. {{other}} signs the corrected terms instead of another accusation.

choices.label: Use the disagreement to humiliate the claimant

outcome.text: You win the audience and lose {{other}}’s trust. The people who offered no care offer excellent applause.

events.title: THE MIDWIFE ASKS FOR A HEARTH
events.text: {{other}} asks to use your main room for a birth. The floor is dry, the fire is good, and your household had other plans for both.

choices.label: Make room and provide clean fuel

outcome.text: You give up privacy and supplies. {{other}} moves the work indoors and leaves the arguments about inconvenience outside.

choices.label: Pay for another suitable room (6g)

outcome.text: You fund a warm room nearby. {{other}} is grateful for an answer that includes a door which opens.

events.title: WHOSE NAME FITS ROUND THE BELL
events.text: {{other}} wants their name cast round a bell made by several hands. There is room for everyone’s mark, provided the patron’s titles lose a little weight.

choices.label: Credit the makers as well as the patron

outcome.text: The inscription becomes less flattering and more accurate. {{other}} objects to having neighbours in bronze.

choices.label: Reserve the whole inscription for the payer

outcome.text: The payer’s titles go all the way round the bell. Eight gold buys you the excellent opinion of someone now able to hear their own importance every hour.

events.title: THE AMNESTY WITH A PRICE BESIDE EACH NAME
events.text: {{other}} offers to submit names for a poaching amnesty. The list includes a fee column that the royal notice appears to have forgotten.

choices.label: Compare the terms with the public notice

outcome.text: The fee column disappears. {{other}} complains that copying the law word for word leaves no room for initiative.

choices.label: Sell names to the intermediary

outcome.text: You collect ten gold for exposing your neighbours to an arrangement you have not verified. {{other}} now has both the names and yours.

events.title: THE FIRST DRAFT IS STILL WET
events.text: {{other}} asks you to confirm a statement while the clerk has its contradictory first draft drying beside the fire.

choices.label: Correct the statement before swearing

outcome.text: The clerk keeps both copies. {{other}} is annoyed that your conscience has developed such inconvenient timing.

choices.label: Pay to destroy the first draft (7g)

outcome.text: The clerk takes your money and declines to burn evidence. You have purchased a very clear memory in somebody else’s head.

charge.offence: Attempting to destroy a witness statement

events.title: THE OAK HAS ARRIVED IN TWO OPINIONS
events.text: {{other}} delivers split timber for sound-timber money. The split is described as evidence that you can now see the quality inside.

choices.label: Reject the faulty lot and record why

outcome.text: The seller takes it back under witnesses. {{other}} finds a customer with less interest in the inside of wood.

choices.label: Buy cheaply and disclose the limits

outcome.text: You pay for usable offcuts, mark the defects and adapt the work. {{other}} is offended that the discount has become part of the description.

events.title: THE DRIVER RETURNS WITHOUT THE CART
events.text: {{other.intro}} returns without your cart. They blame a bridge, a lord and a pig powerful enough to overturn both. You ask which part happened first.

choices.label: Check the route and talk to people who saw it

outcome.text: The lord disappears from the story, then the bridge. {{other}} admits overloading the cart and returns some of the missing goods.

choices.label: Take eight gold back now

outcome.text: {{other}} counts out eight gold. You acknowledge the payment, but refuse to put the pig’s alleged title in writing.

events.title: THE CONTRACT UNDER THE SUPPER BOWL
events.text: {{other}} offers you private work while your fellow workers dispute the rate. The contract is concealed beneath a bowl, though the wage is not large enough to require hiding.

choices.label: Return the contract and explain why

outcome.text: {{other}} puts the bowl back with great dignity. Your fellow workers know you declined before the story could improve itself.

choices.label: Take the underpriced work

outcome.text: You receive nine gold. {{other}} can now quote your rate to everyone else, which proves much more valuable than the bowl.

events.title: THE ACCOUNT WITH TWO BURIALS FOR ONE MAN
events.text: {{other}} collects dues using a roll that has charged one household for the same burial twice. The second entry praises the deceased’s reliability.

choices.label: Correct the roll in public

outcome.text: The duplicate is struck out and the household keeps its payment. {{other}} announces that a dead clerk must have done it; no living clerk volunteers to disagree.

choices.label: Pay the disputed fee for the household (6g)

outcome.text: You cover the immediate demand and insist on a receipt. {{other}} now has to explain why the deceased has paid so promptly in person.

events.title: THE WITNESS HAS THREE NEW HENS
events.text: {{other}} offers testimony supporting a levy exemption. Their yard has three new hens and their memory has improved by exactly that many birds.

choices.label: Ask who paid for the hens

outcome.text: {{other}} withdraws the useful part of the statement and becomes indignant about your interest in poultry.

choices.label: Buy equally helpful testimony (9g)

outcome.text: The testimony improves. The clerk records the payment as carefully as the evidence you hoped it would replace.

events.title: THE CHARTER IN THE FAMILY CHEST
events.text: {{other}} finds a charter fragment being used beneath a loose chest foot. It may establish a guild right; it certainly establishes why the chest used to wobble.

choices.label: Pay for a witnessed copy (5g)

outcome.text: The copy preserves the right and the original goes somewhere dry. {{other}} repairs the chest with an ordinary piece of wood, now recognised as such.

choices.label: Sell exclusive access to the document

outcome.text: You pocket twelve gold. {{other}} learns how quickly a public right can become a private appointment.

events.title: THE LORD HAS BORROWED YOUR REPAIR TIMBER
events.text: {{other}} has moved your repair timber to the lord’s granary. The steward describes it as communal necessity, with a surprisingly precise sense of whose community you belong to.

choices.label: Quote the repair right before witnesses

outcome.text: The custom is real and the timber comes back. {{other}} complains that knowing the law has made you very difficult to govern efficiently.

choices.label: Buy replacement timber (10g)

outcome.text: Your roof is repaired and the granary keeps its timber. {{other}} calls this an excellent practical resolution, having paid for neither.

events.title: THE WALL THAT HID THE DAMP GRAIN
events.text: {{other}} opens a newly built partition and finds damp grain behind it. The mason says the wall had been intended to improve appearances.

choices.label: Sort and dry what can be saved

outcome.text: You lose a day’s strength and rescue useful stores. {{other}} agrees that food improves a household’s appearance best from inside its occupants.

choices.label: Sell the lot without mentioning the wall

outcome.text: You take twelve gold and lose household stores. {{other}} has retained a sack that illustrates your account rather well.

events.title: THE BOX THE FIRE DID NOT OPEN
events.text: {{other}} finds a locked strongbox in the burned rubble and asks whose it is. The owner’s mark is still readable, if inconveniently so.

choices.label: Return it unopened

outcome.text: The owner receives the box through {{other}}. Nobody has to invent a story about how the fire consumed the name but spared the lock.

choices.label: Force the lock and take the contents

outcome.text: You gain fourteen gold. {{other}} has seen the mark and now knows precisely how much your honesty costs.

charge.offence: Taking marked property from a fire

events.title: THE SCHOLAR’S VERY CAREFUL SILENCE
events.text: {{other}} has examined a supposed holy bone and offers an expensive explanation of why it would be unwise to explain the result.

choices.label: Ask for the actual finding

outcome.text: The bone is an ordinary sheep’s. {{other}} is relieved until you ask for the answer in ordinary writing as well.

choices.label: Buy a flattering description (8g)

outcome.text: Your description mentions antiquity, dignity and almost everything except sheep. {{other}} makes sure not to sign the interesting part.

events.title: THE MOST ALIVE CORPSE
events.text: A draft claim lists {{parent}} as dead and asks for your household’s goods. {{parent}} arrives to dispute it. {{other}}, who supports the claim, asks whether the alleged deceased has brought a witness.

choices.label: Put your very audible parent before the witnesses

outcome.text: {{parent}} reads the claim aloud, adding objections in the margins. Your household keeps its goods; {{other}} acquires a personal reason to dislike you.

choices.label: Pay to withdraw the claim (9g)

outcome.text: You pay nine gold to stop a living person being inventoried. {{parent}} refuses to call the payment a funeral expense.

choices.label: Support the false claim and take the offered share (fraud)

outcome.text: {{other}} pays your share. {{parent}} supplies the court with a living witness against you: {{parent}}.

events.title: THE FUNERAL REHEARSAL
events.text: {{parent}} wants to hear the funeral speech while corrections are still possible. The first objection is to the word “patient.”

choices.label: Read the truthful version

outcome.text: {{parent}} disputes three dates and concedes one unkindness. You leave with a better account of the living person.

choices.label: Offer a magnificently flattering version

outcome.text: {{parent}} approves, then asks which parent you were describing. Affection survives the accusation.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE OF THREE KEYS
events.text: {{other}} offers to sell you three keys said to open a rich relative’s chest. The relative is less clearly identified than the price.

choices.label: Have a smith inspect them (3g)

outcome.text: The smith identifies a stable key, a padlock key and an ambitious piece of wire. You pay for the inspection and keep your savings.

choices.label: Buy the supposed inheritance (14g)

outcome.text: The keys open nothing you own. Fourteen gold has passed into a household with better working locks.

choices.label: Leave the chest to its remarkable relatives

outcome.text: You decline. {{other}} lowers the price so quickly that you feel richer without buying anything.

events.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S NEW BAILIFF
events.text: {{child.intro}} has stretched a string across the doorstep. Visitors must pay a button to get in. A neighbour is already missing one and wants to see where this leads.

choices.label: Help return every button

outcome.text: {{child}} knocks on the neighbours’ doors with you and returns the buttons. One coat is fastened again before you get home.

choices.label: Back your child and keep charging

outcome.text: {{child}} beams at your support. The neighbours stop visiting, and somebody cuts the string while you are inside.

choices.label: Make it a counting game with no real toll

outcome.text: You put the buttons in a pile and count them with {{child}}, then give them back. The child tries to count the neighbours too.

events.title: THE BED IN THE WILL
events.text: {{sibling}} wants the better bed when your household divides its goods. The argument has reached the point of measuring old childhood injuries against the mattress.

choices.label: Trade the bed for a fair division of other goods

outcome.text: You surrender the bed and keep the dispute from becoming a family occupation. {{sibling}} thanks you without listing the injuries again.

choices.label: Offer to saw the bed exactly in half

outcome.text: {{sibling}} sits on the bed to end the demonstration. You are left holding a saw and the much smaller half of the conversation.

choices.label: Keep the goods together until there is actual need

outcome.text: The division waits. You use the intervening quiet to mend the bedding. It becomes easier to sleep on than the argument.

events.title: THE HEIR WITH THE WRONG FACE
events.text: {{parent}} commissions a little family portrait and asks that you be painted looking more like a prosperous relation. The painter has brought a ruler.

choices.label: Keep your own inconvenient face

outcome.text: The portrait remains unpainted while you explain yourself. {{parent}} is disappointed, but no commission fee leaves the household.

choices.label: Pay for an honest portrait instead (8g)

outcome.text: The painter uses your actual nose. {{parent}} admits the nose belongs to the household. You accept the nearest available thing to praise.

events.title: THE PENSION PAID IN BREAD
events.text: {{parent}} insists that support should arrive as bread rather than promises. The loaf specified in the agreement is drawn at its desired size.

choices.label: Set aside stores for the support

outcome.text: You put food into the household reserve and reduce the ready coin available to you. {{parent}} approves the part that can be sliced.

choices.label: Offer another elegantly worded promise

outcome.text: {{parent}} asks whether the promise can be toasted. Trust declines, though the question improves the discussion.

choices.label: Repair the hearth instead of pledging money

outcome.text: The household’s living conditions improve. {{parent}} accepts work that can be felt through a cold evening.

events.title: YOUR NAME UNDER SOMEONE ELSE’S DEBT
events.text: {{sibling}} has promised a lender that you will guarantee a loan. Your signature looks splendid, particularly for something you did not write.

choices.label: Buy back the false guarantee (18g)

outcome.text: The lender cancels the claim. {{sibling}} offers to sign a note of gratitude; you suggest leaving the pen where it is.

choices.label: Reject the forgery publicly

outcome.text: The family’s reputation suffers under the accusation. You keep your purse and acquire a genuine sibling rivalry in place of a counterfeit signature.

choices.label: Accept the obligation, not the forgery

outcome.text: You record a real twenty-gold debt in your own name. {{sibling}} promises to remember it; the lender has a more dependable method.

events.title: THE COAT WITH ROOM TO GROW
events.text: {{child}} hates the new coat because it has room for another child inside. The tailor calls this economy; {{child}} calls it a tent.

choices.label: Pay for a coat that fits this year (4g)

outcome.text: The sleeves stop collecting soup. {{child}} is delighted by the expensive discovery of wrists.

choices.label: Teach a fold that makes the sleeves useful

outcome.text: You fold, stitch and let {{child}} choose the thread. The household gains a small practical skill and a less furious wearer.

events.title: THE LADDER THAT IS NEVER HOME
events.text: {{other.intro}} has your ladder again. Their roof is mended. Your ladder is now holding up a washing line.

choices.label: Help finish up and carry it home

outcome.text: You climb up to free the line, then carry the ladder home together. Your shoulders ache, but you can finally repair your own rafters.

choices.label: Ask for five gold for all that borrowing

outcome.text: {{other}} hands over five gold and takes the washing down very slowly. The next greeting across the lane is much shorter.

choices.label: Let them keep it and lower your shelves

outcome.text: {{other}} carries it away with both hands and a grin. You move the high shelves down and gain a friend who no longer needs an excuse to call.

events.title: THE SALT CELLAR’S SECOND BOTTOM
events.text: {{parent}} shows you the household’s hidden savings beneath the salt. The ceremony would feel grander if the emergency reserve did not smell of herring.

choices.label: Leave the reserve where it is

outcome.text: You promise discretion. {{parent}} trusts you with something more substantial than a story.

choices.label: Take twelve gold from the household reserve

outcome.text: The household loses twelve gold and you gain it. {{parent}} discovers the missing weight before the missing salt.

choices.label: Add to the household reserve (6g)

outcome.text: The reserve grows. {{parent}} moves you from the category of people protected by it to the category of people protecting it.

events.title: THE CONDITIONAL BLESSING
events.text: {{child.intro}} writes a promise to obey you, then adds “when I am not busy.” The handwriting is much neater around those last six words.

choices.label: Agree which chores come before being busy

outcome.text: You work through the chores together. {{child}} grumbles over two, agrees to the rest, and lets you keep the finished copy.

choices.label: Tear off the qualifying words

outcome.text: {{child}} takes back the torn sheet. The next promise is shorter and leaves out everything you might disagree with.

events.title: THE ROOF’S CONTRIBUTION TO SUPPER
events.text: Rain falls onto your household’s table. {{other}} offers a hurried roof repair, priced on the assumption that you have already noticed the weather.

choices.label: Pay for proper work (12g)

outcome.text: The bowls return to holding supper instead of rain. The repairer leaves with your money and, at last, the household’s weather.

choices.label: Patch it together and lose a day’s rest

outcome.text: The patch improves the roof modestly. Your back protests a job that the clouds had made urgent.

choices.label: Spend nothing and let the room deteriorate

outcome.text: You move the bowls and keep the coin. The damp eats part of the stores without once presenting an estimate.

events.title: THE STOLEN FAMILY ANECDOTE
events.text: {{sibling}} tells your most embarrassing childhood story and gives themselves your heroic part. You are left with the bucket.

choices.label: Restore the bucket’s true owner

outcome.text: You correct the story in front of everyone. {{sibling}} loses affection for you; your family’s standing survives its inability to agree about a bucket.

choices.label: Tell the part where both of you fell in

outcome.text: You trade a little dignity for a better laugh. {{sibling}} remembers why the original story was worth keeping.

events.title: THE HONEST LITTLE WITNESS
events.text: {{child}} saw you conceal goods during an argument over a levy. The child is now asking whether lying becomes lawful at a particular age.

choices.label: Return the goods and admit the example was poor

outcome.text: You return the goods and pay the loss. {{child}} watches you admit the lesson before asking whether adults have to practise it too.

choices.label: Teach silence by threatening punishment

outcome.text: {{child}} stops asking and loses trust in you. A household secret is created, together with a witness who has reasons to resent it.

choices.label: Challenge the assessment openly instead

outcome.text: You abandon concealment and put your objection in public. Your family’s reputation improves without settling the assessment for the court.

events.title: THE LAST HILL ON THE ROAD
events.text: {{parent}} insists the road is no steeper than it used to be. Only the pauses have grown longer.

choices.label: Take the road at your parent’s pace

outcome.text: You lose the afternoon and keep the company. {{parent}} lets you carry the basket without calling it help.

choices.label: Hire a cart for the journey (5g)

outcome.text: {{parent}} complains about the expense all the way home. The complaint is delivered from a comfortable seat.

choices.label: Leave the basket and hurry ahead

outcome.text: You preserve your time and damage your parent’s trust. The rest of the road is quieter than you expected.

events.title: THE HEIRLOOMS ON THE MARKET CLOTH
events.text: {{sibling}} is selling household keepsakes to meet a creditor. Each object comes with a family story. The buyers ask for shorter stories and lower prices.

choices.label: Buy the goods back for the household (20g)

outcome.text: You pay for the keepsakes and put them back in the household. {{sibling}} thanks you for saving the objects without making a speech over each one.

choices.label: Help make a fair sale

outcome.text: You accept that survival can require parting with things. The family’s standing improves and {{sibling}} trusts you more.

choices.label: Buy cheaply and keep the proceeds yourself

outcome.text: You profit from the sale while the household loses wealth. {{sibling}} recognises exactly which family tradition you have preserved.

events.title: THE FAMILY SEAL CUT IN SOAP
events.text: {{sibling}} has cut a convincing family seal in soap. It is clever, cheap and already on an agreement nobody authorised.

choices.label: Destroy the seal and pay to correct the agreement (10g)

outcome.text: The false seal dissolves in a basin. Ten gold pays for correction, and {{sibling}} discovers an expensive use for clean hands.

choices.label: Use the false seal to obtain an advance

outcome.text: You receive the advance and create a genuine forgery charge. The soap has left a wonderfully clear impression on the evidence.

charge.offence: Obtaining an advance with a false seal

choices.label: Give the impression to the clerk

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and damage your bond with {{sibling}}. The household’s reputation suffers, but your own legal record remains clear.

events.title: THE BOWL KEPT WARM
events.text: {{child}} has kept a bowl beside the hearth for you. It is nearly cold; the child has been watching it for a long time.

choices.label: Sit down and eat together

outcome.text: You eat slowly enough to hear the whole account of the day. {{child}} stops watching the bowl.

choices.label: Thank the child while attending to other work

outcome.text: Your thanks is sincere and your attention is elsewhere. {{child}} learns the difference.

events.title: THE BOUNDARY MARK UNDER THE BED
events.text: {{sibling}} has brought a boundary stone indoors for safekeeping. Unfortunately it was keeping two households from arguing about the field.

choices.label: Put it back before witnesses

outcome.text: The boundary is restored under witnesses rather than by memory. {{sibling}} helps carry it and resents the audience.

choices.label: Use the confusion to enlarge your household’s claim

outcome.text: Your household gains wealth from the disputed use, and you acquire a fraud charge. The stone is silent; the witnesses are not.

choices.label: Pay for a fresh survey (7g)

outcome.text: You fund a new survey and improve the household’s standing. {{sibling}} is disappointed that measuring settles what shouting could not.

events.title: THE WEDDING OF THREE GROOMS
events.text: {{sibling}} has promised to pay three different wedding brokers for one match. All three bring contracts to the same supper. The prospective marriage is the only part nobody has arranged.

choices.label: Read all three contracts aloud

outcome.text: You expose the conflicting promises. Family standing suffers and {{sibling}} blames the only person at supper who could read.

choices.label: Pay the brokers to cancel the claims (15g)

outcome.text: The contracts are cancelled for fifteen gold. Everybody leaves unmarried. The family counts this as the evening’s first clear success.

choices.label: Demand a share of the household’s wedding reserve

outcome.text: You take ten gold from the reserve. {{sibling}} now has three brokers and one blackmailer to satisfy.

events.title: THE INVENTORY OF MATRIMONY
events.text: {{spouse}} has drawn up a list of everything each of you brought to the marriage. Under your name, “confidence” is underlined twice.

choices.label: Add a fair account of the unpaid work

outcome.text: You list the work both of you do. {{spouse}} puts the inventory away before it needs another sheet.

choices.label: Prove that you brought more

outcome.text: You win the valuation and lose affection. {{spouse}} asks whether you would like a receipt for the triumph.

choices.label: Seek a formal separation and divide your goods

outcome.text: You end the marriage and surrender part of the household reserve. The list becomes useful in a way neither of you intended.

events.title: THE BENCH BETWEEN TWO FAMILIES
events.text: At your wedding anniversary meal, {{spouse}} objects to the order of the benches. Everyone insists that seating means nothing while refusing to move.

choices.label: Mix the benches and serve the food yourself

outcome.text: You put conversation before precedence. {{spouse}} helps, and the household’s reputation improves without buying another bench.

choices.label: Let your spouse choose the seats

outcome.text: {{spouse}} gets the arrangement right to at least one person’s satisfaction. Your willingness to yield is remembered kindly at home.

events.title: THE LOVE LETTER WITH A TALLY
events.text: {{other}} sends a declaration of affection on the back of a household account. The account is paid. This is the most encouraging part of the letter.

choices.label: Answer honestly, without promising a wedding

outcome.text: You begin a warmer acquaintance with {{other}}. Nobody is married by correspondence, though both of you enjoy the ink.

choices.label: Accept the offered marriage

outcome.text: You and {{other}} marry by mutual consent. The household account becomes the least interesting part of the document.

choices.label: Return a kind refusal

outcome.text: You decline without circulating the letter. {{other}} appreciates having one disappointment instead of an audience.

events.title: THE PETITION AGAINST YOUR EVENINGS
events.text: {{spouse}} asks why every errand takes you past the same doorway. You offer a well-prepared explanation. {{spouse}} asks how long you have been preparing it.

choices.label: Give a full account and change the arrangement

outcome.text: You answer the question and make room for your spouse’s worry. Trust improves through a less entertaining use of the evening.

choices.label: Turn the suspicion into a public joke

outcome.text: The joke reaches an audience. {{spouse}} withdraws affection and acquires a grievance that is entirely about what you actually did.

choices.label: End the marriage rather than answer

outcome.text: You choose separation. The marriage ends, the household loses resources and the unanswered question survives without a husband or wife to ask it.

events.title: A SUITOR’S EARLY TESTAMENT
events.text: {{other}} offers you a marriage contract and a draft will in the same sitting. The second document has been written considerably more neatly.

choices.label: Discuss how to live together before discussing death

outcome.text: You leave the contracts unsigned and the acquaintance more honest. {{other}} is relieved to put away the better pen.

choices.label: Accept the marriage without the speculative will

outcome.text: You marry {{other}} by consent. Neither of you gains an inheritance in advance of anyone’s death.

choices.label: Forge a richer settlement than you own

outcome.text: You create a false marriage settlement without making a marriage. {{other}} becomes a witness to the fraud, not your spouse.

events.title: THE GIFT RETURNED IN BETTER WRAPPING
events.text: {{other}} returns a courtship gift wrapped more beautifully than when it left you. The rejection appears to have received professional help.

choices.label: Accept the answer and admire the wrapping

outcome.text: You take the refusal without turning it into a quarrel. {{other}} trusts you more for the boundary you respect.

choices.label: Demand payment for the humiliation

outcome.text: You make an enemy of someone who had merely declined you. The wrapping is now the kindest part of the exchange.

events.title: A WITNESS TO THE WRONG ROMANCE
events.text: {{other}} asks you to swear you saw a courting couple promise marriage. You saw two people quarrel over a borrowed cloak, but the fee for remembering otherwise is tempting.

choices.label: Describe exactly what you saw

outcome.text: {{other}} folds the proposed testimony. Your memory has failed to become useful, an imperfection they find very difficult to forgive.

choices.label: Sign the false testimony for a promised reward

outcome.text: The clerk records your oath and asks a second question. {{other}} remembers promising payment rather less clearly than you remember promising to have been there.

choices.label: Warn the people whose names are being used

outcome.text: {{other}} spends supper explaining why nobody should believe you. The explanation repeats your warning to everyone who missed it.

events.title: THE PRACTICAL LOVE POEM
events.text: {{spouse}} discovers a poem you wrote early in the marriage. Your present skill at remembering where the firewood is stored compares poorly with your former devotion.

choices.label: Fetch the wood before discussing the poem

outcome.text: The room warms and {{spouse}} accepts the new verse as an improvement. It has fewer adjectives and better fuel.

choices.label: Recite it with undiminished confidence

outcome.text: You make {{spouse}} laugh, though the wood remains where it was. Affection improves more than the room temperature.

events.title: THE IDENTICAL TOKEN
events.text: {{spouse}} finds a love token that looks exactly like one given to a neighbour. The pedlar who sold them is wisely absent.

choices.label: Admit the token came from a crowded stall

outcome.text: You admit that the token was common and the affection was not. {{spouse}} accepts the distinction after enjoying your discomfort.

choices.label: Commission something personal (7g)

outcome.text: Seven gold buys a token with a private inscription. {{spouse}} reads it twice before deciding not to ask what the first one cost.

choices.label: Accuse your spouse of inventing the comparison

outcome.text: You answer a small doubt with a larger cruelty. Trust falls, and the cheap token has become an expensive object.

events.title: THE PRICE OF PARTING
events.text: You and {{spouse}} are considering separation. The clerk has quoted for three copies: one for each of you and one for everyone who will pretend not to have read it.

choices.label: Pay for a formal separation (12g)

outcome.text: The marriage ends and twelve gold pays for the record. The clerk is the only person who calls the day satisfactory.

choices.label: Try an honest conversation before signing

outcome.text: You keep the marriage and rebuild a little trust. It is a beginning, not a miraculous repair.

choices.label: Destroy the draft and forbid further discussion

outcome.text: The marriage continues under less trust. A torn document is easier to silence than the person who asked for it.

events.title: THE DOWRY WHICH HONKS
events.text: {{spouse}} wants the household’s wedding reserve spent on food rather than another display of respectability. The proposed display has a ribbon budget larger than its supper budget.

choices.label: Put the money into household food (9g)

outcome.text: You fund the reserve and cancel the ribbons. {{spouse}} values an anniversary that can be eaten.

choices.label: Buy the display and leave supper thin (9g)

outcome.text: The ribbons are splendid and the household’s food reserve shrinks. {{spouse}} declines to be nourished by colour.

choices.label: Hold a quiet meal with what you have

outcome.text: You choose an unshowy supper and keep your savings. {{spouse}} enjoys not having to praise anything you have bought.

events.title: THE CHAPERONE’S EXPENSES
events.text: {{other}} brings an itemised account for supervising two people’s courtship. “Looking away at suitable moments” is the largest charge.

choices.label: Ask the supervised couple to review the account

outcome.text: You expose the exaggerated bill without inventing a romantic scandal. {{other}} dislikes the new interest in arithmetic.

choices.label: Pay to spare the couple an argument (5g)

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts payment for having seen less. The bill is exceptionally legible for work conducted in such poor light.

events.title: THE SERENADE AT THE STOREROOM
events.text: {{other}} has been singing beneath a shutter that opens onto a storeroom. The household wants the flour left out of the next verse.

choices.label: Privately explain the mistake

outcome.text: You save {{other}} from a second performance and gain a grateful acquaintance. The flour remains unmoved.

choices.label: Call loudly for an encore

outcome.text: The street demands the refrain. {{other}} discovers that a love song can carry a name much farther when the person named wishes it would stop.

choices.label: Offer the singer a quiet cup indoors (3g)

outcome.text: You pay for a dry place to wait and close the door on the audience. {{other}} discovers that a little hospitality travels farther than the verse.

events.title: THE GUEST WHO CAME WITH THE MARRIAGE
events.text: {{spouse}} has invited a relation to stay. “A short visit” has now acquired a spare blanket and an opinion about the way you cook.

choices.label: Agree on a leaving date together

outcome.text: You and {{spouse}} settle the invitation without a public quarrel. Household trust improves and the spare blanket remains only a blanket.

choices.label: Fund another week’s food (9g)

outcome.text: The food is bought before the visit becomes an argument. {{spouse}} welcomes a contribution that has not brought its own speech.

choices.label: Order the guest out and blame your spouse

outcome.text: The household loses harmony and {{spouse}} loses trust in you. Winning the doorway has cost you something farther inside.

events.title: THE MATCHMAKER’S UNHELPFUL RECOMMENDATION
events.text: {{other}} recommends you for a marriage by praising your ability to withstand disappointment. You would prefer the compliment not to need so many examples.

choices.label: Set out what you actually want in a match

outcome.text: You replace a flattering description with an honest one. {{other}} understands you better and has less material for the next introduction.

choices.label: Invent impressive relations and property

outcome.text: Your invented position becomes a concealed falsehood. {{other}} is impressed by facts that will be expensive to defend.

events.title: THE ANNIVERSARY NEITHER MENTIONED
events.text: You and {{spouse}} have both forgotten the date of your marriage. Each of you is carefully waiting to see whether the other has remembered.

choices.label: Admit it first and share the relief

outcome.text: {{spouse}} laughs with the relief of a person acquitted before accusation. You begin a better evening than either of you had planned.

choices.label: Wait, then accuse your spouse of forgetting

outcome.text: You win a small advantage and spend it immediately on an argument. {{spouse}} is less inclined to celebrate the next year.

events.title: THE OATH THAT WAS NOT YOURS
events.text: {{other}} has circulated a claim that you promised marriage. You remember promising to return a borrowed pot. The pot is still at home.

choices.label: Return the pot before witnesses

outcome.text: You return the object you actually promised and reject the other claim publicly. {{other}} resents the clarity.

choices.label: Pay to withdraw the accusation (9g)

outcome.text: Nine gold buys an end to this claim, together with a secret about how readily your name can be priced.

choices.label: Produce a forged counterclaim

outcome.text: Your counterclaim reaches the clerk, who recognises the false seal. You face a forgery charge; the pot has become the most innocent participant.

charge.offence: Forging evidence in a marriage dispute

events.title: THE LORD WHO TAXED SHADE
events.text: {{other}} demands rent because your roof casts a shadow over a boundary. A servant has measured the offence at noon, when it is cheapest.

choices.label: Pay the demand (7g)

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts seven gold for the shade. A cloud passes over the transaction without paying anything.

choices.label: Ask for a hearing with the measuring stick present

outcome.text: You invite the neighbours to inspect the shade. {{other}} objects to so many people standing in an asset they have not paid to admire.

choices.label: Help neighbouring households object together

outcome.text: The Commons gain confidence and {{other}}’s household records a feud with yours. Shade has become a matter of family honour.

familyFeud.reason: Opposed the demand for shadow rent

choices.label: Pay to mislay the measurements (4g)

outcome.text: Four gold makes the measurements difficult to find. A secret remains about the smaller, more useful payment.

events.title: THE WINDOW WITH A FEE
events.text: In your cell, daylight comes through a gap {{other}} says can be widened. The price is clear. The size of the wall beyond it is less so.

choices.label: Keep your money and mend the bedding

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and make the cell marginally less miserable. {{other}} loses interest in your purse.

choices.label: Attempt the escape (risk a severe head injury)

success.text: You squeeze through and reach open ground. You are outside the prison, with an outstanding charge and very little dignity.

failure.text: The opening leads to a fall. You remain imprisoned with a head injury, and the wall proves much firmer than the offer.

choices.label: Tell the gaoler about the proposed opening

outcome.text: You remain inside, but your cooperation improves your reputation. {{other}} will not offer you another window.

events.title: THE PARDON WITH ROOM FOR A NAME
events.text: {{other}} offers a blank royal pardon, complete with a convincing stain where the seal ought to be. It forgives anything you are prepared to write small enough.

choices.label: Refuse the portable mercy

outcome.text: You decline the forgery. {{other}} moves on to people who have more to forgive and less to lose.

choices.label: Present it as genuine evidence

outcome.text: You acquire a fresh forgery charge without erasing any older one. The stain receives considerably more official attention than expected.

choices.label: Give the blank to the clerk as evidence

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and gain standing with the Crown. {{other}} knows exactly who supplied the paper.

events.title: THE THIEF WHO STOLE THE SIGN
events.text: {{other}} has stolen a tradesperson’s sign rather than any goods. Customers are now queuing outside the thief’s empty shed.

choices.label: Help return the sign before opening time

outcome.text: You restore the sign and gain local standing. {{other}} calls this a waste of an unusually successful theft.

choices.label: Sell directions to the wrong shop (risk a fraud complaint)

success.text: You collect a small payment before the joke is discovered. The shed remains empty and you keep a secret about the route you sold.

failure.text: A customer follows the directions with you still in sight. The complaint names both the empty shed and the person selling its address.

charge.offence: Taking payment for a false shop

events.title: THE JUROR’S LUNCH
events.text: {{other}} asks you to carry a handsome pie to a juror. Inside the lid is the verdict the sender would prefer him to reach.

choices.label: Deliver the whole thing as evidence

outcome.text: You expose the attempted bribe and gain public standing. {{other}} regards the crust as a betrayal.

choices.label: Carry the suggested verdict discreetly

outcome.text: The delivery makes you a party to attempted bribery. The pie is consumed; the written suggestion is kept.

charge.offence: Carrying a bribe to a juror

choices.label: Return it unopened to its owner

outcome.text: You decline the errand and lose a little favour with {{other}}. Your supper remains your own responsibility.

events.title: THE PAID SUBSTITUTE
events.text: {{other}} offers a purse if you will stand in for a relative’s punishment. The promised mark on your arm is described as small by someone who will not be wearing it.

choices.label: Refuse a punishment that is not yours

outcome.text: {{other}} improves the offer, apparently believing your skin has failed to understand the first price. Your arm leaves the negotiation unchanged.

choices.label: Accept the money and the lasting injury

outcome.text: You receive twenty-four gold and a painful burn that leaves chronic pain. {{other}} is satisfied that the family punishment has been properly outsourced.

choices.label: Expose the proposed substitution

outcome.text: The public accusation damages {{other}}’s trust in you and improves your own standing. No part of the payment reaches your skin.

events.title: THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE
events.text: {{other}} wants a disputed receipt washed until the inconvenient line vanishes. The laundress has asked whether justice should be boiled with the linens.

choices.label: Keep the receipt dry and legible

outcome.text: The stain stays on the cloth and out of the wash. {{other}} calls this an unreasonable use of cleanliness as evidence.

choices.label: Wash away the line (risk an evidence charge)

success.text: The stain vanishes. {{other}} admires the clean sleeve with the uncomfortable warmth of someone who now knows exactly what you will wash for a friend.

failure.text: A retained copy exposes the missing line. You acquire an evidence-destruction charge; the paper is cleaner than the account of washing it.

choices.label: Pay for witnessed copies before washing (3g)

outcome.text: You fund copies and make the original trick useless. {{other}} has to dispute what the document says instead of whether anyone can read it.

events.title: THE PRISON SUPPER LIST
events.text: Your cell’s meal list includes meat for four people. {{other}} asks whether anybody has seen either the meat or the other three.

choices.label: Add your name to a truthful complaint

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and gain a little public standing for the complaint. {{other}} becomes a firmer ally inside the walls.

choices.label: Share a better prison meal (8g)

outcome.text: You buy food to share instead of waiting for the list to become edible. You recover some health and {{other}} trusts the meal more than the list.

choices.label: Save your own portion and refuse the argument

outcome.text: You eat your share in full. {{other}} watches the bowl empty with an expression that will be present at the next division.

events.title: THE ALIBI WITH A HOLE IN IT
events.text: {{other}} wants you to swear you spent the night together. The proposed alibi includes an hour when the whole square saw you somewhere else.

choices.label: Point out the missing hour

outcome.text: {{other}} asks whether you are quite certain you remember correctly. You remain inconveniently certain.

choices.label: Swear to the impossible evening (risk perjury)

success.text: The contradiction is not tested at this hearing. {{other}} gains trust in you and you acquire a secret whose witnesses still live in the square.

failure.text: The missing hour is put to witnesses. You acquire a perjury charge with unusually easy evidence.

events.title: THE ROPE INSPECTOR
events.text: {{other}} asks you to test a condemned climbing rope before it is sold again. The test consists of trusting the seller’s statement that it was only condemned on a technicality.

choices.label: Cut the rope so it cannot be sold

outcome.text: You destroy a dangerous bargain and gain public trust. {{other}} loses faith in your respect for private property.

choices.label: Test it above the quarry (risk a fatal fall)

success.text: The rope holds long enough for you to come down. You are paid ten gold and acquire an enduring dislike of technicalities.

failure.text: The rope parts above a lower shelf. You survive the fall with a broken bone; the rope seller describes this as useful information.

catastrophe.text: The condemned section parts over the quarry. The last assurance you hear is that it held yesterday.

effects.death: Killed in a fall while testing a condemned rope.

choices.label: Leave the seller without endorsing the rope

outcome.text: You decline to give an opinion that somebody might later mistake for a guarantee. {{other}} will need a different signature.

events.title: THE CHICKENS UNDER GUARD
events.text: {{other}} supports a new fine for wandering hens. The guard hired to watch the impounded birds is a dog, and expenses are rising whenever it looks hungry.

choices.label: Challenge the expense list publicly

outcome.text: You make the claim difficult to defend and gain standing with the Commons. {{other}} becomes a rival with a remarkably poultry-shaped grievance.

choices.label: Contribute to the households’ release fund (6g)

outcome.text: You contribute to the relief fund. Your family’s reputation improves; the dog remains the only participant without a receipt.

choices.label: Claim the release money with forged ownership papers

outcome.text: You obtain eleven gold and a fraud charge. Several actual owners are able to identify what you do not own.

charge.offence: Claiming impounded birds with false papers

events.title: THE KEY THAT OPENS EVERY DOOR
events.text: {{other}} claims to have a prison key that opens every door. It is drawn on parchment. The proposed escape requires a smith and a great deal of belief.

choices.label: Keep out of the scheme

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned without adding another charge to your record. {{other}} calls you unadventurous from inside a locked room.

choices.label: Commission the key and attempt escape (10g; more prison if caught)

success.text: The copied key opens a service door. You escape the cell, but remain wanted for breaking custody.

failure.text: The key turns in nothing. The search finds the drawing and adds three years to your sentence.

choices.label: Surrender the plan without accusing anyone else

outcome.text: The gaoler takes the plan and examines the drawing. {{other}} now regards you as a rival; the drawing has still opened more conversation than doors.

events.title: THE WITNESS IN A DIFFERENT CAP
events.text: {{other}} offers to testify twice in a boundary dispute using a different cap for the second appearance. The caps are convincing. The beard is exactly the same.

choices.label: Stop the second testimony

outcome.text: You expose the trick and improve your standing. {{other}} cannot decide which cap to wear while resenting you.

choices.label: Act surprised at the second witness (risk a charge)

success.text: You sustain the performance long enough to escape immediate questioning. {{other}} trusts you more, and the deception remains a dangerous secret.

failure.text: The beard is recognised between the two caps. You acquire a false-testimony charge for pretending not to notice it.

events.title: THE THIEF’S CONFESSION BOOK
events.text: {{other}} has stolen the book in which a penitent listed stolen goods. It may be the only theft in the lane that comes with its own inventory.

choices.label: Return the book without reading it aloud

outcome.text: You protect the private confession and improve your reputation. {{other}} sees the book depart without any of the profit intended for it.

choices.label: Use the list to demand money

outcome.text: You create a blackmail charge and a secret about your own conduct. Confession has finally added something to the list.

choices.label: Hand it to the clerk as evidence of the theft

outcome.text: You expose the theft and anger {{other}}. The book is treated as evidence rather than as an invitation to collect from everyone in it.

events.title: THE FINE FOR BEING AVAILABLE
events.text: A clerk has put your name on an unpaid fine because you were standing nearest the desk. {{other}} offers to vouch for you, provided you explain what innocence usually pays.

choices.label: Request the original charge and witnesses

outcome.text: You contest the clerical shortcut and gain local standing. {{other}} is disappointed to discover that assistance can be made unnecessary.

choices.label: Pay five gold and keep your day (5g)

outcome.text: The disputed fine is paid and a receipt supplied. {{other}} has settled the amount without once managing to establish the offence.

choices.label: Alter the account to name a neighbour

outcome.text: You create an actual forgery charge while trying to escape an administrative error. The clerk now has something definite to write.

events.title: THE COFFIN WHICH RATTLES
events.text: {{other}} offers work carrying a coffin that rattles like tableware. The supposed mourner asks you not to tilt his uncle.
