choices.label: Ask what the work actually pays

outcome.text: You insist on a clear wage and receive five gold for a day carrying equipment. The knight leaves without an oath from you.

choices.label: Decline the offer without a quarrel

outcome.text: You decline the post. The road remains open, and you have not promised to carry someone else’s mistakes.

events.title: AN UNCANNY STREAK
events.text: You keep winning at dice. The other players have reached the point of blaming sorcery rather than their own arithmetic, a stage at which leaving may be the cleverest throw.

choices.label: Ride the luck for all it is worth

success.text: You cleaned out the whole table and walked home whistling, pockets jingling.

failure.text: Your luck finally blinked. You lost the lot, and a tooth, to a sore loser.

choices.label: Quit while you are ahead

outcome.text: You pocketed your winnings and left. The gamblers glared; fortune, like milk, can turn.

events.title: A CRUEL WINTER
events.text: The cold settles deep in your frail chest, as it always does. The herb-wife eyes you with pity and a price.

choices.label: Buy the strongest tonic (7g)

outcome.text: The tonic was vile and dear, but you saw the spring. For a sickly soul, that is a victory. The herb-wife now greets you by name across the market, which is not the compliment it sounds like.

choices.label: Endure it by the hearth

success.text: You wrapped in every blanket you own and outlasted the cold. Barely.

failure.text: The fever took hold and very nearly took you. You emerge in spring, hollow-eyed, with a cough that never entirely leaves.

events.title: THE SWEATING SICKNESS
events.text: A real fever has reached your household. The herb-wife is frank about what she can attempt, which makes her prices less comforting and her advice more credible.

choices.label: Pay the herb-wife at once (6g)

outcome.text: Her tonic is bitter but swift. The fever breaks before it can take root.

choices.label: Sweat it out and pray

success.text: You sweated through three foul nights and woke clear-eyed. Spared, this time.

failure.text: The fever digs in for the long haul. This sickness will not pass quickly.

events.title: THE REEVE COMES KNOCKING
events.text: The reeve’s men bring questions about your misdeeds. One has brought irons in case the answers prove inconvenient; the other has brought a receipt book.

choices.label: Bribe your way out (15g)

outcome.text: A heavy purse changes hands. The reeve discovers he was quite mistaken. Funny, that.

choices.label: Make a run for it

success.text: Out the back and over three fences. Free, filthy, and faster than you look.

failure.text: They caught you at the treeline and clapped you in irons.

choices.label: Surrender with dignity

outcome.text: You go quietly. The dungeon door clangs shut behind you.

events.title: A MATCH IS PROPOSED
events.text: A matchmaker offers an introduction to someone kind, capable and tired of being valued by the contents of a dowry chest. Consent, rather than a wedding, is the first business.

choices.label: Consent to the proposed household match

outcome.text: You marry by mutual consent and welcome a real spouse into the household. The settlement begins a life together, not a transfer of somebody’s belongings.

choices.label: Hold out for nobility

outcome.text: You spurned the match, eyes fixed on a grander union. Ambitious. Possibly foolish.

choices.label: Decline the match without insulting the suitor

outcome.text: You refuse kindly and leave the other person free to choose another life. No animal is required to explain the decision.

events.title: AN INVITATION TO THE HALL
events.text: You are invited to the high table after an account of your wit reaches the steward. It arrives slightly improved. You must now live up to something you never quite said.

choices.label: Charm the whole table

success.text: You had them roaring with laughter. The lord himself toasted you. Doors are opening.

failure.text: You used the wrong spoon, then the wrong fork, then insulted a baroness. A long carriage ride home.

choices.label: Quietly observe and learn

outcome.text: You said little and watched much. You now know who hates whom, and that is power.

events.title: A RIVAL AT COURT
events.text: {{other}} dismisses your success as an accident of useful acquaintances. The charge is delivered to as many useful acquaintances as possible.

choices.label: Expose the contradiction in the rumour

success.text: You make {{other}} answer for the contradictory story. Your reputation rises and the rivalry becomes explicit.

failure.text: Your trap contradicts your own account. {{other}} gains an advantage and a clearer reason to keep the rivalry alive.

choices.label: Buy a pause in the rumour (12g)

outcome.text: You pay twelve gold and gain a brief respite. {{other}} learns that silence has a price worth remembering.

choices.label: Challenge the rumour in public

outcome.text: You demand an answer before witnesses. {{other}} becomes a named rival instead of a rumour without an address.

events.title: A NOBLE PROPOSAL
events.text: {{other}} proposes a marriage of mutual advantage and asks what sort of life you would want beyond the advantage. It is the first question not answered by the settlement.

choices.label: Accept the proposed marriage

outcome.text: You marry into a better-connected household. Your standing can improve through that connection; no title is granted merely by the wedding.

choices.label: Decline without humiliating the suitor

outcome.text: You refuse the match graciously. Your reputation improves because you leave the proposal as private as it can still be.

events.title: THE NIGHT VIGIL
events.text: To be dubbed a knight you must keep an overnight vigil in the cold chapel, armour on, praying till dawn.

choices.label: Endure the full vigil

success.text: You knelt unmoving till dawn, half-frozen and wholly resolved. The bishop is impressed.

failure.text: You nodded off and clattered to the floor at midnight. Mortifying, but you finished anyway.

choices.label: Sneak a flask of wine for warmth

outcome.text: The wine kept you warm and the vigil bearable. The bishop suspects nothing. The goose would be proud.

events.title: A CHALLENGE OF HONOUR
events.text: Sir Roderick produces a glove for a challenge of honour. The careful preparation suggests he has been finding the original quarrel insufficiently productive.

choices.label: Accept the duel (risk a serious cut)

success.text: You disarm Roderick and stop with the weapon at his throat. He remains alive, humiliated and much less likely to call the next quarrel accidental.

failure.text: Roderick cuts you badly. The injury is real; your refusal to pretend it was a victory earns a small measure of respect.

choices.label: Refuse. It is beneath you

outcome.text: You called the challenge childish and walked away. Some respect the restraint. Roderick crows victory.

choices.label: Propose a contest of wits instead

outcome.text: You out-argued him so thoroughly the crowd laughed Roderick out of the square. A bloodless rout.

events.title: THE LORD’S SUMMONS
events.text: Your liege calls a muster over a disputed river crossing. The written claim is dry; the crossing, you are warned, will not be.

choices.label: Ride to war for your liege

outcome.text: You don your armour and ride out. The road to glory is muddy and smells of fear.

choices.label: Send coin in your stead (20g)

outcome.text: You paid scutage to avoid the muster. Pragmatic, if not glorious. Some call it cowardice.

events.title: THE PEASANTS’ PETITION
events.text: Tenants bring a petition against a levy assessed on roofs, including two roofs that fell in last winter. Your steward calls the assessment consistent.

choices.label: Fund relief from the harsh assessment

outcome.text: You pay for relief and improve loyalty. Your household gives up coin and stores; the tenants receive an answer they can survive.

choices.label: Enforce the assessment without relief

outcome.text: Your coffers grow as household loyalty and stores fall. The cruelty is recorded in your reputation rather than blamed on a parent who may not be alive.

choices.label: Offer a smaller assessment and clear terms

outcome.text: You take a smaller return and improve loyalty. People can plan around an amount that no longer changes with the steward’s mood.

events.title: A WHISPER OF TREASON
events.text: Plotters invite you to lend your name and evidence against a powerful baron. They promise to share the reward and are less exact about whose neck secures the attempt.

choices.label: Join the conspiracy

success.text: Your evidence reaches the council and the plotters pay you fifty gold. The baron faces an inquiry; no new title has yet been granted.

failure.text: The plot was betrayed. Guards drag you to the block at dawn.

effects.death: Beheaded for treason. The crowd, as ever, brought pies.

choices.label: Betray the plotters to the baron

outcome.text: You sold them out. The baron rewards your "loyalty" handsomely, though you sleep with one eye open now.

choices.label: Refuse without inventing a later victory

outcome.text: You keep your name off the conspiracy. What the plotters do next is theirs; your legal record does not acquire their plan.

events.title: BUILDING A LEGACY
events.text: A mason offers a public dedication worthy of your wealth. The relief wardens ask whether the money might also do something for people who cannot read the inscription.

choices.label: Fund chapel relief and a public dedication (40g)

outcome.text: You endow relief associated with the chapel. Food security and Church standing improve; the dedication does not pretend a new building rose in an afternoon.

choices.label: Fund care for the sick and poor (40g)

outcome.text: You pay for practical relief and improve public health conditions. The people doing the work receive supplies rather than an expensive drawing of a hospital.

choices.label: Keep the reserve for your household

outcome.text: You retain the money and improve the household’s food reserve by careful planning. There will be no inscription recording the choice.

events.title: A PEDLAR OF RELICS
events.text: A pedlar offers a supposedly angelic feather. The story is magnificent; the object is the sort a barnyard bird leaves without an audience.

choices.label: Buy it faithfully (8g)

outcome.text: You bought the feather and prayed over it nightly. Faith asks no questions. Strangely, you feel comforted.

choices.label: Expose him as a fraud

success.text: You show why the feather is an ordinary bird’s feather. Your reputation improves and {{other}} loses your trust rather than vanishing from the town.

failure.text: Your objection fails to convince the onlookers. {{other}} keeps the advantage and you keep the memory of being contradicted by people who never examined the feather.

choices.label: Steal it for the goose

outcome.text: You take the feather for Sir Quackbeard, who does not recognise a need to have it back. {{other}} has a genuine theft to complain about.

charge.offence: Taking a relic seller’s goods without payment

events.title: A CALLING TO THE CLOISTER
events.text: The abbot offers you holy orders, long work and a small place in a community that will know when you are avoiding either. You are allowed time to answer.

choices.label: Take the vows and duties

outcome.text: You take holy orders and gain Church standing. The vows do not appoint you to a paid post; service and qualifications must still earn one.

choices.label: Decline while offering ordinary help

outcome.text: You decline the vows and offer practical service. The abbot accepts an honest answer more readily than a beautiful promise.

events.title: A VILLAGER CRIES MIRACLE
events.text: A child’s recovery is being attributed to your nearby prayer. The people praising you have forgotten the person who carried water through the night.

choices.label: Accept the attention and its donations

outcome.text: You receive donations and public standing. The prayer is remembered, together with your willingness to stand beside its collection bowl.

choices.label: Credit the care and decline the claim

outcome.text: You insist that care deserves thanks as well as prayer. Church standing improves; you do not manufacture a new miracle to explain your humility.

events.title: A MOTHER TAKES ILL
events.text: {{mother}} is seriously ill. The herb-wife offers a costly treatment without a promise. Your mother objects to the expense before allowing herself to ask whether it might work.

choices.label: Fund the uncertain treatment (15g; she may die)

success.text: The treatment succeeds. {{mother}} recovers enough to complain about the fee, a sound you had been afraid of never hearing again.

failure.text: The treatment cannot save {{mother}}. You stay beside the bed and hold a hand no amount of spending can keep warm.

choices.label: Offer care and prayer without the treatment (she may die)

success.text: The fever breaks. {{mother}} credits your company before discussing anybody’s theology.

failure.text: {{mother}} dies despite the care you can give. You do not mistake being unable to pay for having been unwilling to love.

events.title: A CHILD IS BORN
events.text: A child has arrived in your household. The smallest person in the room has reorganised every task without speaking a comprehensible word.

choices.label: Welcome the child with joy

outcome.text: A healthy babe joins your household and your line continues. You weep, then panic about feeding it.

choices.label: Welcome the child quietly

outcome.text: You keep the first days close to the household, making promises before making announcements.

events.title: AN OLD FOE, HUMBLED
events.text: Sir Roderick appears at your door, greyer and smaller and short of a manor. "I... was wrong about you," he mutters. "About the apple. About all of it."

choices.label: Forgive him at last

outcome.text: You clasp his hand. Decades of grudge dissolve in a moment. He weeps; so, secretly, do you.

choices.label: Hand him a single apple, and shut the door

outcome.text: You give him one apple. "Now we are even," you say. The door closes. Petty? Perhaps. Satisfying? Immensely.

events.title: A SQUALLING ARRIVAL
events.text: Your mother sits you down with a strange smile. By harvest, you will not be the only small person in this cottage.

choices.label: Rejoice! A playmate at last

outcome.text: A sibling is born! Loud, wrinkled, and immediately beloved. You vow to teach them everything about turnips.

choices.label: Sulk about sharing the porridge

outcome.text: A sibling is born anyway. You sulk magnificently, but the baby grips your finger and your cold heart thaws a little.

events.title: THE CHILD AT YOUR FENCE
events.text: A child keeps stopping outside your fence. Today they kick the same pebble in a circle until you look over. Then they kick it straight to you.

choices.label: Share your turnip

outcome.text: You split the turnip and sit together on the fence. By the time the last piece is gone, you have a new friend.

choices.label: Challenge them to a pebble contest

success.text: You lose by a suspiciously small amount. Your new friend demands a rematch before you have even picked up the pebbles.

failure.text: You win, then explain exactly how much you won by. The other child stalks away and leaves you to admire the pebble alone.

choices.label: Hide behind Sir Quackbeard

outcome.text: Sir Quackbeard hisses the child back down the lane. You are left with one goose and a pebble that nobody wants to kick.

events.title: A KINDRED SPIRIT
events.text: A traveller laughs at your worst joke and stays for the explanation. By the time you share a bench, you know the kindness was deliberate.

choices.label: Stand them a round (3g)

outcome.text: Ale flowed, tales grew taller, and by closing time you had sworn eternal friendship twice. Once even sober.

choices.label: Swap stories but guard your purse

outcome.text: A fine evening of talk. You part warmly, but strangers stay strangers when the purse stays shut.

events.title: A DEBT OF STEEL
events.text: In the training yard a falling practice beam nearly brains another squire, and you shove them clear at the last instant.

choices.label: Help them up and make light of it

outcome.text: "I owe you my skull," they grin, clasping your arm. You have gained a shield-brother, the kind who stands beside you when it costs him something.

choices.label: Demand a favour in return

outcome.text: They pay you a grudging coin and remember the price of your help more than the help itself.

events.title: ENVY IN THE LANE
events.text: A neighbour has begun comparing your fortunes in public. The list contains every piece of your luck and none of the work that preceded it.

choices.label: Try to win him over

success.text: You disarmed his envy with honest flattery about barrels. Not a friend, perhaps, but no longer an enemy.

failure.text: He took your kindness for gloating. The feud is now official; he has already composed insulting verses.

choices.label: Let him stew

outcome.text: You ignore him. The grudge ferments nicely in its barrel. Aldwin is now, formally, your rival.

choices.label: Mock him first, publicly

outcome.text: Your jibe about his wobbliest barrel drew roars of laughter. Aldwin will never, ever forgive it.

events.title: THE GREYING COURTIER
events.text: An experienced courtier offers to teach you which doors to knock on and which invitations mean you are being sent out of the room. The second lesson was expensive to learn.

choices.label: Become their protégé

outcome.text: You gain a mentor who knows where every body at court is buried, and can point to three of them from the window.

choices.label: Suspect a trap and decline

outcome.text: At court, kindness is usually bait. You bow out gracefully, and wonder for years what they knew.

events.title: A LORD TAKES NOTICE
events.text: A lord offers a place in the retinue, with protection and obligations to be spoken before witnesses. The promise is useful precisely because it will be remembered.

choices.label: Kneel and swear the oath

outcome.text: You swear fealty before the hall. A liege’s favour opens doors, and his wars are now your wars.

choices.label: Keep your independence

outcome.text: You decline with careful courtesy. Bramwell nods slowly. Freedom kept, favour lost.

events.title: THE PESTILENCE COMES
events.text: A traveller is taken ill in the square. By evening the news has reached every door, growing more certain as the evidence becomes harder to find.

choices.label: Flee to the hills at once

success.text: You fled to the high pastures and waited it out. Lonely and hungry and breathing.

failure.text: The fever finds you on the road. A nearby household gives you shelter, and the illness must run its real course.

catastrophe.text: You fled, but carried the sickness with you. The fever finds you on the road.

effects.death: Taken by the Pestilence on a lonely hill road.

choices.label: Stay and tend the sick

success.text: You nursed the dying with rags and prayers and somehow did not fall ill. The village calls you blessed.

failure.text: You fall ill after tending the sick. Another carer takes your place; accepting the bed is harder than offering it.

catastrophe.text: You tended the sick, and the sickness took you in turn. A merciful death, the priest says. He is lying.

effects.death: Died of the Pestilence, tending those who could not be saved.

choices.label: Barricade yourself indoors

success.text: You sealed the door and rationed turnips for a grim season. The Pestilence passed you by.

failure.text: The sickness reaches the house. You need care and lose strength, but the barred door has not decided the ending.

catastrophe.text: It came through the rats, through the very walls. There was no barricade against it.

effects.death: Died of the Pestilence, alone behind a barred door.

events.title: A WORLD MADE EMPTY
events.text: The sickness has eased, leaving exhausted households and urgent work. People are counting who is available before agreeing what labour is worth.

choices.label: Ask for wages that reflect the actual shortage

outcome.text: You earn more for urgent work and gain standing among labouring households. No particular neighbour is declared dead merely to explain the wage.

choices.label: Pay to restore a neglected dwelling

outcome.text: You improve your own household’s shelter and standing. You do not acquire somebody else’s cottage simply by noticing its empty door.

choices.label: Help with the ordinary work of recovery

outcome.text: You improve household food and public health conditions through practical aid. The quiet work does not require a triumphant explanation.

events.title: THE LEVY IS CALLED
events.text: The levy is called. A spear and a place in the line are offered with considerably more certainty than any account of when you will return.

choices.label: March with the levy

outcome.text: You march off to war, one frightened spearman among hundreds. The mud is the only certainty.

choices.label: Hide in the turnip cellar

success.text: You hid among the turnips until the sergeants gave up looking. Coward? Survivor? Both.

failure.text: They found you cowering and dragged you out by the ankle. Now you march AND everyone knows.

choices.label: Pay the fine to stay (8g)

outcome.text: A few coins to the sergeant and you keep your skin and your turnips. Money well spent.

events.title: THE GOOSE IS SUMMONED
events.text: The reeve summons Sir Quackbeard in a disputed theft. The clerk leaves space for a mark; the goose inspects whether it can be eaten.

choices.label: Interpret the honks

outcome.text: You translate three honks as "the baker did it." The baker confesses to avoid further poultry law.

choices.label: Let the goose speak

outcome.text: Sir Quackbeard bites the reeve. The court accepts this as strong testimony.

choices.label: Blame the pie

outcome.text: You accuse the pie of tempting honest men. The court pauses, then fines you for nonsense.

events.title: A PIG ON TRIAL
events.text: A pig is accused of eating chapel flowers. The court debates intent while the defendant attempts to consume the evidence basket.

choices.label: Defend the pig

success.text: Your speech on floral temptation moves the court. The pig is spared and immediately eats the verdict.

failure.text: Your defense collapses when the accused eats your sleeve.

choices.label: Demand harsh justice

outcome.text: The pig is sentenced to public shame. It appears immune.

events.title: HOLY BATHWATER
events.text: A friar sells holy bathwater that smells of yesterday’s broth. He calls the floating onion a sign that the blessing has taken.

choices.label: Buy a bottle (5g)

outcome.text: You drink it and feel warmth in the soul, or possibly leek. The friar calls both miracles.

choices.label: Expose the soup

success.text: You find a turnip floating in the relic jar. The crowd turns on him with ladles.

failure.text: The friar declares the turnip a sign. You are booed by people holding soup.

choices.label: Ask for bread too

outcome.text: The friar, impressed by your theology of lunch, gives you a heel of bread.

events.title: THE DOCTOR'S CURE
events.text: A leech seller offers to treat unpaid rent. His argument is that the landlord cannot demand blood if somebody else has already taken it.

choices.label: Pay for the dubious treatment (4g)

outcome.text: The treatment costs blood and coin without touching the rent. You leave with a clearer sense of what the leeches actually consume.

choices.label: Ask whether the landlord has agreed

outcome.text: The seller has not consulted the landlord. You gain judgement while the leeches continue to make a much simpler living.

choices.label: Sell a false specimen to the seller

outcome.text: You earn six gold and create a fraud charge. A worm in a cup has proved more difficult to defend than to sell.

events.title: SAINT SOMEBODY'S TOE
events.text: A seller displays a waxy toe attributed to a saint whose name becomes less certain when you ask for the history of the other nine.

choices.label: Buy the toe (7g)

outcome.text: The toe is wax. Your faith wobbles, but your candle supply improves.

choices.label: Ask it to bless you

outcome.text: Nothing happens. The seller says the toe is shy before crowds.

choices.label: Report him to the priest

outcome.text: The priest confiscates the toe, then quietly asks if there were any fingers.

events.title: THE ALEHOUSE OATH
events.text: The tavern agrees to dig defensive works before dawn. Nobody has agreed which side of the ditch Swineford ought to occupy.

choices.label: Dig bravely

outcome.text: By dawn you have made a ditch, lost a shoe, and invented a new smell.

choices.label: Sell shovels

outcome.text: You sell shovels at heroic prices. The moat is poor; your purse is excellent.

choices.label: Sleep under the table

outcome.text: You wake to find the moat is actually around you.

events.title: THE MILLER'S TOLL
events.text: The miller calls his enlarged scoop an improvement in accuracy. It is certainly more accurate at transferring flour into his own store.

choices.label: Challenge the measure

success.text: You find a stone hidden in his scoop. The village laughs until flour comes out of their noses.

failure.text: The miller talks faster than his wheel. You leave poorer and dusted white.

choices.label: Pay and remember

outcome.text: You pay quietly. Your revenge ripens like damp grain.

events.title: THE BELL RINGER'S BET
events.text: The bell ringer bets that you cannot sleep through matins. He holds the rope like a man whose confidence has a very direct source.

choices.label: Take the bet

success.text: You sleep like a blessed log. The bell ringer fears you may be part stone.

failure.text: The first bell launches you out of bed and into a bucket.

choices.label: Ring it first

outcome.text: You ring early. Half the village arrives angry, dressed, and spiritually confused.

events.title: THE TURNIP ORACLE
events.text: A root split by frost is being read as a weather omen. The keeper promises an answer before supper, when the evidence will be eaten.

choices.label: Study the crack rather than buy the prophecy

outcome.text: You learn how frost split the root and improve household food planning. The forecast is useful precisely because nobody claims it speaks.

choices.label: Buy it as food and end the performance

outcome.text: You make a meal of the disputed evidence. The household gains food; no prediction is proved merely because you are fed.

events.title: THE WRONG SPOON
events.text: The steward gives you a spoon whose use depends on the guest seated above you. You have been placed directly beneath a person who will not eat.

choices.label: Use the spoon and accept the risk of a joke

success.text: You choose correctly and gain a little courtly standing. The spoon performs the undistinguished task it was made for.

failure.text: You choose badly and lose standing. The steward now has a story in which the most important object is cutlery.

choices.label: Use bread and leave the rule untested

outcome.text: You eat neatly with bread and gain a little judgement. The idle guest remains the only person waiting on the spoon.

events.title: THE JESTER'S BITE
events.text: The jester has prepared a joke about your boots. The room is waiting to discover whether your power is large enough to survive a small laugh.

choices.label: Laugh loudest

outcome.text: You laugh first and steal the sting. The court likes a target who can bow.

choices.label: Insult him back

success.text: Your reply lands so neatly the jester bows to you. Terrible for him, excellent for your legend.

failure.text: Your comeback limps out and dies near the salt cellar.

events.title: A VERY OLD FAMILY TREE
events.text: A clerk offers a royal pedigree with space left for your preferred ancestor. The oldest branch of the family tree is still drying.

choices.label: Buy the ancestors (18g)

outcome.text: You gain three dukes, a saint, and one suspiciously handsome oak tree.

choices.label: Expose the ink

outcome.text: You point out the wet seal. The clerk says your eyesight is lowborn.

choices.label: Add the goose

outcome.text: Sir Quackbeard is inserted as a Norman baron. Somehow the chart improves.

events.title: THE GOLDEN FLATTERER
events.text: A courtier praises your judgement so extensively that the favour he wants has begun to sound overdue.

choices.label: Reward the praise (8g)

outcome.text: The praise doubles at once. Your nose is now compared to a noble ship.

choices.label: Ask what he wants

outcome.text: He wanted a post, a purse, and your cousin's hand. You give him none and keep your spoon.

events.title: THE BISHOP'S FISH
events.text: The bishop claims the largest fish on grounds of spiritual precedence. The dish has become an excellent test of how hungry theology can be.

choices.label: Agree piously

outcome.text: The bishop takes the fish and a second helping of the argument that got it for him. He blesses you between mouthfuls and has forgotten your name by the fruit.

choices.label: Argue theology

success.text: You prove the smallest fish is humblest and therefore holiest. The bishop loses appetite and argument, in that order.

failure.text: You confuse a psalm with a recipe. The bishop keeps the fish and the moral high ground.

events.title: THE SINGING LAWYER
events.text: A lawyer presents a boundary claim in rhyme. The verse is impeccable, which is awkward because the measurements are not.

choices.label: Join the rhyme

success.text: Your couplet wins the room and, somehow, the argument. The clerk copies it into the roll, where it will embarrass someone for a century.

failure.text: You rhyme "acre" with "baker." The judge ages visibly and rules against everyone present.

choices.label: Demand plain speech

outcome.text: Everyone thanks you except the lawyer, who was halfway to rhyming "ditch." The case is decided in an hour instead of a season.

events.title: THE COURT PORTRAIT
events.text: A painter has rendered your face with dismaying honesty. The clothes are splendid, so no one can claim the same mistake affected the whole canvas.

choices.label: Praise the honesty

outcome.text: The court admires your humility. The painter admits he painted the cabbage from memory. It hangs in the great hall for the rest of your life.

memory.note: A famously unflattering portrait hangs where everyone can see it.

choices.label: Demand beauty (10g)

outcome.text: The new version has heroic cheekbones and no known relation to you. The first one is not destroyed, merely moved somewhere with worse light.

events.title: HONOUR OF THE TURNIP
events.text: A knight mocks the root on your crest. The insult might be harmless if he were not waiting so eagerly to see what you will pay for a reply.

choices.label: Challenge him

success.text: You strike his shield so hard the turnip becomes fashionable.

failure.text: He knocks you into a cart of actual turnips. The symbolism is unbearable.

choices.label: Embrace the turnip

outcome.text: You declare the turnip humble, nourishing, and hard to kill. The crowd cheers despite itself.

events.title: THE SQUIRE'S HELMET
events.text: A squire has polished your helmet through a thin patch. You can now admire the work from both sides of the metal.

choices.label: Praise the work

outcome.text: The squire beams and drops the helmet on your foot.

choices.label: Teach discipline

outcome.text: You lecture on care, duty, and not blinding allies with shine.

events.title: THE PUDDING PRIZE
events.text: The tourney offers a spur for skill and a pudding for endurance. Competitors are becoming suspicious about which contest is expected to produce more casualties.

choices.label: Fight for the spur

success.text: You win the spur and only a modest limp. Chivalry smiles.

failure.text: You lose the bout and land face-first in the prize pudding. The heralds will describe this for years, always at feasts.

memory.note: Unhorsed into a pudding before the whole tourney field.

choices.label: Fight for the pudding

outcome.text: You win the pudding by terrifying everyone with sincerity, then eat a third of it standing up.

events.title: THE HORSE SERMON
events.text: The chaplain blesses the warhorses. One bows its head at exactly the right moment, creating an unfortunate comparison with the riders.

choices.label: Pray beside it

outcome.text: The horse sneezes on you at the amen. The chaplain calls it a sign, and the stable hands start calling you Blessed of the Bay Mare.

choices.label: Question its piety

outcome.text: It steps on your boot. The debate is settled, and the chaplain writes down that you doubted publicly.

events.title: A RANSOM IN POULTRY
events.text: A captured knight’s proposed ransom contains poultry, buttons and an account of why ready coin would be beneath the dignity of his house.

choices.label: Accept the ransom

outcome.text: The ducks arrive furious. The promise not to sing proves priceless, and the knight leaves owing you a courtesy he will one day be asked to repay.

memory.note: A knight ransomed himself in poultry and still owes a favour.

choices.label: Demand proper coin

success.text: His family pays in coin and apologizes for the ducks. They do not forget being made to apologize.

failure.text: His family sends more ducks. You have negotiated poorly and now keep five ducks.

events.title: THE RUSTY SWORD RELIC
events.text: A monk identifies your rusty practice sword as a martyr’s relic. You remember the smith making it, but the monk says certainty can be a spiritual obstacle.

choices.label: Donate it

outcome.text: Pilgrims kiss the rust. You feel pious and slightly worried about tetanus.

choices.label: Keep your sword

outcome.text: You keep it. The monk asks if your boot has any sacred blisters.

events.title: THE DUCKING STOOL HONOUR
events.text: A village asks you to settle a dispute by ducking both parties. The stated advantage is that nobody needs to listen to them finish.

choices.label: Dunk both equally

outcome.text: Justice splashes. Everyone leaves wet, offended, and weirdly satisfied. The village adds your name to the custom.

choices.label: Hear the case properly

outcome.text: You listen for an hour and discover the true villain is a missing cheese. Word spreads that you will actually hear a case, which is going to cost you every future afternoon.

events.title: THE BAD HERALD
events.text: Your herald announces a title from the rehearsal notes rather than the approved roll. The mistake describes your damp estate with painful accuracy.

choices.label: Accept the damp title and laugh first

outcome.text: You make the mistake safe to laugh at and gain household loyalty. The herald retains a job that suddenly feels much less secure.

memory.note: A herald’s joke became a title you chose to keep.

choices.label: Correct the roll without inventing a punishment

outcome.text: You have the proper title read and lose a little charm. The household learns you value precision even when everyone has heard the alternative.

events.title: THE FEAST DISASTER
events.text: At your feast, sauce catches fire just as a guest praises the kitchen’s originality. The cook waits to hear whether this is a compliment or a charge.

choices.label: Call it entertainment

outcome.text: You declare it a new French fashion. No one knows enough French to disagree.

choices.label: Blame the cook

outcome.text: The cook bows and points out you ordered "something memorable." Treason by accuracy.

events.title: YOUR FACE IN GLASS
events.text: A proposed chapel window gives you a halo and very prominent ears. The glazier says the ears will be less noticeable once people start praying.

choices.label: Praise the piety

outcome.text: You praise the holy light. At sunset, your ears glow across the nave.

choices.label: Pay for smaller ears (15g)

outcome.text: The glazier reduces them. The saint beside you now looks disappointed.

events.title: THE OVERPROUD COUSIN
events.text: A relative insists the family has always been noble while hiding the household’s old tools. The tools have a more convincing account of the past.

choices.label: Let him boast

outcome.text: He invents an ancestor who conquered a ditch. The room chooses to believe it, which means someone will eventually check.

choices.label: Mention the mud

outcome.text: You speak warmly of Swineford mud. Half the court laughs; the other half checks its boots. Your cousin does not speak to you until Candlemas.

events.title: THE REEVE'S PETITION
events.text: The reeve asks to tax smoke because it passes through your air. His calculation makes a cold, poor household look like a wilful tax evader.

choices.label: Reject the foolish tax

outcome.text: The villagers cheer. The reeve sadly scratches "cloud rent" from his next proposal. The whole village now knows what sort of lord it has, which is worth more than the four shillings.

choices.label: Allow a tiny tax

outcome.text: The treasury gains coin. Every chimney now smokes accusingly, and the reeve begins drafting cloud rent in earnest.

memory.note: You put a tax on chimney smoke and the village has not forgotten.

events.title: THE FRIAR AND THE PUDDING
events.text: A friar condemns appetite while concealing a pudding under his robe. A dark patch is developing exactly where the argument is weakest.

choices.label: Expose the pudding

outcome.text: The pudding drops at the word "temptation." The sermon ends early and sticky, and the friar remembers precisely who was pointing.

choices.label: Protect his dignity

outcome.text: You cough loudly while he rescues dessert. He blesses you with grateful crumbs and, more usefully, owes you a silence of your own one day.

memory.note: A friar owes you a kindness for a pudding nobody mentioned.

events.title: THE UPSIDE-DOWN FLAG
events.text: A sickness flag hangs the wrong way up. Two factions are arguing over the meaning of a knot nobody has offered to untie.

choices.label: Set it right

outcome.text: You fix the flag. The argument moves to whether you used the blessed ladder, and will still be running at Lammas.

choices.label: Declare both sides wrong

outcome.text: You declare the flag cannot read itself. This is called wisdom by three people and heresy by one, and it is the one who writes letters.

events.title: THE PARDONER'S BUNDLE
events.text: A pardoner offers forgiveness among the combs and trinkets on his stall. He recommends buying it before the afternoon prices rise.

choices.label: Buy forgiveness (6g)

outcome.text: He forgives you for sins you had not planned yet. Efficient, if troubling. You keep the paper, which is the part that will matter.

memory.note: You hold a pardoner’s letter for sins not yet committed.

choices.label: Ask for a receipt

outcome.text: He flees at the word "receipt." The crowd learns a valuable theology of paperwork, and repeats the story at every fair for a decade.

events.title: THE HEIR'S FIRST WORD
events.text: A young child in your household offers an early word that sounds like “goat.” You are asked to judge whether this demonstrates genius or somebody else’s example.

choices.label: Call it genius

outcome.text: You declare the child prophetic. The family begins watching goats for omens.

choices.label: Blame your spouse

outcome.text: Your spouse blames you back with better evidence.

events.title: FATHER'S TALL TALE
events.text: {{father}} tells a story in which the enemy gets larger every time the bowl is refilled. {{mother}} remembers being present and is finding the new numbers difficult.

choices.label: Believe Father

outcome.text: Your father glows with pride and retells it as eight taxmen.

choices.label: Ask Your mother for truth

outcome.text: Your mother describes the goose victory in brutal detail. Your father studies the floor.

events.title: SLEEPING THROUGH SERMON
events.text: {{spouse}} nods off during the sermon and snores into a pause designed for moral reflection. The reflection spreads to your bench.

choices.label: Wake them gently

outcome.text: They wake, nod gravely, and pretend the snore was theological agreement.

choices.label: Let it happen

outcome.text: The priest takes it personally. The pew takes it loudly.

events.title: THE WRONG DOOR
events.text: A marker has mistaken your door for one under sickness watch. The apology is being delivered from a distance the mistake itself has made unnecessary.

choices.label: Scrub it off

outcome.text: You scrub until the door is cleaner than your soul.

choices.label: Use the privacy

outcome.text: No one visits for weeks. Peaceful, except for the screaming outside.

events.title: THE BELL ARGUMENT
events.text: The bell ringer asks what a sickness warning ought to sound like. Everyone wants a warning that is accurate and not intended for them.

choices.label: Choose hopeful

outcome.text: The bells ring bright over a frightened village. For a moment people breathe easier, and afterwards they remember who chose the sound of that year.

choices.label: Choose frightening

outcome.text: The bells terrify everyone except the sickness, which has poor manners. Three households leave Swineford rather than hear them again.

events.title: THE BACKWARDS BANNER
events.text: Your unit’s banner has been sewn backwards. The commander says the enemy must not be allowed to learn how literally the company can face the wrong way.

choices.label: Fix it before muster

outcome.text: You fix the banner and earn respect from everyone who can read cloth.

choices.label: Call it strategy

outcome.text: The captain loves it. Confusion, he says, is half of war and most of command.

events.title: COUNTING ARROWS
events.text: The quartermaster’s arrow count changes every time a bundle is opened. He proposes blessing the total rather than counting the shafts.

choices.label: Count them properly

outcome.text: You count thirty-seven arrows and one suspicious knitting needle.

choices.label: Pray over the bundle

outcome.text: The arrows remain thirty-seven. The needle seems holier.

events.title: THE COWARDLY DRUM
events.text: The war drum splits before the muster. The drummer gives it an honourable speech and asks whether a barrel might be promoted into the vacancy.

choices.label: Praise the drum

outcome.text: The men laugh, then cheer. Morale is a strange stew.

choices.label: Find a barrel

outcome.text: You beat a barrel into service. It sounds terrible, but so does war.

events.title: A VACANT BARONY
events.text: A border barony lacks a lord. The council wants coin, manners, and someone foolish enough to live near raiders.

choices.label: Buy the claim (90g)

outcome.text: The seal is yours. Your patent is entered in the royal register; your household now holds a barony.

choices.label: Wait for a better chance

outcome.text: You smile, bow, and keep your purse closed. The chance may come again, if death does not get bored first.

events.title: OATH DAY
events.text: Your tenants gather to swear loyalty. They look hungry, hopeful, and very aware of your boots.

choices.label: Promise fair rule

outcome.text: You promise justice first and coin second. The crowd cheers like people who have heard promises before, but want to believe.

choices.label: Demand proper dues

outcome.text: You remind them that loyalty has fees. The strong nod. The poor stare at the mud.

events.title: A FACE FROM SWINEFORD
events.text: An old neighbor asks for mercy after stealing grain from your storehouse.

choices.label: Forgive the theft

outcome.text: You send them home with grain enough for winter. Nobles call it weakness. Everyone else calls it dinner.

choices.label: Make an example

outcome.text: The stocks fill by sunset. Your barns remain full, and your halls grow quieter.

events.title: RAIDERS AT THE BORDER
events.text: Smoke rises from the edge of your lands. Your steward asks whether to muster riders or count losses.

choices.label: Ride out yourself

success.text: You drive the raiders off and return with a dented helm and a louder legend.

failure.text: The raid breaks your line. You survive, but the songs do not flatter your horse.

choices.label: Pay scouts and guards (20g)

outcome.text: Paid guards do paid work. The raiders find easier prey, and your villagers sleep.

events.title: TAX SEASON
events.text: The ledgers are thin. Your steward suggests squeezing the villages. He says squeezing with a smile helps.

choices.label: Keep taxes light

outcome.text: The treasury groans, but the people bless your name in every bakehouse.

choices.label: Fill the coffers

outcome.text: Coin pours in. So do complaints. You discover complaints cannot be minted.

events.title: A POWERFUL MATCH
events.text: A neighboring house offers marriage ties. The portrait is flattering. Suspiciously flattering.

choices.label: Accept the match

outcome.text: The wedding is grand, costly, and full of relatives counting your plates.

choices.label: Politely decline

outcome.text: You decline with such grace that only half the family vows revenge.

events.title: LESSONS FOR AN HEIR
events.text: A child in your household asks how to rule. A dangerous question from someone holding a wooden sword.

choices.label: Teach mercy

outcome.text: You teach that power is lent, not owned. The child nods, then pardons a biscuit thief.

choices.label: Teach strength

outcome.text: You teach that crowns are held by steady hands. The child immediately orders the spoon drawer inspected.

events.title: THE COURT POET
events.text: A poet offers to make you immortal in verse. The first draft rhymes "baron" with "barren."

choices.label: Fund better rhymes (12g)

outcome.text: The second draft flatters your jaw, your wisdom, and a battle you barely attended.

choices.label: Banish the poem

outcome.text: The poet leaves, loudly comparing you to damp porridge. Annoying, but accurate in meter.

events.title: ROYAL FAVOR
events.text: A royal messenger praises your household. Praise from above is rarely free.

choices.label: Send a lavish gift (35g)

outcome.text: The crown remembers your generosity, which is the polite word for payment.

choices.label: Send loyal words

outcome.text: Your letter is loyal, cheap, and only slightly damp from panic.

events.title: SICKNESS IN THE VILLAGES
events.text: A fever moves through your lands. The physician asks whether the poor are worth expensive herbs.

choices.label: Open the stores (30g)

outcome.text: Herbs, bread, and clean straw save more lives than any sermon. People remember.

choices.label: Seal the manor

outcome.text: Your household survives behind locked gates. Outside, the bells do not stop.

events.title: A CLAIM TO THE CROWN
events.text: Your documented claim reaches the council while the reigning monarch’s mandate falters. The genealogist recommends bringing witnesses rather than fresh ink.

choices.label: Press the claim (140g)

success.text: Banners rise. Rivals kneel. Somehow, impossibly, the crown rests on your head.

failure.text: The claim collapses under laughter and steel. You flee with fewer friends and lighter coffers.

choices.label: Keep the secret

outcome.text: You tuck the family tree away. Some branches are best left unclimbed.

events.title: FIRST DAY WITH THE CROWN
events.text: Everyone bows. Everyone wants something. The crown is heavier than it looked on other heads.

choices.label: Speak of peace

outcome.text: You promise peace, bread, and fewer public hangings. The hall applauds cautiously.

choices.label: Speak of obedience

outcome.text: You promise order. The hall applauds very quickly, which is almost the same as love.

events.title: THE EMPTY TREASURY
events.text: s=>`The royal treasury contains ${s.world.court?.treasury??0} gold, two moths, and a note blaming the previous ruler.`

choices.label: Seek gifts from wealthy households

outcome.text: Wealthy households contribute coin and grain to the royal appeal. The kingdom eats, and the donors keep very careful receipts.

choices.label: Raise royal taxes

outcome.text: The treasury fattens overnight. So does the list of people muttering near tavern doors.

events.title: REBELLION
events.text: A duke declares you unfit to rule. Rude, dangerous, and annoyingly well funded.

choices.label: Meet them in battle

success.text: The rebellion breaks. You return with torn banners and a kingdom that suddenly remembers its manners.

failure.text: Your army scatters. The council recognises a rival, removes your seal and sends you into exile.

choices.label: Offer pardon

outcome.text: You offer mercy with one hand and hold guards behind the door with the other. It works.

events.title: ROYAL PROGRESS
events.text: You ride through the kingdom so people may cheer, complain, or throw root vegetables from a patriotic distance.

choices.label: Hear every petition

outcome.text: Your ears ache, but your people feel seen. Even the beet-thrower bows.

choices.label: Wave from the carriage

outcome.text: The route is shorter, cleaner, and less informative. Royal wrists are delicate things.

events.title: THE HEIR QUESTION
events.text: Courtiers whisper about succession. They do this loudly enough to be helpful and insulting.

choices.label: Name an heir publicly

outcome.text: The court exhales. A named heir is a shield against chaos, and a target for everyone ambitious.

choices.label: Keep them guessing

outcome.text: Mystery has power. It also has daggers.

events.title: A GRAND FEAST
events.text: Foreign envoys arrive. The cook asks whether to serve modest dignity or edible showing off.

choices.label: Feast like legend (45g)

outcome.text: The tables groan, the envoys beam, and someone writes a ballad about the pudding.

choices.label: Serve simple fare

outcome.text: The meal is plain, honest, and described by envoys as "educational."

events.title: JUSTICE DAY
events.text: Two nobles argue over land. Both have witnesses. Both witnesses look purchased.

choices.label: Judge by evidence

outcome.text: You untangle lies until truth limps into view. The court hates how long fairness takes.

choices.label: Favor the richer house

outcome.text: The richer house wins, naturally. Justice wears a very expensive hat today.

events.title: SWINEFORD REMEMBERS
events.text: Your birth village sends a gift: a turnip wearing a tiny crown.

choices.label: Laugh and reward them

outcome.text: You laugh until the court dares to join in. Swineford receives a new well and unbearable pride.

choices.label: Ban the joke

outcome.text: The turnip is removed. Unfortunately, jokes grow better underground.

events.title: THE HOLY CROWN
events.text: A bishop suggests your rule needs divine polish. He has incense, hymns, and a very large invoice.

choices.label: Hold a sacred rite (35g)

outcome.text: The rite dazzles the realm. Even skeptics bow while checking where the smoke comes from.

choices.label: Rule without incense

outcome.text: You decline. The bishop looks wounded, which is a skill bishops practice.

events.title: A KNIFE IN THE CURTAIN
events.text: At midnight, a curtain sneezes. Curtains should not know how.

choices.label: Trust your guards

success.text: Your guards seize the assassin. Loyalty, it turns out, is cheaper than a funeral.

failure.text: The guards are late. The knife is not.

effects.death: Assassinated behind a curtain. A poor review for the guards.

choices.label: Sleep in armor

outcome.text: You survive the night and wake shaped like a soup pot.

events.title: YEARS UPON THE THRONE
events.text: You have ruled long enough that young courtiers think you were born wearing the crown.

choices.label: Celebrate the realm

outcome.text: Bells ring from coast to border. For one bright day, even your enemies pretend to enjoy you.

choices.label: Take the praise quietly

outcome.text: You accept the praise with a small nod. The crown has taught you the value of neck muscles.

events.title: THE WEARY CROWN
events.text: Your bones ache. Your heir is ready enough. The throne looks more like a chair every year.

choices.label: Abdicate with grace

outcome.text: You lay the crown down and live to hear people miss you. A rare royal victory.

choices.label: Cling to power

outcome.text: You grip the throne until your knuckles pale. The court smiles the way knives smile.

events.title: A LAW FOR COMMONERS
events.text: A clerk proposes a law protecting common folk from noble whims. Nobles call this the end of civilization.

choices.label: Sign the law

outcome.text: The common folk cheer. The nobles sulk. This is how you know the ink mattered.

choices.label: Shelve it forever

outcome.text: The law vanishes into a drawer deep enough to have weather.

events.title: WHAT WILL THEY SAY?
events.text: A chronicler asks how history should remember you. A dangerous thing, history.

choices.label: As a beloved ruler

outcome.text: The chronicler writes of mercy, bread, and a crown that remembered the mud.

choices.label: As a feared ruler

outcome.text: The chronicler writes carefully. Very carefully. Your enemies are described in the past tense.

choices.label: As truth allows

outcome.text: The chronicler sighs with relief and begins with the turnip fields.

events.title: THE BISHOP ADMIRES THY FALCON
events.text: The bishop stops mid-procession to admire your hunting falcon, and asks its breeding in a tone that is not entirely about birds.

choices.label: Give him the falcon

outcome.text: He is delighted and slightly embarrassed, and a bishop in that condition is worth a great deal. Your name reaches the diocese before you do.

choices.label: Fly her for him instead

outcome.text: She takes a heron in front of the whole procession. The bishop talks about it for years and never once offers to buy her.

choices.label: Name a price

outcome.text: He pays it without blinking, which tells you the price was too low. You have coin and he has a story about a grasping fellow from Swineford.

events.title: A HORSE WORTH TAKING
events.text: The muster clerk looks at your destrier, then at his roll, and informs you that a man with a warhorse serves mounted, at his own cost, for twice the term.

choices.label: Serve mounted and be seen doing it

outcome.text: You ride out at the head of the Swineford contingent, which is four men and a cart. It is absurd and it is remembered.

choices.label: Swear the horse is lame

outcome.text: You keep the horse and the clerk keeps a note. Both of you know the horse is sound and neither of you says so.

events.title: THEY HAVE HEARD ABOUT THE RELIC
events.text: Three pilgrims are at your gate before Prime, having walked from Ely on the strength of a rumour about what you keep in your house.

choices.label: Let them see it, and take nothing

outcome.text: They stay an hour and leave weeping. By Lammas there are thirty of them, and by Michaelmas the road past your door is a road.

choices.label: Ask a penny a head

outcome.text: They pay it. Word of the penny travels exactly as fast as word of the relic, and arrives in the same conversation.

choices.label: Send them on to the abbey

outcome.text: You point them up the road and shut the gate. They go, and they tell the abbey where they were sent from.

events.title: A MAN WHO KEEPS A LEDGER
events.text: Word has got round that you keep written accounts. The reeve arrives with a box of tallies, an apologetic expression, and no intention of leaving with the box.

choices.label: Do the parish accounts

outcome.text: Nine evenings of somebody else’s arithmetic. You find two errors in the parish’s favour and one very much not, and you report both.

choices.label: Do them for a fee

outcome.text: Four shillings and the work is done properly. The reeve pays and thereafter treats you as a tradesman rather than a neighbour.

choices.label: Do them, and improve them

outcome.text: The accounts balance beautifully and two of the entries are yours. It will hold until somebody else learns to read a tally.

events.title: A STONE OF THINE OWN
events.text: Your own millstone means your own flour, and half the lane has worked that out. They arrive with sacks and a hopeful manner.

choices.label: Grind for them, and take no toll

outcome.text: You grind for nine households and take nothing. The miller hears about it within the day and is not amused.

choices.label: Take a toll, honestly measured

outcome.text: A twentieth, measured in front of them. The mill takes a tenth and everybody knows it, so you are paid and nobody feels robbed.

choices.label: It is your stone

outcome.text: You shut the door on them. It is entirely your stone and they go back to the mill, past your house, every week, for years.

events.title: THE ONE WITH THE MASK
events.text: Sickness is in the row by the ford and you own the only beaked mask in the parish, which in everyone else’s eyes makes you the nearest thing Swineford has to a physician.

choices.label: Put it on and go in

outcome.text: The mask does nothing at all and the vinegar-soaked rag inside it may do a little. You bring four people through and take a cough that lasts till spring.

choices.label: Lend it to the herb-wife

outcome.text: She takes it without comment and uses it for nine years. You never get it back and never ask.

choices.label: Keep it, and keep indoors

outcome.text: You are well all season. The lane knows exactly what is hanging on your door and exactly who did not come.

events.title: A MAN WITH A SWORD IS ASKED
events.text: A carter is being beaten in the market by two men over a debt. You are wearing a sword, which the whole market has noticed, and which changes what standing still means.

choices.label: Draw it

outcome.text: They go. Nobody is cut and everybody saw the steel come out, and you will be answering for that at the tourn.

choices.label: Put a hand on the hilt and say nothing

outcome.text: They look at the hand, then at your face, and decide the debt can wait. Not one word is spoken and it works completely.

choices.label: Walk on

outcome.text: You walk on wearing a sword past a man being beaten. The market watches you do it and draws the obvious conclusion.

events.title: THE FORESTER LOOKS AT THY HOUND
events.text: The forester stops you on the coppice road and looks a long time at your hunting hound. Under forest law a dog that can run down a deer must be lawed: three claws off the forefoot.

choices.label: Have the dog lawed

outcome.text: It is done at the next swanimote with a mallet and a chisel. The dog lives, limps, and never runs anything down again.

choices.label: Pay the fine instead (12g)

outcome.text: Twelve shillings buys the dog its claws and buys the forester a new opinion of your purse. He will be back.

choices.label: Keep the dog out of the wood

outcome.text: The hound never goes near the coppice again and neither do you. It is a small life for a good dog and it keeps all four feet.

events.title: THE STONE’S SECOND APPOINTMENT
events.text: {{other}} remembers selling you the heated healing stone. It has, the seller explains, used up its medicinal warmth and requires a fresh fee.

choices.label: Decline to pay for the same fire twice

outcome.text: You keep your money and damage {{other}}’s confidence in repeat business.

choices.label: Show the stone to the waiting customers

outcome.text: You expose the sales trick, gain public standing and make {{other}} a rival who remembers your first purchase less fondly.

events.title: THE RUMOUR’S NEW PRICE
events.text: {{other}} returns to the silence you bought. Its new price is announced loudly enough to explain what the first bargain was worth.

choices.label: Refuse the second payment

outcome.text: You keep the coin and lose more of {{other}}’s trust. The rivalry now has a clear financial history.

choices.label: Admit the original payment publicly

outcome.text: You disclose your part in the bargain and improve your own reputation. {{other}} acquires a rival who is no longer protecting the same secret.

events.title: THE ANCESTOR’S OTHER DESCENDANTS
events.text: {{other}} has sold a similar pedigree to a second household. Your shared ancestor has suddenly become more productive than any surviving record suggests.

choices.label: Withdraw your claim before it becomes testimony

outcome.text: You lose some family standing and keep the disagreement from producing a fresh lie. {{other}} resents an ancestor being returned.

choices.label: Defend the invented descent under oath

outcome.text: You add a genuine perjury charge to a false family history. {{other}} is now a named witness to the origin of the pedigree.

charge.offence: Defending an invented pedigree under oath

events.title: THE SCOOP’S NEW WITNESS
events.text: {{other}} still remembers your challenge to the milling measure. Another household asks whether you will repeat it before witnesses this time.

choices.label: Repeat only what you actually observed

outcome.text: You gain Commons standing and lose {{other}}’s affection. The dispute has acquired an honest witness rather than a larger story.

choices.label: Decline to enlarge the old quarrel

outcome.text: You preserve your time and lose a little public standing. {{other}} regards your silence as a useful, temporary arrangement.

events.title: THE PEDLAR’S LESS ANGELIC STOCK
events.text: {{other}} returns after your argument over the feather, now selling ordinary quills. The prices still suggest a distinguished ancestry.

choices.label: Welcome the honest description

outcome.text: You improve the acquaintance and gain Church standing. {{other}} is allowed to make a living without making an angel.

choices.label: Retell the old scandal for the new customers

outcome.text: You gain a little charm and turn a possible reform into a continuing rivalry.

events.title: THE LETTER YOUR INFORMANT KEPT
events.text: {{other}} has kept a copy of the accusation you helped deliver against the plotters. A useful letter, the holder explains, should not be allowed to retire.

choices.label: Publicly stand by what you actually reported

outcome.text: Your reputation falls under renewed attention, but you refuse a new secret bargain. {{other}} loses leverage over your silence.

choices.label: Pay for the copy without trusting it is the only one (12g)

outcome.text: You pay twelve gold for one copy and gain no promise that the rest have vanished. {{other}} finds your caution less profitable than your secrecy.

events.title: THE MIRACLE’S ACCOUNT BOOK
events.text: {{other}} asks how the donations attracted by your supposed miracle were used. The account needs figures rather than another account of the miracle.

choices.label: Fund visible relief (8g)

outcome.text: You fund actual relief, improve food security and gain Church standing. {{other}} accepts an answer that somebody can eat.

choices.label: Claim that the giving itself was sufficient

outcome.text: You lose trust and family standing by refusing an account. The original child’s recovery has not supplied a receipt.

events.title: THE COLLECTOR WITHOUT A PRINCIPAL
events.text: {{other}} remembers the lunch collection you resisted. The miller’s big son is absent; the smaller collector asks whether the old quarrel must continue without him.

choices.label: Accept a truce without pretending to be friends

outcome.text: You improve trust with {{other}}. The rivalry is not erased by a speech, but the next meeting need not collect another grievance.

choices.label: Demand lunch in repayment

outcome.text: You deepen the rivalry and lose a little reputation. {{other}} recognises the collection method immediately.

events.title: THE FEE YOUR MOTHER REMEMBERS
events.text: {{other}} has recovered enough to discuss the money spent during the fever. The question is less about the sum than whether you will ever stop reminding her of it.

choices.label: Tell her the account is closed between you

outcome.text: You deepen trust without erasing any actual loan. {{other}} relaxes into a conversation that is finally about something else.

choices.label: List everything you sacrificed

outcome.text: You keep the list and damage the bond. {{other}} is alive to hear it, which makes the account no kinder.

events.title: THE GLOVE LEFT IN A POCKET
events.text: Roderick remembers losing the argument instead of the duel. {{other}} has brought no glove this time, but has rehearsed an opening sentence.

choices.label: Hear the grievance without staging another victory

outcome.text: You hear {{other}} out without inviting the neighbours to enjoy it. The grievance becomes easier to understand when nobody is performing it.

choices.label: Repeat the winning argument in public

outcome.text: You gain charm and deepen the rivalry. {{other}} now has a second date to attach to the same grievance.

events.title: THE DECEASED OBJECTS AGAIN
events.text: {{other}} has received a copy of the corrected claim. Your parent asks whether being officially alive now excuses the next assessment.

choices.label: Explain that the victory restored ordinary obligations

outcome.text: You improve trust by refusing to turn one honest correction into another convenient fiction.

choices.label: Help meet the assessment (6g)

outcome.text: You contribute toward the household assessment. {{other}} agrees that life is expensive but preferable to the earlier paperwork.

events.title: THE WITHDRAWN CLAIM’S STORAGE FEE
events.text: {{other}} remembers the nine gold you paid to withdraw the false death claim. A new fee is proposed for storing the withdrawn document.

choices.label: Contest the second demand openly

outcome.text: You gain local reputation and make {{other}} a rival. The document has become expensive to keep hidden.

choices.label: Pay four gold to avoid another day in court

outcome.text: You spend four gold on delay rather than on a lasting settlement. {{other}} remembers which part of the first demand worked.

events.title: THE WEIGHT OF THE SALT CELLAR
events.text: {{other}} has found the missing household savings you took. The salt was weighed, which makes your explanation about rats particularly unhelpful.

choices.label: Restore twelve gold to the household (12g)

outcome.text: You replace the money and regain some trust. {{other}} does not have to pretend the loss was imaginary.

choices.label: Keep denying a loss that has been counted

outcome.text: You lose more trust and deepen the family quarrel. The unchanged cellar has become a very patient witness.

events.title: THE GUARANTEE’S FIRST ANNIVERSARY
events.text: {{other}} remembers the debt you accepted after the false guarantee. The promised contribution has not materialised; the explanation has improved substantially.

choices.label: Set clear terms for future help

outcome.text: You improve your own judgement and lose some of {{other}}’s affection. Existing debt remains real until paid.

choices.label: Keep the family bond without making a new promise

outcome.text: You preserve trust while refusing another guarantee. {{other}} learns that affection need not include an empty signature line.

events.title: THE QUESTION NO LONGER ASKED
events.text: {{other}} has stopped asking about the goods you concealed. The silence is obedient in exactly the way you once demanded.

choices.label: Admit that threatening the witness was wrong

outcome.text: You regain some trust by acknowledging the threat. The old evidence and any charges are not wiped away by the apology.

choices.label: Praise the silence and demand it continue

outcome.text: You deepen the damage to trust. {{other}} learns another lesson about what you call loyalty.

events.title: THE SEAL LEFT A GOOD IMPRESSION
events.text: {{other}} has been asked about the advance obtained with the soap seal. The seal has dissolved; the impression on the agreement has not.

choices.label: Give an honest account of the forgery

outcome.text: You gain some reputation for candour without removing the existing charge. {{other}} trusts the admission more than the earlier plan.

choices.label: Invent another document to support the first

outcome.text: You add a second forgery charge. {{other}} now has a much more complicated account to remember.

charge.offence: Creating false evidence for the soap-seal advance

events.title: THE GOODS LEFT AFTER THE LIST
events.text: {{other}} returns to discuss a small item omitted when your marriage ended. Both of you have brought the old inventory and a newer caution.

choices.label: Give up the disputed household item

outcome.text: Your household loses four gold of wealth and trust with {{other}} improves. The former marriage does not resume because an argument ends.

choices.label: Insist the silence in the list means ownership

outcome.text: You preserve the goods and deepen the quarrel. {{other}} adds a useful annotation to the old inventory.

events.title: THE JOKE REACHES THE OTHER DOOR
events.text: {{other}} hears the public joke you made about the suspected visits repeated back at home. It has acquired a kinder ending for everyone except your spouse.

choices.label: Correct your own story publicly

outcome.text: You regain some trust by taking the embarrassment yourself. {{other}} hears a difference between an apology and another joke.

choices.label: Insist that being hurt proves there was something to hide

outcome.text: You deepen the loss of trust. {{other}} is given a fresh accusation in place of an answer.

events.title: THE FOURTH WEDDING CREDITOR
events.text: {{other}} asks for the ten gold you took from the wedding reserve. The three brokers have become much less impressive as excuses for the fourth demand.

choices.label: Restore the ten gold (10g)

outcome.text: You replace the household money and recover some trust. {{other}} removes one name from the list of people awaiting payment.

choices.label: Keep the money and call it your fee

outcome.text: The family quarrel deepens. {{other}} now regards your help as something to budget against.

events.title: THE SINGER FINDS THE RIGHT WINDOW
events.text: {{other}} remembers your quiet correction of the storeroom serenade and offers to help you avoid a public embarrassment of your own.

choices.label: Accept the advice before making a speech

outcome.text: You gain charm and deepen the friendship. The favour is useful precisely because the audience never sees it happen.

choices.label: Trust your own judgement this time

outcome.text: You keep the decision your own and lose only a little of {{other}}’s enthusiasm for rescuing you.

events.title: THE SHADE OF AN OLD QUARREL
events.text: {{other}}’s household still remembers your family’s opposition to the shadow rent. A minor boundary question has arrived wearing the larger feud.

choices.label: Pay for a witnessed boundary discussion (11g)

outcome.text: You pay for mediation and improve trust. The existing family feud remains a real problem rather than disappearing into the refreshments.

choices.label: Answer with the old accusation

outcome.text: You deepen the quarrel and lower public order. {{other}} supplies the family with a fresh version of the grievance.

events.title: THE PARDON’S HANDWRITING
events.text: {{other}} is asked who filled in the blank pardon you presented. The missing seal is no longer the most interesting absence in the account.

choices.label: Give a truthful account without claiming a pardon

outcome.text: You improve your reputation a little. The forgery charge remains, and {{other}} is spared a second invented story.

choices.label: Blame the supplier for words you wrote

outcome.text: You damage trust with {{other}} and gain a rival who can identify your handwriting.

events.title: THE PIE’S UNHAPPY OWNER
events.text: {{other}} has not forgotten that you delivered the suggested verdict as evidence. The next meeting contains no pie and several extremely polite threats.

choices.label: Have the threats witnessed

outcome.text: You gain public standing by refusing to let the old evidence become a private bargain. {{other}} loses further trust in your discretion.

choices.label: End the meeting without a new bargain

outcome.text: You keep your record clear and the rivalry intact. {{other}} is left with the refreshments and the unsaid part of the threat.

events.title: THE MONEY AFTER THE MARK
events.text: {{other}} sees the arm injured by the substitute punishment and asks whether you would recommend the arrangement to someone else.

choices.label: Refuse to recruit a second substitute

outcome.text: You gain reputation and keep the chronic pain that made the offer real. {{other}} finds your endorsement unexpectedly unavailable.

choices.label: Ask for practical support rather than another bargain

outcome.text: You gain a little health and a more honest bond. The disability remains; the account of what it cost is less easy to evade.

events.title: THE UNCLE’S SECOND JOURNEY
events.text: {{other}} asks whether you will carry another supposed coffin. This one has ventilation holes and a much stricter request not to shake it.

choices.label: Refuse the second cargo

outcome.text: You keep clear of a new smuggling attempt and lose some of {{other}}’s favour. Your earlier record remains whatever it actually was.

choices.label: Require the cargo to be declared openly

outcome.text: You gain Crown standing by insisting on an honest declaration. {{other}} decides the route may be less profitable with you on it.

events.title: THE REHEARSAL’S NEXT AUDIENCE
events.text: {{other}}’s household remembers the rehearsed accusation you exposed. A new invitation has arrived, careful to contain no words that can easily be quoted.

choices.label: Refuse the invitation without inventing a threat

outcome.text: You preserve your distance and lose further affection. The household feud remains recorded rather than becoming a new conspiracy by assumption.

choices.label: Attend with witnesses of your own

outcome.text: You gain public standing through an openly witnessed meeting. {{other}} finds you difficult to invite into confidence.

events.title: THE BARRELS COME BACK FULL OF AIR
events.text: {{other}} returns with complaints about the false-measure barrels you signed. The workmanship has held up better than the description.

choices.label: Pay toward a correction (10g)

outcome.text: You spend ten gold and improve your working standing a little. The original fraud charge remains for the court.

choices.label: Defend the false capacity again

outcome.text: You deepen the loss of trust and professional standing. {{other}} has a barrel available for the demonstration.

events.title: THE CUSTOMER WHO KEPT THE RECALL
events.text: {{other}} remembers that you recalled the rejected goods at your own expense. A new customer asks whether your mark can be trusted.

choices.label: Ask for a plain account of the correction

outcome.text: You gain work performance and trust through the recommendation. The old mistake is included rather than hidden.

choices.label: Give the repairers their share of the credit

outcome.text: Your professional standing improves more broadly. {{other}} likes an account that makes room for the people who did the work.

events.title: THE BARGE’S VERY DRY DEBT
events.text: {{other}} brings the accounts of the venture you borrowed to fund. Whatever happened to the goods, the interest has remained perfectly sheltered.

choices.label: Review the real accounts before borrowing again

outcome.text: You gain work experience and a more cautious bond. No existing debt is cleared by understanding it better.

choices.label: Borrow another twelve gold against hoped-for returns

outcome.text: You add a twelve-gold obligation without creating an imaginary cargo. {{other}} finds the confidence encouraging.

events.title: THE PARTNER HAS FOUND A VOICE
events.text: {{other}} remembers your guarantee and proposes another. The earlier silence was evidently intended to leave room for this request.

choices.label: Refuse another guarantee while the first remains

outcome.text: You lose some favour and improve your judgement. Existing debt is not a qualification for acquiring more.

choices.label: Demand a full account before discussing terms

outcome.text: You gain work experience and a more exacting relationship. {{other}} has to turn the conversation from trust to figures.

events.title: THE WORD RETURNED TO THE CASE
events.text: {{other}}’s omitted “not” has been found in a retained draft. A single word now occupies most of the hearing.

choices.label: Provide the accurate draft

outcome.text: You gain a little reputation for candour and lose {{other}}’s trust. The original alteration remains a real charge.

choices.label: Try to destroy the retained draft

outcome.text: You add an evidence-destruction charge. The case now has two carefully named acts instead of one missing word.

charge.offence: Destroying evidence of a deliberately altered agreement

events.title: THE PATIENT WHO READ THE DATE
events.text: {{other}} has compared the certificate you sold with the day of the actual visit. Your former employment is being discussed in the past tense for a very definite reason.

choices.label: Acknowledge the false certificate

outcome.text: You gain some reputation for honesty without regaining the post or removing the charge. {{other}} finally receives an accurate statement.

choices.label: Insist that the date was clinically unimportant

outcome.text: You damage trust further. {{other}} regards the calendar as one of the few instruments used correctly in the case.

events.title: THE PATRON’S SAFER VERSE
events.text: {{other}} asks for another performance after you refused the accusation of treason. This time the proposed enemy is a badly maintained bridge.

choices.label: Accept a subject that cannot be imprisoned

outcome.text: You improve work performance and rebuild trust. The bridge is allowed no right of reply, but neither is it made into a person.

choices.label: Agree only to an honest account of the repair

outcome.text: You gain professional experience by writing within the facts. {{other}} learns that a commission can come with a conscience.

events.title: THE MEN WHO ARE ACTUALLY HERE
events.text: {{other}} brings the next muster list with the duplicate names crossed out. There are fewer men and far fewer explanations.

choices.label: Support the accurate muster

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing and rebuild trust. The smaller force is at least large enough to match its own account.

choices.label: Read out the earlier list for the company

outcome.text: You gain charm and deepen the rivalry. {{other}} discovers that correction has not bought discretion.

events.title: THE RING KEPT BY THE OTHER HOUSE
events.text: {{other}}’s household has kept the account of your accusation over the falcon. The old supper now appears whenever the families disagree about anything edible.

choices.label: Admit your false accusation

outcome.text: You improve trust at the cost of family standing. The recorded feud remains until the households actually find a way to repair it.

choices.label: Repeat the accusation for the new generation

outcome.text: You deepen the feud and lose public standing. {{other}} supplies another accurate account of what you have chosen to repeat.

events.title: THE RIVER AT THE HEARING
events.text: {{other}} has brought a corrected map after you demanded a survey. The river has resumed its inconvenient natural course.

choices.label: Accept the corrected evidence without a victory speech

outcome.text: You improve trust and gain Crown standing. {{other}} keeps enough dignity to continue using the accurate map.
