choices.label: Make a public account of the earlier drawing

outcome.text: You gain reputation and damage the relationship. The corrected river now has to carry the old humiliation as well.

events.title: THE COIN RETURNS BY WEIGHT
events.text: {{other}} brings back the light coin issued under your order. Traders have begun weighing your face instead of trusting it.

choices.label: Fund a public correction (18g)

outcome.text: You spend personal gold to improve public order and family standing. The correction buys some goodwill; the charge over the dishonest issue remains on the roll.

choices.label: Blame the people weighing the coins

outcome.text: Public order falls further and {{other}} loses trust. The silver continues to be absent without asking anyone’s permission.

events.title: THE MORNING YOU REFUSED TO SAVE
events.text: {{other}} remembers your refusal to approve a condemnation before evidence. Another petition now arrives with witnesses rather than a convenient conclusion.

choices.label: Hear the better petition

outcome.text: You improve public order and rebuild trust. The earlier refusal has produced something more useful than an obedient morning.

choices.label: Require an ordinary hearing rather than a private favour

outcome.text: You gain Crown standing by keeping the decision out of a personal bargain. {{other}} accepts the limits reluctantly.

events.title: THE SAINT’S REVISED INVENTORY
events.text: {{other}} has removed the claim about the smaller skull. The new label says “object of uncertain history,” which is both less profitable and more defensible.

choices.label: Support the honest revision

outcome.text: You improve Church standing and trust with {{other}}. The object is allowed to remain interesting without another childhood.

choices.label: Keep telling the original joke

outcome.text: You gain a little charm and lose the chance to reward correction. {{other}} finds honesty a poor protection against your memory.

events.title: THE OVEN’S LESS CONVINCING WITNESS
events.text: {{other}} sees the lasting pain left by the burning ordeal. The oven has produced bread since, but no new evidence about your innocence.

choices.label: Explain publicly what the ordeal actually proved

outcome.text: You gain reputation by refusing to recommend the injury. The chronic pain remains a real cost rather than becoming proof of guilt.

choices.label: Accept practical help and rest

outcome.text: You recover some health and improve trust. Help eases the day without curing the disability.

events.title: THE SHORTER DONOR LIST
events.text: {{other}} has changed the distribution so food is served while names are read. Several donors object to not being heard over the grateful eating.

choices.label: Support the practical arrangement

outcome.text: You gain Church standing and deepen trust. The names still exist; they no longer have to be hungry first.

choices.label: Demand the old ceremony for the important donors

outcome.text: You lose public reputation and {{other}}’s trust by making the meal wait for precedence again.

events.title: THE FAVOUR WITH BOTH HANDS FREE
events.text: {{other}} remembers the promise you made while the wound was dressed. A practical household chore now needs the help you said you would give.

choices.label: Give the promised afternoon

outcome.text: You spend a little strength and deepen a real friendship. The favour is repaid through work, without claiming the wound never happened.

choices.label: Say the promise belonged to a frightening day

outcome.text: You lose trust with {{other}}. The knot has come untied more easily than the memory.

events.title: THE PEG KEPT ON THE BENCH
events.text: {{other}} has kept the peg you fitted before climbing the scaffold. Another worker asks why the smallest part of the job is being shown so proudly.

choices.label: Explain the repair without making the blessing a joke

outcome.text: You gain craft experience and trust. {{other}} is able to repeat the lesson without defending the earlier mistake.

choices.label: Make the explanation mostly about your own good sense

outcome.text: You gain charm and lose a little affection. The peg is patient enough to remain the useful part of the story.

events.title: THE GUARANTEE’S NEW WORDING
events.text: {{other}} returns with a tonic guarantee rewritten after your public objection. This version promises only that the bottle contains tonic.

choices.label: Welcome the smaller, honest promise

outcome.text: You improve trust and gain a little public standing. {{other}} has discovered a claim that fits inside the bottle.

choices.label: Keep clear of the seller without renewing the argument

outcome.text: You preserve your judgement and lose no money. {{other}} accepts that changed wording need not buy a customer.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE’S SECOND MESSENGER
events.text: {{other}} brings a new demand connected with the fortune you borrowed to pursue. The estate is still unnamed; its expenses have become very well documented.

choices.label: Refuse to finance the claim further

outcome.text: You gain judgement and lose {{other}}’s favour. The existing loans remain, but no new obligation is invented on their behalf.

choices.label: Put the demands before the clerk

outcome.text: You gain public standing and make {{other}} a rival. The supposed fortune has finally produced an identifiable person for the inquiry.

events.title: THE DEVIL REMEMBERS A FAIR WAGE
events.text: {{other}} remembers that you helped pay the pageant performer. A later neighbourhood task needs someone trusted to account for everyone’s work.

choices.label: Help keep the accounts fairly

outcome.text: You gain experience and public standing through a reputation based on an actual payment. {{other}} trusts you with the list.

choices.label: Decline the responsibility without insulting the work

outcome.text: You keep the evening free and preserve the acquaintance. The earlier kindness remains completed rather than becoming permanent employment.

events.title: THE STONE WHERE YOU PUT IT
events.text: {{other}} wants your help identifying a boundary mark. The stone restored before witnesses is still there, inconveniently available for everybody to inspect.

choices.label: Stand by the witnessed position

outcome.text: You improve family standing and trust. {{other}} is reminded that a useful agreement can survive without being rewritten.

choices.label: Keep out of the new argument

outcome.text: You preserve your time and lose some trust. The stone remains a better witness than the people avoiding it.

events.title: THE THING YOU BOUGHT BACK
events.text: {{other}} returns a small keepsake to your hand after you saved the household goods. This one, the explanation goes, should not need rescuing twice.

choices.label: Keep it without turning the gift into a debt

outcome.text: You deepen the family bond. The object carries no new price. {{other}} waits until you understand that part.

choices.label: Remind the giver what the rescue cost

outcome.text: You damage trust by making the gift another entry in the debt account. The actual loans are unchanged.

events.title: THE COUNCILLOR’S CREATIVE ACCOUNTS
events.text: function scandalText(s){const q=currentCourtScandal(s);if(!q)return"This incident has already received a decision. No second reward or punishment is due.";const p=s.world.characters[q.actorId],traits=p?.personalityTraits??[];const detail=q.office==="marshal"?"The paid guards turn out to be hunting dogs. They obey the command to sit rather better than the command to hold a bridge.":q.office==="religious_adviser"?"The new vestment needs two servants to carry it. Its owner describes the weight as an instrument of humility.":q.office==="chancellor"?"A private feast has consumed the public money. The councillor\u2019s cousins are still too full to help explain it.":"The missing silver has become a pair of decorative horses. Neither horse has volunteered to repay the treasury.";const manner=traits.includes("cunning")?"The explanation changes whenever a different councillor enters.":traits.includes("cruel")?"The official recommends questioning the servants first.":traits.includes("ambitious")?"The official proposes promotion as the best way to avoid this sort of distraction.":"The official arrives with an explanation and a household ally.";return`${p?.name??"The recorded official"}${p&&!p.alive?" (now deceased)":""}, ${q.office.replaceAll("_"," ")}, diverted ${q.amount} treasury gold. ${detail} ${manner} This decision concerns this incident alone.`}

choices.label: Demand a public investigation

outcome.text: Half the missing gold returns; the official does not return to the chair. Their household departs slowly enough for every doorway to hear what a loyal servant has been lost.

choices.label: Cover up the accounts

outcome.text: The official thanks you with both hands clamped round the seal. Outside the chamber, somebody is already explaining how generous you have been with other people’s money.

choices.label: Blame the treasurer

outcome.text: The innocent treasurer leaves without the seal. The real culprit thanks you a little too warmly for anybody to miss it.

choices.label: Dismiss the official quietly

outcome.text: The official asks whether a smaller chair might be available. You take back the seal; they take the insult and all the money they have not already spent.

events.title: THE CONTESTED SEAL
events.text: s=>{const q=s.world.court?.petition;return q&&!q.resolved?`Your request for the ${q.office.replaceAll("_"," ")}\u2019s seal is before the ruler. ${(0,import_courtPolitics.petitionProspects)(s,"merit").detail} Appointment depends on the council\u2019s decision.`:"The court has already recorded this petition."}

choices.label: Present your learning and service

outcome.text: The ruler considers your service against the vacancy, incumbent and rival candidates. The court record gives the decision.

choices.label: Ask your patron to speak for you

outcome.text: Your patron addresses the council. Their support helps; the incumbent still has a case to answer.

choices.label: Offer further service before a new petition

outcome.text: The ruler records a condition of further professional service. You receive a target rather than a seal.

choices.label: Withdraw the request

outcome.text: The request is withdrawn. The existing officeholder remains responsible.

events.title: THE OPPOSING HOUSEHOLDS
events.text: s=>{const q=(0,import_courtPolitics.oppositionAudienceCoalition)(s);return`${s.world.characters[q?.leaderId??""]?.name??"An opposing household"} brings a coalition before the council${q?.claimantId?` backing ${s.world.characters[q.claimantId]?.name}'s claim`:""}. Their strength is ${q?.strength??0}. They have withheld cooperation and demand an answer.${s.world.court?.crisis&&s.world.court.crisis.responseYear===void 0&&s.world.court?.crisis?.leaderId===q?.leaderId?" Your reign is in crisis. After your response, you may lose the crown next year if legitimacy stays below 15, public order below 25 and coalition strength at least 40. A settlement reduces strength by 20; a hearing by 8; dismissal adds 12.":""}`}

choices.label: Fund a negotiated settlement (15 treasury)

outcome.text: A recorded settlement reduces the coalition’s strength. Rival claims remain in the family record.

choices.label: Hear the households’ grievances

outcome.text: The hearing earns some respect and eases opposition while leaving the dispute open.

choices.label: Assert royal authority and dismiss them

outcome.text: The rejected petition becomes a rallying point. The coalition gains strength and public order falls.

events.title: THE DYER’S BLUE DEBT
events.text: {{client}} offers a winter’s cloth on credit. The blue dye washes out in rain. {{rival}} has already promised to sell it as royal indigo.

choices.label: Test the dye before signing

outcome.text: You test and mark the cloth honestly. The blue remains in the water rather than the warranty; the buyers pay for what you can defend.

choices.label: Sell it before the weather turns

outcome.text: You collect the fees and make a powerful enemy of the first damp customer. The retained sample is a very portable accusation.

choices.label: Pay a dyer to fix the cloth

outcome.text: Your hired dyer corrects the cloth before delivery. The colour stays where it belongs, which is a novel basis for a trading concern.

events.title: THE DYER’S BLUE DEBT · THE RECKONING
events.text: The first rain has arrived. Your buyers bring their sleeves to the counting house as evidence.

choices.label: Defend the cloth contract

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the dyer’s blue debt. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Refund the disputed dye charges (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the dyer’s blue debt. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE RIVAL’S LAST BALE
events.text: {{rival}} claims that {{client}}’s wool bears a stolen mark. The guild may seize the entire consignment, including your stake.

choices.label: Call the shepherd as witness

outcome.text: The shepherd identifies the flock and the mark. The rival’s claim collapses under the testimony of a man less impressively dressed.

choices.label: Buy the rival’s silence

outcome.text: You buy silence and keep the stock. Your rival keeps enough evidence to make the silence expensive to maintain.

choices.label: Hire a clerk to trace the sales

outcome.text: Your clerk traces the bales through every sale. The title is recorded before anyone can add another ingenious owner.

events.title: THE RIVAL’S LAST BALE · THE RECKONING
events.text: The guild opens the bales before both households. Inside one lies a very indignant living lamb.

choices.label: Present the wool title

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the rival’s last bale. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Settle the wool claim openly (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the rival’s last bale. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE FUNERAL BELL WARRANTY
events.text: {{client}} orders a bell guaranteed to outlive the abbot. The mould is cracked. {{rival}} offers a coat of paint and a quiet blessing.

choices.label: Recast the faulty bell

outcome.text: The recast bell rings soundly. The abbot asks about the warranty; you point out that the bell has already survived his longest speech.

choices.label: Conceal the crack beneath the inscription

outcome.text: The bell rings badly beneath its handsome inscription. You keep the fee and acquire a customer who can demonstrate the defect to the whole parish.

choices.label: Hire an apprentice for a second casting

outcome.text: The apprentice helps cast a sound bell and stays in your service. The wardens grudgingly approve work whose second pair of hands has been paid.

events.title: THE FUNERAL BELL WARRANTY · THE RECKONING
events.text: The bell is raised above the churchyard. Your maker’s mark sits where the whole parish can read it.

choices.label: Answer for the bell’s casting

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the funeral bell warranty. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Compensate the parish for the bell (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the funeral bell warranty. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE WIDOW’S WORKSHOP
events.text: {{client}} keeps a workshop after the master’s burial. {{rival}} petitions the guild to confiscate the tools before the candles burn down.

choices.label: Defend the household’s charter

outcome.text: The charter protects the workshop. The rival has to find a living master to rob of commissions, an irritating restriction on enterprise.

choices.label: Take the disputed commissions yourself

outcome.text: You take the contracts. The widow keeps the charter and an exact account of the kindness your competitors can expect.

choices.label: Pay a clerk to establish the succession

outcome.text: Your clerk records the succession and takes paid work with you. The tools stay where their owner can use them.

events.title: THE WIDOW’S WORKSHOP · THE RECKONING
events.text: The guild court hears whether a dead master’s tools must become a living rival’s property.

choices.label: Submit to the workshop hearing

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the widow’s workshop. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Restore the disputed workshop fees (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the widow’s workshop. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE PHYSICIAN’S GREAT SUCCESS
events.text: {{client}} asks you to organise care for a household. {{rival}} advertises expensive bloodletting without first asking who is ill. Your own record must distinguish actual symptoms from preventive advice.

choices.label: Select the difficult cases

outcome.text: You record the actual needs and arrange care. Your practice earns confidence without having to declare healthy people dramatically cured.

choices.label: Accept every patient and every fee

outcome.text: You take too many fees and spread your care too thinly. A complaint arrives with a much more reliable record of your promises.

choices.label: Hire a medical apprentice

outcome.text: Your paid assistant takes routine work under supervision. Care is recorded for review; nobody is promised a recovery merely because help has arrived.

events.title: THE PHYSICIAN’S GREAT SUCCESS · THE RECKONING
events.text: Three new patients arrive with identical complaints and contradictory instructions from the same cousin.

choices.label: Present your treatment record

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the physician’s great success. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Pay the patients and correct the record (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the physician’s great success. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE WELL OF SAINT ITCH
events.text: Fever follows the water sold by {{client}} as a saint’s blessing. {{rival}} proposes charging double for blessed leeches.

choices.label: Inspect the well and separate the sick

outcome.text: You document the water risk and arrange safer care. The well keeper is asked to explain why a blessing needs to stand downhill from a privy.

choices.label: Sell the fashionable treatment

outcome.text: You collect the fees. Harmful treatment leaves an actual complaint wherever illness made the treatment more than an expensive performance.

choices.label: Pay an assistant to boil cloth and water

outcome.text: Your paid assistant supplies clean cloth and safer water. Fever pressure falls; ongoing patients remain under care rather than being cured by the account.

events.title: THE WELL OF SAINT ITCH · THE RECKONING
events.text: The parish asks why the blessed well stands downhill from the privy. The well keeper invokes mystery.

choices.label: Give evidence about the fever well

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the well of saint itch. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Refund the fever treatment and publish the evidence (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the well of saint itch. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE TITHE OF THE DEAD
events.text: {{client}} discovers that the abbey charges burial tithe on bones washed out of last year’s graves. {{rival}} calls this recurring revenue.

choices.label: Seek restitution for the households

outcome.text: The burial roll is corrected. One tanner ceases to be the abbey’s most reliable repeat customer.

choices.label: Defend the abbey’s profitable custom

outcome.text: The collectors keep their silver and the households keep their anger. Your improved connection with the former is noted carefully by the latter.

choices.label: Pay a clerk to reconcile the burial roll

outcome.text: Your clerk reconciles the burial entries and stays in paid service. The dead are allowed to stop financing their own paperwork.

events.title: THE TITHE OF THE DEAD · THE RECKONING
events.text: The archdeacon summons you to explain why one parish has buried the same tanner five times.

choices.label: Answer for the burial tithe

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the tithe of the dead. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Repay the duplicate burial fees (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the tithe of the dead. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE SAINT’S HORSE TOOTH
events.text: {{client}} seeks a ruling on the priory’s newest relic. {{rival}} has already sold indulgences for venerating what looks remarkably like a horse’s tooth.

choices.label: Submit the relic to an honest inquiry

outcome.text: The inquiry rejects the horse tooth’s saintly pedigree. The stable boy supplies the most useful evidence without once consulting Latin.

choices.label: Protect the priory’s profitable reputation

outcome.text: The display remains profitable. The stable boy recognises the tooth, and your rival recognises what that knowledge is worth.

choices.label: Hire a scholar to examine its provenance

outcome.text: The hired scholar establishes the tooth’s provenance and joins your service. The horse loses a canonisation; the record gains a species.

events.title: THE SAINT’S HORSE TOOTH · THE RECKONING
events.text: The bishop requests the relic, its history and an explanation for the stable boy’s recognition of it.

choices.label: Report to the relic inquiry

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the saint’s horse tooth. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Compensate the petitioners at the relic hearing (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the saint’s horse tooth. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE COMPANY AT THE BROKEN BRIDGE
events.text: {{client}} brings orders to cross a broken bridge before dawn. {{rival}} proposes sending the levy first to test its strength.

choices.label: Find a ford and protect the levy

outcome.text: The company uses the ford and avoids the broken bridge. You earn command credit for a route with fewer opportunities to become a memorial.

choices.label: Force the crossing before the enemy arrives

outcome.text: The crossing is forced and the operation harms the client entrusted to your command. You collect the fee; your surviving witnesses keep their account.

choices.label: Pay engineers to shore the bridge

outcome.text: Your paid engineer shores the bridge and remains with the company. The convoy crosses something more substantial than confidence.

events.title: THE COMPANY AT THE BROKEN BRIDGE · THE RECKONING
events.text: The supply train arrives as enemy scouts appear on the far bank. The company waits for your command.

choices.label: Accept responsibility for the crossing

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the company at the broken bridge. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Pay restitution and revise the crossing report (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the company at the broken bridge. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE CAPTIVES’ EMPTY PURSES
events.text: {{client}} brings three captured scouts. {{rival}} insists they are noblemen in unusually convincing poverty.

choices.label: Exchange them for your missing soldiers

outcome.text: The exchange is recorded and your service recognised. The clerk is asked to count returned people rather than the social importance of their boots.

choices.label: Extort a ransom from their families

outcome.text: The ransom brings profit and a feud between the households concerned. Your rival keeps the demand, complete with your excellent signature.

choices.label: Hire a clerk to verify their names

outcome.text: Your hired clerk verifies the names and records the exchange. The captives lose their imaginary nobility before it can be priced.

events.title: THE CAPTIVES’ EMPTY PURSES · THE RECKONING
events.text: A messenger offers peace on the road if the prisoners return alive. Your soldiers recognise one missing man’s belt.

choices.label: Answer for the prisoners’ exchange

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the captives’ empty purses. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Return the disputed ransom (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the captives’ empty purses. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE CHANCELLOR’S SALTED CAMEL
events.text: {{client}} sends a draft levy taxing every salt camel. The realm has no camels. {{rival}} recommends retaining the revenue estimate.

choices.label: Rewrite the levy around actual trade

outcome.text: The levy is corrected around real trade. The treasury benefits and the council reluctantly admits that a camel is a poor source of local revenue.

choices.label: Sell exemptions before anyone notices

outcome.text: You take exemption fees and leave an account your rival can read. The treasury has less silver and an exceptionally well-documented camel.

choices.label: Hire a clerk to survey the ports

outcome.text: Your hired clerk surveys the ports and stays in service. The decree acquires actual cargoes, which are less picturesque and considerably more taxable.

events.title: THE CHANCELLOR’S SALTED CAMEL · THE RECKONING
events.text: The council demands the promised revenue. The treasurer presents a drawing of a camel in place of payment.

choices.label: Defend your salt-levy advice

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the chancellor’s salted camel. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Repay the exemption fees before the council (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the chancellor’s salted camel. The record includes the correction.

events.title: THE DEAD FALCONER’S WAGES
events.text: {{client}} pays a falconer dead these nine years. {{rival}} claims the hawks remain loyal enough to justify his wages.

choices.label: Expose the accounts to the council

outcome.text: The false wages are recovered into the treasury. The hawks decline to testify about the last nine years of their employer’s work.

choices.label: Sell your silence to the beneficiary

outcome.text: You take hush money. Your rival keeps the burial entry beside the wage account, two documents that have finally found someone alive to blame.

choices.label: Hire an auditor to follow the payments

outcome.text: The paid auditor follows the payments and joins your service. The treasury recovers funds; the glove on its cushion is excused further duty.

events.title: THE DEAD FALCONER’S WAGES · THE RECKONING
events.text: The council calls for the falconer. Someone sends a glove on a cushion. The accounts are rather more talkative.

choices.label: Submit the falconer audit

outcome.text: Your account enters the record: the dead falconer’s wages. The recorded agreement determines who pays and who is believed.

choices.label: Return the hush money and publish the audit (6g)

outcome.text: You pay six gold in restitution over the dead falconer’s wages. The record includes the correction.

events.title: ROTATE THE STRIPS
events.text: {{client}} brings a thin harvest from exhausted strips. {{rival}} has offered a new rotation without testing the soil.

choices.label: Test a small strip first

outcome.text: You mark a trial strip and record the soil before committing seed.

choices.label: Replant the whole field now

outcome.text: The whole strip is planted under your new plan; the harvest will test its ambition.

choices.label: Plan around the tenants’ observations

outcome.text: The tenants compare their observations with yours before the rotation is agreed.

events.title: NEGOTIATE A TENANCY
events.text: {{client}} needs a rent agreement that survives a poor harvest. The landlord wants a fixed payment even if the seed fails.

choices.label: Bring the recorded harvest

outcome.text: The harvest tally becomes the basis of your proposed rent.

choices.label: Demand a lower rent outright

outcome.text: Your demand for a lower rent puts the landlord’s agent on the defensive.

choices.label: Negotiate through a trusted neighbour

outcome.text: The neighbour brings both parties’ accounts to the negotiation.

events.title: INSPECT THE LIVESTOCK
events.text: {{client}} brings news of coughing livestock. No one has yet established whether the illness has spread beyond one stall.

choices.label: Inspect and isolate the sick animals

outcome.text: You examine the coughing animals separately and record what you find.

choices.label: Return the herd to work quickly

outcome.text: The owner is asked to return the herd to work before every uncertainty is settled.

choices.label: Ask a herder to review the symptoms

outcome.text: A second herder compares the animals’ signs with your notes.

events.title: ACCEPT A COMMISSION
events.text: {{client}} orders hinges before a funeral date has been agreed. The metal, dimensions and delivery promise are yours to settle.

choices.label: Measure and test before delivery

outcome.text: The customer receives a delivery plan with measured dimensions and a test piece.

choices.label: Promise a quick, expensive delivery

outcome.text: You offer an earlier delivery for a larger fee, accepting a smaller margin for error.

choices.label: Share the work with an apprentice

outcome.text: The apprentice receives a defined part of the commission under your supervision.

events.title: TEACH AN APPRENTICE
events.text: {{client}} asks you to train a workshop apprentice. The learner needs supervision, wages and a piece suited to their ability.

choices.label: Teach a supervised trial piece

outcome.text: The learner starts a trial piece with your hand close enough to stop an error.

choices.label: Set a difficult independent job

outcome.text: You give the learner an independent job that will test their present limits.

choices.label: Pay for a second master’s advice

outcome.text: The second master is paid to inspect the learner’s work alongside yours.

events.title: CHALLENGE THE GUILD
events.text: {{client}} disputes a guild assay. {{rival}} wants the hearing held over the inspecting master’s private wine.

choices.label: Submit a witnessed assay

outcome.text: A witnessed assay enters the guild record before the hearing.

choices.label: Challenge the guild officers publicly

outcome.text: You challenge the officers in public, making their pride part of the dispute.

choices.label: Seek support from a respected master

outcome.text: A respected master agrees to examine the claim before supporting your petition.

events.title: NEGOTIATE A GRAIN DEAL
events.text: {{client}} offers a grain shipment with a disputed measure. Price, quality and the partner’s share must be agreed before loading.

choices.label: Negotiate price against honest measures

outcome.text: The buyer and seller compare the grain against a witnessed measure.

choices.label: Press for a high margin and rapid shipment

outcome.text: You press for a higher margin and accept the risks of a hurried shipment.

choices.label: Share the shipment with a trading partner

outcome.text: The partner’s cargo and share are written into the shipment agreement.

events.title: SETTLE THE BRIDGE TOLL
events.text: {{client}} has a cart held at a bridge charging for six wheels. There are two on the cart, and armed men beside the toll board.

choices.label: Check the toll charter and escort

outcome.text: The keeper receives the toll charter and the convoy’s actual wheel count.

choices.label: Run the disputed crossing at speed

outcome.text: Your cart approaches the crossing quickly enough to limit time for negotiation.

choices.label: Negotiate a shared convoy

outcome.text: The convoy partners present a joint toll offer with a shared escort.

events.title: CONTEST A RIVAL’S CLAIM
events.text: {{rival}} claims the mark on {{client}}’s wool. The shepherd remembers the shearing and expects someone to ask.

choices.label: Present witnesses and the wool marks

outcome.text: The shepherd and wool marks enter the disputed sale’s record.

choices.label: Undercut the rival’s price

outcome.text: Your lower offer challenges the rival’s custom as well as their claim.

choices.label: Offer a witnessed settlement

outcome.text: Both counting houses receive a proposed settlement in writing.

events.title: DELIVER A SERMON
events.text: {{client}} asks for a sermon after counterfeit relics divide the parish. Their neighbours disagree about who should be named.

choices.label: Address the parish’s actual distress

outcome.text: The sermon begins with the parish’s needs and the evidence about the relics.

choices.label: Condemn the offenders by name

outcome.text: Your sermon names the suspected offenders before the whole congregation.

choices.label: Ask the parish elder to help reconcile them

outcome.text: The parish elder helps frame a sermon that leaves room for restitution.

events.title: MEDIATE THE TITHE DISPUTE
events.text: {{client}} disputes another household’s goose tithe. The old custom is unclear and the archdeacon dislikes an empty purse.

choices.label: Hear both households openly

outcome.text: Both households give their account of the goose tithe in the same hearing.

choices.label: Back the more influential household

outcome.text: Your support for the stronger household makes their influence part of the settlement.

choices.label: Seek a private settlement with the elder

outcome.text: The elder carries a private proposal between the disputing households.

events.title: SEEK PARISH RESPONSIBILITY
events.text: {{client}} can bring your parish work before the archdeacon. {{rival}} has already requested the same responsibility.

choices.label: Submit the parish work record

outcome.text: The archdeacon receives an account of the parish work you actually completed.

choices.label: Press your patron for precedence

outcome.text: Your patron is asked to press your claim ahead of competing candidates.

choices.label: Accept a supervised parish assignment

outcome.text: You offer to take a supervised parish task before receiving wider responsibility.

events.title: LEAD A ROAD PATROL
events.text: {{client}} reports bandits on the road. The reeve’s nephew insists they cannot be there; a familiar tent suggests otherwise.

choices.label: Scout the dangerous road first

outcome.text: Scouts return with observations before the patrol takes the road.

choices.label: Ride a direct armed patrol

negative: Risk of injury to the client

outcome.text: The armed patrol moves directly toward the reported camp.

choices.label: Coordinate with local watchmen

outcome.text: Local watchmen compare routes and signals with your patrol.

events.title: ORGANISE THE COMPANY
events.text: {{client}} brings the company muster. Spears, boots and soldiers appear in three different totals, and the next march is approaching.

choices.label: Inspect equipment and practise formations

outcome.text: The equipment list is checked against the soldiers present at drill.

choices.label: Demand an immediate forced drill

negative: Risk of injury to the client

outcome.text: The company is ordered into a forced exercise before every shortage is repaired.

choices.label: Give experienced soldiers a voice

outcome.text: Experienced soldiers identify the failures they will have to carry on the march.

events.title: COMMAND A CONVOY ESCORT
events.text: {{client}} needs an escort for a supply convoy. A fast route crosses an exposed ford; the longer road needs ration stops.

choices.label: Scout the convoy route and ration stops

outcome.text: The convoy plan names water, cover and ration stops along the scouted road.

choices.label: Race the convoy through the threat

negative: Risk of injury to the client

outcome.text: You accept exposure at the ford in exchange for a faster crossing.

choices.label: Hire engineers and share command

outcome.text: Engineers and soldiers divide the work of protecting the convoy.

events.title: SEEK A NOBLE PATRON
events.text: {{client}} will consider patronage if you can offer a useful service. {{rival}} promises access to people neither of you has met.

choices.label: Offer a documented service

outcome.text: The proposed service is specific enough for a patron to judge your usefulness.

choices.label: Promise influence beyond your standing

outcome.text: Your promise of influence reaches beyond your established position.

choices.label: Seek an introduction from a colleague

outcome.text: A colleague carries an introduction and an account of your previous work.

events.title: ADVISE ON A DECREE
events.text: {{client}} brings a salt levy that counts the same barrel three times. Changing the draft may offend its author.

choices.label: Compare the decree with actual accounts

outcome.text: The salt draft is compared with the accounts of actual cargoes.

choices.label: Demand the council adopt your draft

outcome.text: You demand the council adopt your correction in front of the original author.

choices.label: Circulate a revised draft privately

outcome.text: A revised draft circulates privately before the council’s decision.

events.title: INVESTIGATE COURT ACCOUNTS
events.text: {{client}} asks you to inspect wages paid to a dead falconer. {{rival}} suggests the hawks remain loyal enough to justify a pension.

choices.label: Publish the checked accounts

outcome.text: The burial entry and wage account are checked before publication.

choices.label: Confront the beneficiary immediately

outcome.text: The beneficiary is confronted before every payment has been traced.

choices.label: Ask another auditor to witness the books

outcome.text: A second auditor signs the checked account beside your name.

events.title: EXAMINE A PATIENT
events.text: {{client}} requests an examination. Establish actual symptoms first; a healthy person needs advice rather than an invented disease.

choices.label: Compare actual symptoms and history

outcome.text: Your examination begins with the person’s own history and observable signs.

choices.label: Give a rapid confident opinion

outcome.text: You give a rapid opinion and accept responsibility for its certainty.

choices.label: Consult another practitioner

outcome.text: Another practitioner reviews the observations before an opinion is recorded.

events.title: TREAT A HOUSEHOLD
events.text: {{client}} requests care based on the recorded symptoms. Relief depends on the real condition, your preparation and the risks of your method.

choices.label: Treat the recorded condition cautiously

outcome.text: Your care follows the actual record and avoids an unnecessary intervention.

choices.label: Attempt an aggressive intervention

negative: Risk of client harm or a professional complaint

outcome.text: You accept the greater risks of a forceful intervention for a hoped-for recovery.

choices.label: Arrange supervised care and follow-up

outcome.text: A colleague joins the care plan and agrees a follow-up examination.

events.title: ORGANISE FEVER RELIEF
events.text: {{client}} asks you to organise fever relief. The sick households share water, bedding and several contradictory explanations.

choices.label: Trace sick households and clean water

outcome.text: The relief plan traces sick households and the water they share.

choices.label: Order a public purge of suspect goods

outcome.text: A public order calls for suspect goods to be removed before the cause is fully established.

choices.label: Organise parish volunteers and beds

outcome.text: Volunteers arrange beds, clean cloth and separate drinking vessels.

events.title: PERFORM IN THE HALL
events.text: {{client}} offers a place in the hall’s programme. The audience likes a fine genealogy and dislikes finding its own scandals in the rhyme.

choices.label: Prepare a piece suited to the audience

outcome.text: You prepare a piece for the audience’s tastes and its known sensitivities.

choices.label: Improvise for a larger purse

outcome.text: You improvise before listeners whose generosity is not assured.

choices.label: Share the bill with another performer

outcome.text: The fellow performer receives an agreed place and share of the bill.

events.title: SEEK A PAYING PATRON
events.text: {{client}} is considering a place for a performer at their table. Supper, a deposit and the patron’s right to request encores all remain negotiable.

choices.label: Offer a documented service

outcome.text: The proposed service is specific enough for a patron to judge your usefulness.

choices.label: Promise influence beyond your standing

outcome.text: Your promise of influence reaches beyond your established position.

choices.label: Seek an introduction from a colleague

outcome.text: A colleague carries an introduction and an account of your previous work.

events.title: ANSWER A PUBLIC SCANDAL
events.text: {{rival}} has added a verse about you to a public performance. {{client}} offers a stage, with no guarantee that powerful listeners will laugh.

choices.label: Use facts and keep the verse measured

outcome.text: The verse stays close to facts that can be defended after the laughter.

choices.label: Name the powerful subject openly

outcome.text: Your public verse names the powerful subject and places your safety beside the rhyme.

choices.label: Test the verse with a fellow performer

outcome.text: A fellow performer tests the verse before it reaches the public stage.

events.title: DEFEND A TENANT
events.text: {{client}} needs evidence prepared for a proper hearing. An advocate’s opinion cannot erase a charge or end a lawful sentence.

choices.label: Prepare the real evidence for a hearing

outcome.text: Your evidence bundle is submitted for the hearing; the court retains judgment.

choices.label: Challenge the prosecution publicly

outcome.text: You publicly dispute the prosecution’s account without claiming a pardon.

choices.label: Retain a second advocate

outcome.text: A second advocate reviews the evidence and lawful grounds for defence.

events.title: INVESTIGATE A CHARTER
events.text: {{client}} produces an ancient charter whose youngest witness is inconveniently still alive. The ink and testimony need checking.

choices.label: Check the charter against witnesses

outcome.text: The charter is checked against its witnesses and surviving copies.

choices.label: Accuse the claimant of forgery now

outcome.text: You accuse the claimant openly before every disputed mark is explained.

choices.label: Commission a second reading

outcome.text: A second reader compares the ink, names and boundaries.

events.title: HEAR A SWORN CASE
events.text: {{client}} brings a sworn boundary dispute. Both neighbours claim a pig which appears to prefer a third household.

choices.label: Record sworn testimony for the court

outcome.text: Sworn testimony is recorded for the judge to consider.

choices.label: Deliver a forceful public opinion

outcome.text: Your public opinion enters the dispute as advice, with the actual court still responsible.

choices.label: Seek an agreed submission to the judge

outcome.text: The neighbours receive a proposal for an agreed submission to the judge.

events.title: RECRUIT AN ASSOCIATE
events.text: {{client}} proposes joining your associates. Their account includes three debts and an unusually detailed knowledge of the sheriff’s route.

choices.label: Check the associate’s account first

outcome.text: The proposed associate’s debts and account are checked before an agreement.

choices.label: Promise a large share for quick service

outcome.text: You offer a large share for quick service and take the risk of an untested promise.

choices.label: Ask a trusted associate to vouch for them

outcome.text: A trusted associate is asked to stake their reputation on the newcomer.

events.title: ORGANISE AN OPERATION
events.text: {{client}} brings a plan for a collector’s chest. The guards, escape route and division of the proceeds remain unsettled.

choices.label: Scout guards and plan an escape

outcome.text: The plan records guards, an escape route and what to do if the chest is empty.

choices.label: Strike before the guard changes

outcome.text: You bring the operation forward to exploit the present guard’s weakness.

choices.label: Divide the operation among trusted partners

outcome.text: Partners receive separate roles and a witnessed division of the expected proceeds.

events.title: INVESTIGATE AN INFORMER
events.text: {{client}} suspects an informer. {{rival}} is repeating details that only a few associates were supposed to know.

choices.label: Compare who knew each detail

outcome.text: The inquiry compares each leaked detail with the people who knew it.

choices.label: Confront the suspected informer

outcome.text: You confront the suspected informer and risk warning the real source.

choices.label: Use an associate to check the story

outcome.text: An associate quietly checks the account against a second witness.

events.title: THE RENT NOTCH
events.text: The bailiff counts an extra rent notch on the household tally. {{classmate}} is holding the grain sack open. If the bailiff is right, there will be very little left for supper.

choices.label: Fit the two halves of the tally together

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks your count and {{classmate}} helps fit the halves. The old notches line up; the extra demand does not.

choices.label: Trim the notch and blame the knife on {{classmate}}

outcome.text: The fresh cut is pale against the old wood. {{mentor}} sees it at once, and {{classmate}} refuses to lend you anything sharp again.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the tally

outcome.text: {{mentor}} runs a thumb along the fresh mark and shows you where to compare it. You finish the count without sacrificing supper.

events.title: THE SEED POT
events.text: There is a drowned rat in the seed pot. {{classmate}} looks from the rat to the bread dough and says, “We need not mention it.”

choices.label: Help {{classmate}} sort out clean seed

outcome.text: You spread the grain to dry. {{mentor}} checks it with you, and {{classmate}} starts counting what can still be sown.

choices.label: Say {{classmate}} put the rat there

outcome.text: {{classmate}} gets a filthy pot to scrub. {{mentor}} catches your smirk before you can wipe it away.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} how to store the seed

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds a dry bin with a stone lid. {{classmate}} carries the saved grain while you clean out the old pot.

events.title: LETTERS ON THE DOOR
events.text: {{mentor}} chalks letters onto a soot-blackened door. A neighbour sees the crooked marks and fetches holy water. {{classmate}} helpfully draws a little tail on the B.

choices.label: Read the letters before the bucket arrives

outcome.text: You sound out the words while {{classmate}} rubs off the tail. The neighbour lowers the bucket; {{mentor}} gives you a harder word.

choices.label: Tell the neighbour {{classmate}} wrote the curse

outcome.text: The neighbour makes the sign of the cross at {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} has just watched you write the letters, so the excuse lasts one breath.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to read with you

outcome.text: {{mentor}} guides your finger along a familiar household name. The neighbour recognises it and takes the holy water home.

events.title: THE WOOL ACCOUNT
events.text: You and {{classmate}} must count six fleeces for a buyer. One is dripping onto the floor. {{mentor}} asks whether water has become as valuable as wool.

choices.label: Dry them and work out the true weight

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps spread the wool. {{mentor}} checks the dry weight and lets you finish the count together.

choices.label: Hide the wet fleece in {{classmate}}’s sack

outcome.text: The sack drips all the way to {{mentor}}’s feet. {{classmate}} opens it and looks straight at you.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for a dry sample to compare

outcome.text: You weigh the sample, then the suspect fleece. {{mentor}} helps you calculate the difference before the buyer comes back.

events.title: THE SAINT WITH TWO ELBOWS
events.text: {{mentor}} sets you to copy the relic list. You give Saint Aelfric three elbows. {{classmate}} peers over and asks whether he used all of them for praying.

choices.label: Check the older list together

outcome.text: {{classmate}} finds the missing saint. {{mentor}} watches you move one elbow to its proper owner and praises the correction.

choices.label: Let {{classmate}} copy your splendid extra elbow

outcome.text: The visiting canon counts the elbows aloud. {{classmate}} recognises your mistake on their own page, and {{mentor}} recognises who lent it.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the relic list

outcome.text: {{mentor}} lays the old list beside yours. You correct the extra elbow without making the saint lose anything else.

events.title: THE PSALTER PIG
events.text: A pig eats the bottom half of a psalter page. {{classmate}} catches it by one hind leg; {{mentor}} catches the book. Neither rescue restores the words.

choices.label: Rebuild the missing lines with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: Between you, enough of the psalm comes back. {{mentor}} checks a second book and helps you fill the gap honestly.

choices.label: Accuse {{classmate}} of feeding the page to the pig

outcome.text: {{classmate}} lets go of the leg in shock. The pig escapes, and {{mentor}} has seen enough to doubt your story.

choices.label: Bring the torn book to {{mentor}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} borrows another psalter. You compare the lines while {{classmate}} keeps the pig outside.

events.title: THE BURIAL FEE
events.text: A widow finds her husband entered twice in the burial book. “He was difficult,” she tells {{mentor}}, “but I only buried him once.” {{classmate}} is trying not to laugh.

choices.label: Find and correct the duplicate entry

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps find the earlier burial. {{mentor}} checks your correction and the widow keeps her pennies.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s signature under the extra charge

outcome.text: The widow curses {{classmate}} by name. {{mentor}} spots the copied hand, and your classmate learns exactly why everyone is staring.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to strike out the second burial

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks both dates with you and crosses out the duplicate. You take the corrected book back to the widow.

events.title: THE BELL ROPE EXAMINATION
events.text: {{classmate}} hangs from the bell rope with the only clean lesson sheet clamped between their teeth. Every attempt to speak rings the bell again. {{mentor}} is coming to find out why.

choices.label: Help them down and share the sheet

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks the answers with both of you. The bell rings once more when {{classmate}} finally lets go.

choices.label: Read the answers while {{classmate}} dangles

outcome.text: You finish first. {{mentor}} looks from your neat page to {{classmate}}’s white knuckles and stops looking pleased.

choices.label: Fetch {{mentor}} and something to stand on

outcome.text: {{mentor}} steadies a stool while you guide {{classmate}} down. The lesson resumes with the bell rope tied out of reach.

events.title: THE MASTER’S PERFECT HORSESHOE
events.text: {{mentor}} selects a horseshoe for inspection. You saw it crack under the hammer. {{classmate}} is about to carry it in on a cushion, which will not improve the metal.

choices.label: Repair the crack with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} watches your careful repair. {{classmate}} carries in a sound shoe and makes sure your help is mentioned.

choices.label: Blame {{classmate}} for cracking the shoe

outcome.text: {{classmate}} gets the blame before the inspector. {{mentor}} remembers who was at the anvil and asks you to stay behind.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} the crack before the inspection

outcome.text: {{mentor}} turns the shoe in the light and puts it aside. You help make a sound replacement instead of learning how to hide a split.

events.title: THE STOLEN GUILD SEAL
events.text: A customer wants a silver mark stamped on pewter spoons. {{mentor}} sets the proper sample on the bench. {{classmate}} is watching the customer’s purse rather closely.

choices.label: Test the spoons against the real sample

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps with the test. The metal fails; {{mentor}} gives you credit for catching it before the spoons leave.

choices.label: Stamp {{classmate}}’s mark on the false spoons

outcome.text: {{classmate}} is called to explain the mark. {{mentor}} finds the spoons on your side of the bench, still warm from your work.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to test one in front of the customer

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you compare the two metals. The customer takes back the purse when the difference can no longer be talked away.

events.title: THE APPRENTICE’S FINGER
events.text: {{classmate}} traps a finger in the vice. The job is already late. {{mentor}} calls from the next room, asking why the hammering has stopped.

choices.label: Free the finger and finish together

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps check the hand. {{classmate}} works beside you once the pain settles, and you learn how to handle the vice safely.

choices.label: Tell {{mentor}} that {{classmate}} jammed it on purpose

outcome.text: {{mentor}} frees the hand, then hears your excuse. {{classmate}} holds the swollen finger against their chest and will not look at you.

choices.label: Call {{mentor}} before you turn the screw

outcome.text: {{mentor}} steadies the trapped hand while you ease the vice open. The job can wait; the finger cannot.

events.title: THE MASTERPIECE IN THE ASHES
events.text: A spark burns through your measured drawing. {{classmate}}’s neat copy lies unattended beside it. {{mentor}} will want both pieces of work before supper.

choices.label: Ask {{classmate}} to help rebuild the measurements

outcome.text: {{classmate}} shares the figures while you redraw the lost lines. {{mentor}} checks the finished work and credits you both.

choices.label: Hand in {{classmate}}’s drawing as your own

outcome.text: {{mentor}} recognises the compass holes from the earlier work. {{classmate}} holds out a hand for the drawing and leaves it there until you give it back.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the surviving lines

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps you recover the measurements from the unburnt corner. The new drawing is slower to make, but it is yours.

events.title: THE DEVIL IN THE MARGIN
events.text: {{classmate}} draws a bishop being swallowed by a snail. {{mentor}} finds the picture while the ink is wet. The snail is wearing a remarkably familiar mitre.

choices.label: Defend the picture as a warning against vanity

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you explain the warning. {{classmate}} keeps a straight face, then whispers thanks when the page is put away.

choices.label: Say {{classmate}} drew it to mock the bishop

outcome.text: {{classmate}} has to scrape the picture off the parchment. {{mentor}} notices that your explanation changes once the scraping starts.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} what the snail could mean

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds a solemn explanation with surprising speed. You learn which parts of it are safe to repeat outside the room.

events.title: THE GREEK THAT WASN’T
events.text: {{mentor}} proudly reads a Greek quotation. {{classmate}} turns it the right way up: it is a merchant’s laundry list, with a great deal to say about stained shirts.

choices.label: Translate it quietly before the lecture

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} work through the list. {{mentor}} changes the quotation and gives you a better passage to study.

choices.label: Encourage {{classmate}} to recite it to the chapter

outcome.text: The chapter hears the price of washing six shirts. {{mentor}} sees your face, and {{classmate}} realises why you were so eager to help.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} the list in private

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks your translation and shuts the book. The lecture begins with a different quotation.

events.title: THE FASTING DISPUTATION
events.text: The chapter is arguing over whether a goose counts as fish on a fast day. {{mentor}} wants your argument. {{classmate}} is guarding the goose from a cook who seems ready to settle it.

choices.label: Check the text with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} hears a careful argument instead of a hungry guess. {{classmate}} gets the goose out of the kitchen while the discussion continues.

choices.label: Blame {{classmate}} for the forbidden supper

outcome.text: The chapter turns on {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} has heard you arguing for the meal and makes you answer for your own words.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to keep the cook waiting

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you find the relevant passage before anyone picks up a knife. The goose gets a little longer to be a goose.

events.title: THE MEDICAL GLOSS
events.text: A manuscript recommends bleeding anyone who faints. {{classmate}} has fainted over it. {{mentor}} reaches the desk while somebody is looking for a lancet.

choices.label: Read the patient before trusting the page

outcome.text: You help {{classmate}} lie safely while {{mentor}} checks their breathing. You compare what happened with what the manuscript actually claims.

choices.label: Say {{classmate}} demanded the lancet

outcome.text: {{mentor}} puts down the lancet and asks who suggested it. {{classmate}} hears you shift the blame and remembers it once the room stops spinning.

choices.label: Fetch {{mentor}} before anyone uses the blade

outcome.text: {{mentor}} arranges immediate care. Later, you set the actual symptoms beside the old advice and mark the dangerous difference.

events.title: THE PAGE AND THE PRIVY
events.text: Your watch is outside the lord’s privy. {{classmate}} has a desperate visitor by the elbow, and {{mentor}} has told you not to let anyone through.

choices.label: Hear the visitor before enforcing the order

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} find a sensible way to help without abandoning the watch. {{mentor}} hears a clear account rather than a wet complaint.

choices.label: Send the visitor to {{classmate}}’s post instead

outcome.text: The complaint lands on {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} follows the visitor’s route back to you, while your classmate begins taking a careful interest in your next watch.

choices.label: Fetch {{mentor}} to settle the urgent problem

outcome.text: {{mentor}} handles the visitor and shows you how to keep the watch without making misery its main purpose.

events.title: THE SQUIRE’S WOODEN HORSE
events.text: {{classmate}}’s practice saddle slips beneath the rider. {{mentor}} calls it a lesson in balance. The horse appears to be learning how far a pupil can slide.

choices.label: Check the girth and help remount

outcome.text: {{classmate}} holds the horse while you fix the girth. {{mentor}} checks it and lets you practise together on sound tack.

choices.label: Claim {{classmate}} loosened your saddle

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks the straps and finds your careless fastening. {{classmate}} hears the accusation before you can take it back.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to inspect the tack

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you check every buckle before the next ride. {{classmate}} holds the reins and waits until you get it right.

events.title: THE BLUNT LANCE
events.text: A fresh split runs down the training lance. {{mentor}} wants it ready for drill. {{classmate}} holds up a pot of paint and raises an eyebrow.

choices.label: Replace the damaged shaft together

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps fit sound wood. {{mentor}} checks the lance, then gives you both another turn at the drill.

choices.label: Give the painted split lance to {{classmate}}

outcome.text: The paint flakes when {{mentor}} tests the shaft. {{classmate}} sees the split and realises why you insisted on swapping.

choices.label: Bring the shaft to {{mentor}} before drill

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds a sound replacement and shows you where a painted crack will still give under pressure.

events.title: THE HUNGRY MUSTER
events.text: {{mentor}} asks you to check the muster. There are four dead soldiers on it and a horse drawing a cook’s wage. {{classmate}} wants to meet this very talented horse.

choices.label: Recount the living soldiers with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: You cross-check the names together. {{mentor}} approves the corrected roll and has a useful drill ready for you.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s name beside the extra rations

outcome.text: {{classmate}} is called to account for food never received. {{mentor}} compares the marks with your earlier work and calls you over.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the suspicious names

outcome.text: {{mentor}} removes the false entries while you copy the corrected ration order. The horse returns to being paid in oats.

events.title: THE WRONG COAT OF ARMS
events.text: {{mentor}} asks you to seat two hostile cousins at supper. {{classmate}} has drawn crossed swords between their names on the plan.

choices.label: Check the family ties before placing them

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps redraw the table. {{mentor}} approves seats with several calm people and a great deal of food between the cousins.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s name on the insulting plan

outcome.text: The cousins demand to know why {{classmate}} put them together. {{mentor}} has already seen your first drawing and asks for it back.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the disputed arms

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps you trace the descent, then moves the cousins away from the sharp cutlery. You keep the corrected plan.

events.title: THE ACCOUNT OF THE SWANS
events.text: The kitchen has paid for thirteen swans and received twelve. {{mentor}} gives you the receipts. {{classmate}} points out that the thirteenth looks suspiciously like a goose.

choices.label: Find the goose receipt together

outcome.text: {{classmate}} tracks down the cheaper bird. {{mentor}} praises the careful sum before anyone accuses the cook of eating a swan.

choices.label: Slip the missing swan into {{classmate}}’s account

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds two different hands in the account. {{classmate}} has to explain a purchase you made up for them.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to compare the kitchen receipts

outcome.text: {{mentor}} puts the goose receipt beside the swan price. You correct the total and return the money to the proper column.

events.title: THE EMBASSY’S CHAIRS
events.text: An envoy’s chair is an inch lower than yours. {{classmate}} notices first; {{mentor}} arrives just as the envoy’s secretary demands a ruler.

choices.label: Change the seating without singling anyone out

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps swap the chairs. {{mentor}} watches the envoy sit down without having to defend anyone’s knees.

choices.label: Tell the envoy {{classmate}} chose the low chair

outcome.text: {{classmate}} receives a frosty bow. {{mentor}} has watched you move the chairs and is unimpressed by the explanation.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to replace the whole row

outcome.text: Every guest gets an equally uncomfortable chair. {{mentor}} lets you explain the seating plan while nobody can claim a shorter seat.

events.title: THE TENANT’S PETITION
events.text: A tenant asks for seed grain. {{mentor}} calls it a lesson in managing a household. “Mine is hungry,” the tenant replies. {{classmate}} stops fiddling with the seal.

choices.label: Count what can safely be spared

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps work out the grain. {{mentor}} checks your proposal and approves an answer the household can actually carry out.

choices.label: Forge a refusal under {{classmate}}’s name

outcome.text: The tenant blames {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} catches the copied seal and makes you read the refusal aloud to the person it would hurt.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the stores with you

outcome.text: You count the grain beside {{mentor}} instead of guessing from the tenant’s manners. The request gets a practical answer.

events.title: THE WINTER ACCOUNT
events.text: The grain reserve and a creditor both need the same coins. {{mentor}} brings the figures; {{classmate}} brings a loaf to make sure the lesson lasts until supper.

choices.label: Plan the stores with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks the sums. You and {{classmate}} find enough for seed and supper without making a debt disappear.

choices.label: Hide the arrears under {{classmate}}’s figures

outcome.text: {{classmate}} finds the debt tucked beside their signature. {{mentor}} asks you to add it up again, this time with every number showing.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check what can be spared

outcome.text: {{mentor}} keeps the seed grain separate while you and {{classmate}} work out the payment. You leave with a plan you can explain at home.

events.title: AN EVENING OF LETTERS
events.text: After work, {{classmate}} brings a tenancy clause neither of you understood as children. {{mentor}} fetches the older agreement. The rent has grown much faster than the words.

choices.label: Read the two agreements side by side

outcome.text: {{classmate}} finds the changed line while {{mentor}} checks your reading. You can both explain the new rent without guessing.

choices.label: Pretend the clause gives you the advantage

outcome.text: {{classmate}} takes your reading to the landlord and comes back with the old agreement. {{mentor}} does not need to ask which line you left out.

choices.label: Read the disputed sentence with {{mentor}}

outcome.text: You work through the unfamiliar words with {{mentor}}. The altered obligation is much less impressive once you can read all of it.

events.title: THE LATE READER
events.text: {{classmate}} brings a contract to the evening reading lesson. {{mentor}} starts with the large decorated initial. “That bit owes nothing,” your classmate says. “Try the rest.”

choices.label: Read the contract together

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} pick out the promises hiding under the fine writing. {{mentor}} checks each one and lets you read the last sentence unaided.

choices.label: Copy {{classmate}}’s fluent exercise

outcome.text: {{mentor}} praises the borrowed page until {{classmate}} lays the original beside it. The two pages have the same ink blot.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for a shorter passage to start with

outcome.text: {{mentor}} covers the rest of the page. You get through one hard sentence properly before trying the next.

events.title: A LETTER HOME
events.text: {{classmate}} needs a letter for a relative working away from home. The first attempt contains a great deal of weather and none of what they want to say. {{mentor}} leaves you a quiet corner.

choices.label: Help write what they actually mean

outcome.text: {{classmate}} reads it back slowly and folds it with care. {{mentor}} checks the difficult words without prying into the rest.

choices.label: Read the private lines aloud for a laugh

outcome.text: The room laughs before {{classmate}} can take the page away. {{mentor}} sends the listeners back to work; your classmate folds the letter without your help.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} how to keep the letter private

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps you find plain words for the reply. {{classmate}} watches you leave the private lines covered.

events.title: THE LATE APPRENTICE
events.text: {{classmate}} gets the heavy lifting because an older apprentice is supposedly stronger. {{mentor}} asks you to choose the work for a trial piece. Your classmate is rubbing a shoulder.

choices.label: Suggest a fair rotation and a proper trial

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps with the piece while you share the lifting. {{mentor}} tests the result and gives both of you useful work.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s mark on your flawed trial piece

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds the fault. {{classmate}} recognises the piece they helped you carry and sees the mark you added.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to test the work you already know

outcome.text: {{mentor}} gives you a small job at the bench and watches your hands. You find out which parts of the late apprenticeship still need practice.

events.title: THE EVENING MASTERPIECE
events.text: You have one evening to finish your apprenticeship sample. {{classmate}} offers their measurements. {{mentor}} will test the piece in the morning. The first cock has already crowed.

choices.label: Use the figures and credit their help

outcome.text: {{mentor}} tests the finished piece. You name the help, and {{classmate}} stays to hear the answer beside you.

choices.label: Put your mark on {{classmate}}’s finished sample

outcome.text: {{mentor}} asks about a joint you have never cut. {{classmate}} produces the drawing and waits for you to stop describing it.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} what you can honestly finish

outcome.text: {{mentor}} sets a smaller trial from the surviving measurements. You have time to make it properly rather than sign somebody else’s work.

events.title: THE INFERMARER’S COMMENTARY
events.text: {{mentor}} sets a fever diary beside an old commentary. The patient recovered on the day the commentary says recovery was impossible. {{classmate}} asks whether the patient has been told.

choices.label: Compare the observations honestly

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps set out the dates. {{mentor}} makes you separate what was seen from what the commentary merely assumed.

choices.label: Change the diary to flatter the old authority

outcome.text: {{classmate}} keeps the original notes. When {{mentor}} compares the dates, your corrected patient appears to have recovered twice.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the symptoms with you

outcome.text: You work through the diary beside {{mentor}}, marking the actual symptoms before discussing the old explanation.

events.title: THE VISITING EXAMINER
events.text: A visiting examiner asks which study you completed between paid jobs. {{mentor}} has the real hours; {{classmate}} has a finished certificate with remarkably tempting blank space.

choices.label: Present your honest study record

outcome.text: {{mentor}} confirms the hours. {{classmate}} helps you list what remains, and the examiner can question you on work you actually did.

choices.label: Borrow the completed clerical certificate

outcome.text: The paper passes the first inspection. {{classmate}} recognises the borrowed certificate, and its signatures may still be checked later.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for the real examination requirements

outcome.text: {{mentor}} lists the hours and arguments still needed. You practise one of the difficult questions instead of practising a signature.

events.title: THE VETERAN AT DRILL
events.text: {{mentor}} asks for a plan to defend a narrow gate. {{classmate}} draws a wonderful formation with you standing directly in front of every spear.

choices.label: Work through the drill together

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} move the markers until both lines have cover. {{mentor}} checks the plan and sends you out to try it.

choices.label: Present {{classmate}}’s plan as your own

outcome.text: {{mentor}} asks why your plan has {{classmate}}’s initials in the corner. {{classmate}} waits to hear the answer.

choices.label: Review the drill beside {{mentor}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} moves you out of the spear line and makes you explain why the new position is safer. You practise until you can hold it.

events.title: THE CONTRACTED WATCH
events.text: The adult recruits have paid work in the morning, but somebody must stand the cold watch. {{classmate}} finds their name on nearly every empty space. {{mentor}} hands you the rota.

choices.label: Take your share and make a fair rotation

outcome.text: {{classmate}} checks the new list while {{mentor}} checks your name is on it too. You learn the watch instead of merely assigning it.

choices.label: Leave {{classmate}} on every cold watch

outcome.text: {{classmate}} makes a second copy. {{mentor}} reads it at breakfast while you try to look well rested for an innocent reason.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to review the watch with you

outcome.text: You and {{mentor}} fit the watches around the recruits’ paid work. {{classmate}} keeps a turn, but so do you.

events.title: THE PRIVATE TUTOR’S TABLE
events.text: {{classmate}} brings a household request to the adult lesson. {{mentor}} asks for useful advice. Your classmate puts away the beautifully phrased version and shows you the unpaid bills.

choices.label: Work from the actual household figures

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks your proposed relief. {{classmate}} has an answer that may help at home, rather than a compliment to repeat at supper.

choices.label: Trade their private grievance for influence

outcome.text: The story comes back to {{classmate}} with your name attached. {{mentor}} sets aside your polished advice and asks about the confidence you broke.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the relief you propose

outcome.text: {{mentor}} counts the grain with you before you promise it. {{classmate}} leaves with a smaller, affordable request.

events.title: THE ADULT AUDIENCE
events.text: An envoy asks why the household pays for tutoring while tenants need seed. {{mentor}} gives you the figures; {{classmate}} waits to see whether your answer contains any grain.

choices.label: Explain the figures and offer affordable relief

outcome.text: You answer the difficult questions while {{classmate}} checks the sums. {{mentor}} has you defend a practical decision rather than a borrowed phrase.

choices.label: Produce a borrowed court certificate

outcome.text: The seal opens a door for now. {{classmate}} recognises the document, and a later examination may ask what you actually learned.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for an honest assessment

outcome.text: {{mentor}} offers a witnessed examination. You work on the questions still beyond you instead of pretending the certificate answered them.

events.title: THE EVE OF BATTLE
events.text: Dawn. The enemy host gathers across the muddy field. Your sergeant bellows the order to form ranks. Your hands will not stop shaking.

choices.label: Hold the line bravely

outcome.text: You locked shields with the men beside you and held. The first charge breaks against your wall of spears.

choices.label: Pray for deliverance

outcome.text: You prayed harder than you have ever prayed. Whether God listened, the battle will decide.

choices.label: Slip toward the baggage train

outcome.text: You edged away from the front toward the wagons. Safer, until somebody notices, and then a great deal worse.

events.title: THE ROUT
events.text: The lines dissolve into screaming chaos. A mounted knight in enemy colours bears down on you, lance lowered. There is no time to think.

choices.label: Stand and brace your spear

success.text: You set your spear and the charging horse impaled itself. You stand, blood-soaked and alive, a hero of the field. The lord himself learns your name.

failure.text: The lance took you in the shoulder and the world went white. You wake days later in a surgeon’s tent, ruined but breathing.

choices.label: Dive into the mud and play dead

success.text: You lay among the fallen, unmoving, until the horses thundered past. Survival has no honour, but it has a pulse.

failure.text: A looter finds you breathing and strikes before fleeing. You stagger out wounded, furious at having played the least convincing corpse on the field.

catastrophe.text: A looter found you "dead" and was most surprised when you flinched. The scuffle did not go your way.

effects.death: Cut down by a battlefield looter while feigning death.

choices.label: Surrender and beg ransom

outcome.text: As a knight, you are worth more alive. You yield your sword and are held for ransom, which is humiliating and survivable, in that order.

events.title: A YEAR OF MARRIED LIFE
events.text: A year wed. The first flush has settled into something steadier. Your spouse asks, gently, what you both should build toward.

choices.label: A houseful of children

outcome.text: You agree to fill the cottage with noise and turnip-stained little hands. Terrifying. Wonderful.

choices.label: Saving toward a better life

outcome.text: You both resolve to scrimp and climb. Every coin saved is a brick in a grander future.

choices.label: Admit you are restless

outcome.text: You confess a wandering heart. The conversation is hard, and honest, and leaves a small crack that may yet widen.

events.title: THE RIVAL · A CONTEST MADE PUBLIC
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Win the turnip race

outcome.text: You cross first, wheezing turnip dust. {{rival.name}} insists the sack was uneven. The crowd insists they do the victory bow anyway.

choices.label: Refuse to make it a contest

outcome.text: You ask why anyone should carry turnips for free. The crowd drifts away. {{rival.name}} is left guarding two sacks and an excellent bow.

choices.label: Try to make an ally of them instead

outcome.text: You offer to carry the sack together. {{rival.name}} accuses you of pitying them, then drops it on their own foot.

events.title: THE RIVAL · A PATRON TAKES AN INTEREST
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Put yourself in front of {{patron.name}} too

outcome.text: You offer to keep the pig accounts. {{patron.name}} likes your confidence. {{rival.name}} now has to explain every missing turnip to you.

choices.label: Improve your own vegetable patch

outcome.text: You improve your own vegetable patch and fill the store cupboard. No patron required. No badge either, which is a mercy.

choices.label: Let {{patron.name}} hear the worst of them

outcome.text: You tell {{patron.name}} that the Deputy Pig Marshal lost a pig inside the chapel. It is true. Repeating the part about the baptismal font is optional, but you do.

events.title: THE RIVAL · A RUMOUR WITH ONE SOURCE
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Name {{rival.name}} as the source, publicly

outcome.text: You name {{rival.name}} as the liar and demand they produce the alleged ladle. Half the market cheers. The other half wants to see the ladle.

choices.label: Trace it properly and say nothing yet

outcome.text: You question the sellers. Each heard the tale from {{rival.name}}, who received a sealed note from {{patron.name}}. You keep the note.

choices.label: Make sure it cannot touch your household

outcome.text: You settle your household’s accounts in front of witnesses. The traders keep selling to your family, though the ladle jokes continue.

events.title: THE RIVAL · BEFORE THE WHOLE HALL
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Offer them terms in front of everyone

outcome.text: You offer a truce: no more rumours, no pressure on either household, and one public apology each. {{rival.name}} agrees. The priest takes his clapper home.

choices.label: Make them repeat the accusation beside the evidence

outcome.text: You ask the priest to hold up the clapper while {{rival.name}} repeats the accusation. They cannot finish. You have won, and made the humiliation needlessly thorough.
