outcome.text: Two children go to households that can feed them. It is plainly right and there is a real chance they do not come back.

choices.label: Take the whole household to kin in the next parish

outcome.text: Four miles and a different manor. You keep everybody and you lose your holding, your suit of court and every claim Swineford owed you.

events.title: ASHES OF THE HOUSEHOLD · IT STARTED AT THE BYRE END
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Ask, and hear the answer

outcome.text: It was carelessness by somebody who is fourteen and has not eaten properly since. You now know and can never quite unknow it.

choices.label: Say you do not want to know

outcome.text: You say it clearly enough that nobody ever raises it. The household rebuilds with one secret in it that everybody can feel and nobody can name.

choices.label: Let it be understood that a stranger did it

outcome.text: A convenient pedlar is blamed, in his absence, permanently. It protects the household and it is a lie the household has to keep for good.

events.title: ASHES OF THE HOUSEHOLD · WHAT GETS REBUILT
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Build small, and build it debt-free

outcome.text: One room fewer and no money owed to anybody. It is a lesser house and the household holds it outright and sleeps.

choices.label: Borrow and rebuild exactly what was there

outcome.text: The same house, on the same footings, on twenty-two shillings of somebody else’s money at a rate you did not read carefully.

memory.note: You borrowed heavily to rebuild the house exactly as it was.

events.title: ASHES OF THE HOUSEHOLD · A SMALLER ROOF, HELD OUTRIGHT
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Sleep in it

outcome.text: Everybody sleeps under it and the year turns. In forty years somebody adds the missing room and nobody remembers why it was missing.

events.title: ASHES OF THE HOUSEHOLD · THE SAME HOUSE, AND THE DEBT
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Make the first payment

outcome.text: It is paid, and the next, and the one after. The house is beautiful and the household works for it for five years.

events.title: THE DIVIDED PARISH · TWO SERMONS, ONE NAVE
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Sit deliberately on the poorer side

outcome.text: You take your household across the nave in front of everybody. It is a small movement and the whole parish reads it correctly.

choices.label: Read what each of them is actually preaching

outcome.text: You get both men to write down what they hold. Neither text is heresy and neither man will say that about the other one.

choices.label: Sit with the rector and take the churchwardenship

outcome.text: You sit where the power is and are made warden by Lady Day. It is the correct move and everybody watching knows exactly what it was.

events.title: THE DIVIDED PARISH · THE ROOD SCREEN MONEY
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Get it spent on the four households

outcome.text: You take it to a vote at the parish meeting and win by three. The screen is not built and there is no argument in the parish for six years about anything else.

choices.label: Build the screen

outcome.text: It is beautiful, it is still there, and six households spent that winter in a byre looking at it every Sunday.

choices.label: Build it cheaply and give the difference away

outcome.text: A plainer screen and nine shillings to the flooded. Neither party is satisfied and both can live with it. That is what a settlement is for.

events.title: THE DIVIDED PARISH · SOMEBODY WRITES TO THE BISHOP
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Warn the four

outcome.text: All four have time to think about what they will say. Two of them are very careful and two of them are not, and the difference shows.

choices.label: Find out who wrote it

outcome.text: It was the churchwarden, in the rector’s hand, over the chantry priest’s signature. All three of them are involved and none of them expected anyone to check.

choices.label: Be glad you are not on it

outcome.text: You say nothing to anybody. The four are cited, two do penance in the market place, and you watch from a doorway with everyone else.

events.title: THE DIVIDED PARISH · THE ARCHDEACON’S VISITATION
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Answer that the parish quarrelled over money and is done

outcome.text: It is true, it is unflattering to everybody equally, and it deprives both priests of a cause. The archdeacon accepts it with visible relief.

choices.label: Answer with the whole of it, names included

outcome.text: The letter, the screen money, the wardens, the lot. One priest is removed, one warden is ruined, and the parish talks about nothing else until the next rector dies.

events.title: THE DIVIDED PARISH · ONE SIDE OF THE NAVE AGAIN
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Sit where you always sat

outcome.text: The parish goes back to arguing about the churchyard wall, which is the correct thing for a parish to argue about.

events.title: THE DIVIDED PARISH · WHAT THE RECORD SAYS
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Let the record say it

outcome.text: It says it. Three families leave the parish inside eighteen months, and the two sides of the nave are still visible in where people sit in 1450.

events.title: THE GUILD ELECTION · TWO NAMES FOR ONE WARDENSHIP
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Back {{other.name}} openly

outcome.text: You put your name behind theirs early and in public, while it is still an open question and your name is still worth wagering.

choices.label: Read the guild’s own ordinances on the election

outcome.text: It turns out the wardenship is elected by all sworn brethren, not by the livery, and has been since 1311. Nobody has done it that way in thirty years.

choices.label: Let both of them bid for your support

outcome.text: You are courted for six weeks by two men with cellars. It is extremely pleasant and it costs you the respect of everyone who is watching.

events.title: THE GUILD ELECTION · A DINNER FOR THE LIVERY
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Give a dinner for the whole brotherhood (24g)

outcome.text: You feed sixty men badly instead of nine men well. It costs twenty-four shillings and it makes an argument that the swan cannot answer.

choices.label: Have the dinner recorded as an election expense

outcome.text: You get it entered in the book as what it was. The ordinance against treating exists, it is read out, and the swan becomes the most famous bird in the trade.

choices.label: Go to the dinner

outcome.text: You eat the swan and vote as you had already decided. Both facts are noticed and only one of them is believed.

events.title: THE GUILD ELECTION · THE SEARCHERS FIND FAULT
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Have them admit the fault and pay the fine

outcome.text: The fine is twopence and the admission is immediate. It takes the whole weapon away by refusing to pretend, and the searchers look ridiculous.

choices.label: Demand a search of the other candidate’s shop

outcome.text: They find four faults in an afternoon because there are always four faults. The election is now about searching and nobody remembers what it was about.

choices.label: Advise {{other.name}} to withdraw

outcome.text: They withdraw with the fault unadmitted, which the trade takes for guilt. It is the safe advice and it was the wrong advice.

events.title: THE GUILD ELECTION · THE VOTE ITSELF
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Take it by written scrutiny, all brethren voting

outcome.text: Every sworn man votes and nobody sees how. It takes two hours, it is close, and no one afterwards can say the result was arranged.

choices.label: Take it by show of hands, livery first

outcome.text: The livery raise their hands, everyone sees who raised what, and the rest of the hall votes accordingly. It is over in four minutes.

events.title: THE GUILD ELECTION · A WARDEN NOBODY CAN QUESTION
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Get the scrutiny written into the ordinances

outcome.text: Written scrutiny, all brethren, every election. It survives four attempts to repeal it and outlasts everybody who voted that day.

events.title: THE GUILD ELECTION · A WARDEN AND A SHOW OF HANDS
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Let the hands speak

outcome.text: The trade runs perfectly well and rather quietly. Nobody proposes anything at a guild meeting for nine years without checking the room first.

events.title: THE ROYAL BASTARD · A CHILD AT THE PRIORY GATE
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Make sure the child is being decently kept

outcome.text: You go and look. The child is well fed, entirely alone, and has not been outside the precinct since it could walk.

choices.label: Follow the money instead of the child

outcome.text: Four quarters of payments through three hands, and the third hand is a clerk of the wardrobe. That is not a nobleman’s by-blow. That is closer than that.

choices.label: Let the right people know that you know

outcome.text: A word in the right ear and the quarterly payments acquire a small additional recipient. It is the easiest money you have ever made.

events.title: THE ROYAL BASTARD · THE PAYMENTS STOP
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Pay the child’s keep yourself (20g)

outcome.text: Twenty shillings a year out of your own purse, quietly, with no explanation offered to the prior or anybody else.

choices.label: Take the child into your own household

outcome.text: One more at the table and a very large unanswered question living under your roof. The household adjusts and the question does not go away.

choices.label: Find out why the money stopped

outcome.text: Because the man who was paying it is dead, and because his executors are reading every account he kept. The child now appears in an executor’s inventory, listed between a bay gelding and thirteen yards of russet.

events.title: THE ROYAL BASTARD · MEN COME ASKING
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Tell them the child died in the winter

outcome.text: You say it steadily and the prior, to his eternal credit, says the same thing an hour later. They write it down and go, and you have just committed to something very large.

memory.note: You told the king’s men a living child was dead.

choices.label: Tell them the truth

outcome.text: The child is taken south within the week, well-horsed and well-attended, and is never heard of in this shire again by anybody.

choices.label: Ask what the child is worth to them

outcome.text: Rather a lot, it turns out, and they are willing to discuss it in a way that tells you exactly how frightened somebody in London is.

events.title: THE ROYAL BASTARD · THE CHILD ASKS
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Tell them everything and let them decide

outcome.text: You give them the payments, the men, the lie, all of it. They think for three days and choose to stay exactly who they are, which was always the better claim.

choices.label: Tell them to press the claim

outcome.text: You put a young person with no friends into the path of people who employ men on good horses. It might work. It is not principally about them.

events.title: THE ROYAL BASTARD · THE CLAIM NEVER MADE
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Let it be the small ending

outcome.text: They marry locally, hold four acres, and outlive most of the people who were frightened of them. Nothing whatever is written down.

memory.note: A royal claim was left unpressed and a life was left alone.

events.title: THE ROYAL BASTARD · THE CLAIM IN THE OPEN
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: See where it goes

outcome.text: It goes a long way and not far enough. Retainers are quartered in the village for two winters and everybody is very careful about what they say at market.

events.title: THE RELIC HUNTER · A LIST OF WHAT THE ABBEY LOST
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Warn the four parishes what they are holding

outcome.text: Three of them are grateful and one of them threatens you with a proctor. All four now know they may be sued in about eighteen months.

choices.label: Verify the inventory before doing anything

outcome.text: Two priories and a very unhelpful sacrist later, the inventory is genuine and the copy is not. Somebody has added a twelfth item in a newer hand.

choices.label: Go and find the remaining seven first

outcome.text: You are eight months ahead of anybody else who reads that list, and you spend all nineteen of them travelling.

events.title: THE RELIC HUNTER · THE TWELFTH ITEM
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Prove the interpolation and say so

outcome.text: Ink, hand and parchment all disagree with the rest of the sheet. You are entirely right and you have just made a lot of expensive people look foolish.

choices.label: Go looking for the thing anyway

outcome.text: A forged entry does not prove the object never existed. It takes nine months and you find something, in a wall, that nobody can explain.

choices.label: Sell what you know to the abbey

outcome.text: They pay generously for the news that their own inventory was tampered with and rather more for your agreement to stop reading it.

events.title: THE RELIC HUNTER · A COMPETITOR ON THE SAME ROAD
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Buy the remaining two first (28g)

outcome.text: Twenty-eight shillings and both parishes are extremely relieved to deal with somebody who at least tells them what they are selling.

choices.label: Get the archdeacon to forbid all four sales

outcome.text: A monition under seal to four churchwardens. Nothing else moves, nothing is recovered either, and the competitor turns his attention to a different diocese.

choices.label: Propose you split the list

outcome.text: Six each and no bidding against one another. It is efficient, it is profitable, and it turns two searchers into one market.

events.title: THE RELIC HUNTER · WHERE IT ALL GOES
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Give it to the parishes it was found in, with a written history

outcome.text: Each piece goes back where it surfaced with a full account of how it got there attached. Nobody gets everything and every object gets its story.

choices.label: Keep the collection whole and keep it yourself

outcome.text: Thirteen objects in one chest under your floor, worth a very great deal and impossible to show to anybody.

events.title: THE RELIC HUNTER · ELEVEN OBJECTS AND ELEVEN HISTORIES
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Send them the copies

outcome.text: The histories are copied and outlive the objects by three hundred years. Nobody meant that, and it is the better half of the bargain.

events.title: THE RELIC HUNTER · THE CHEST UNDER THE FLOOR
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Put the boards back

outcome.text: You nail the floor down. Twice a year you take it up and look, alone, and put it back, and that is the entire use the collection ever gets.

events.title: THE BROTHERHOOD · A CANDLE AND A COMMON BOX
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Join and pay your dues

outcome.text: Fourpence a quarter into the common box and your name in the brotherhood book. It is a burial club, a sick fund and, on the evidence, something else as well.

choices.label: Find out what happens behind the locked door

outcome.text: It is a burial club, a sick fund, and a meeting at which wages are discussed by men who are not allowed to discuss wages. That is precisely why the door is locked.

choices.label: Take note of who is in it

outcome.text: Seven names, and three of them work for men who would pay for that list. You do not sell it yet. You write it down.

events.title: THE BROTHERHOOD · THE COMMON BOX IS LIGHT
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Make the box up yourself (7g)

outcome.text: Seven shillings, replaced quietly, and the sick are paid on Friday. Two brothers work out what happened and neither of them ever says so.

choices.label: Put it to the brotherhood

outcome.text: He admits it in front of seven men, weeping, and is expelled by their own rule which does not allow for sick children. Everyone follows the rule and nobody defends it.

choices.label: Get the rule changed before anybody is accused

outcome.text: You propose relief for a brother’s household before you propose anything about the box. The rule passes, then the shortfall is raised, and it is a different meeting entirely.

events.title: THE BROTHERHOOD · THE STATUTE AND THE LOCKED DOOR
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Meet in the church porch with the door open

outcome.text: Everything the brotherhood does that is lawful is done in daylight where anyone may hear it. Everything else stops, and three brothers leave in disgust.

choices.label: Burn the brotherhood book

outcome.text: Fifteen names and forty years of burials, on the fire. There is now no evidence of anything, including of who is owed relief.

choices.label: Keep meeting behind the door

outcome.text: You go on exactly as before with a man watching the lane. It holds for two years, and then it holds for one more night than it should.

events.title: THE BROTHERHOOD · A JUSTICE ASKS FOR THE NAMES
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Give him the brotherhood’s accounts instead

outcome.text: Forty years of burials, sick pay and candle wax, handed over entire. It is dull, it is complete, and it makes the conspiracy charge collapse under its own boredom.

choices.label: Give him the seven names

outcome.text: You say them under oath, correctly, one after another. Four are fined, two are ruined, and one of them was the man who let you in.

events.title: THE BROTHERHOOD · THE LIGHT STILL BURNS
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Pay your quarter’s fourpence

outcome.text: You pay it for the rest of your life and the box pays your burial. The light is still burning in that church in 1520.

events.title: THE BROTHERHOOD · THE BOX IS BROKEN UP
events.text: state=>renderBoundText(state,node.text)

choices.label: Take your share of the box

outcome.text: Elevenpence. You are entitled to it, you take it, and you cannot afterwards remember what you spent it on.

events.title: AT THE CHURCH DOOR
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Stand witness and say the words

outcome.text: You say the words. Four households now consider you party to the bargain. In Swineford that is as binding as a seal and rather harder to break.

memory.note: You stood witness at a betrothal made between households, not people.

choices.label: Ask aloud whether the bride consents

outcome.text: The porch goes quiet. Canon law is on your side and nobody in the lane thanks you for it. She says yes, eventually, and everyone hears how long it took.

choices.label: Refuse to put your name to it

outcome.text: You walk back up the lane. They find another witness inside the hour, and remember that they had to.

events.title: THE FOUR SHILLINGS THAT NEVER CAME
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Quietly make up the shortfall (4g)

outcome.text: You put four shillings on the table and let them believe it came from the uncle. Two people know otherwise, and one of them is the uncle.

memory.note: You secretly paid a dowry that was owed by somebody else.

choices.label: Name the uncle at the hallmote

outcome.text: You say it in front of the steward. The uncle is amerced sixpence and swears he will remember your face longer than the debt.

choices.label: Let them work it out themselves

outcome.text: You say nothing. They work it out in March, badly, in front of the whole lane.

events.title: ONE DOOR BARRED
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE FOUR SHILLINGS THAT NEVER CAME

choices.label: Broker a smaller dowry before witnesses

outcome.text: Six ewes, the pot, and the shillings forgiven. Both households sign because you made it hard to refuse in public.

choices.label: Send it to the church court

outcome.text: The consistory court will hear it at Easter, or the Easter after. The bride will be nineteen by then and the pot will have been sold.

choices.label: Let the match die in the lane

outcome.text: Everyone goes indoors. The ewes stay where they are, the pot comes back to you, and two households stop speaking for a generation.

events.title: LETTERS FROM AN EARLIER LOVE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Burn them in the hearth

outcome.text: They go up quickly. {{other.name}} watches the whole time and neither of you says anything about it ever again.

memory.note: You burned letters that would have voided a marriage.

choices.label: Carry them to the priest

outcome.text: The priest takes the letters as evidence for a church hearing. You gain standing for submitting them and lose {{other.name}}’s trust; no marriage is dissolved simply because a witness has arrived.

choices.label: Keep them somewhere you can find them

outcome.text: You put them under the floor of the byre. They are worth nothing until the day they are worth a great deal.

memory.note: You hold letters that could dissolve a marriage whenever you choose.

events.title: THE CHILDREN OF BOTH HOUSES
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Tell them the whole of it

outcome.text: You give them the ewes, the pot, the uncle and the debt. They are disappointed by how small it all was. Nothing you could have said would have taught them more.

choices.label: Give them the kind version

outcome.text: You tell them about eight ewes and a brass pot and leave the uncle out. It is a better story and it will hold for another generation.

choices.label: Tell them to mind the harvest

outcome.text: They go back to the sheaves. The quarrel keeps its teeth for whoever asks next.

events.title: THE LAST WITNESS AT THE PORCH
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Set the table and sit them down

outcome.text: It takes most of an afternoon and two jugs. Nobody apologises, but by the end they are arguing about sheep prices instead, which is as close to peace as Swineford gets.

memory.note: You got two feuding households to sit at one table and hear the truth.

choices.label: Let it die with the witness

outcome.text: The witness is buried in spring and takes it with them. Both houses go on believing the version that suits them, and both are wrong.

events.title: A CHILD AT THE THRESHOLD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Give the child a place at your fire

outcome.text: You clear a corner by the hearth. The parish is relieved, your stores are not, and the child sleeps for fourteen hours.

choices.label: Find them a place at the mill

outcome.text: The miller takes the child for the work in them. It is a roof, and it is not a kindness, and you knew both when you arranged it.

choices.label: Turn them away

outcome.text: You shut the door. The child is taken in three doors down by people with less than you, and Swineford counts the doors.

events.title: THE BIRTH KIN COME BACK
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Pay them to go away (6g)

outcome.text: Six shillings and they are gone by dusk. They will be back in three years, having spent it, with the same argument.

choices.label: Take it to the hallmote

outcome.text: The steward rules the claim has no standing, the birth kin are amerced fourpence for troubling the court, and the whole village now knows the child’s business.

choices.label: Put it to the child

outcome.text: The child stands in the gateway and picks. It takes a long time and everybody has to watch.

events.title: THE LOAVES THAT WALKED
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Send more, and openly

outcome.text: You put a basket on their step yourself. It costs you a fortnight of stores and buys you something the stores could not.

choices.label: Explain what a theft costs, then look away

outcome.text: You explain leyrwite, amercement and the pillory in some detail, then go to bed early and stop counting loaves.

choices.label: Put a lock on the lardarium

outcome.text: The bread stops walking. So does the child’s habit of looking at you when you come in.

events.title: A PLACE AT THE FORGE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Pay the indenture (14g)

outcome.text: The indenture is cut in two and you keep the ragged half. The child is a smith’s apprentice by Whitsun and cries on the way out of the gate.

memory.note: You paid two marks to put your foster child into a trade.

choices.label: Keep them home for the harvest

outcome.text: You need the hands and you say so honestly, which does not make it land any better. The smith takes another boy.

choices.label: Send them to the priest for letters instead

outcome.text: Cheaper than a forge and slower to pay. The child learns to read a rent-roll, which in Swineford is very nearly a weapon.

events.title: WHICH NAME AT THE VIEW OF FRANKPLEDGE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Offer them your name

outcome.text: The clerk writes it without looking up. Your family gains a member and a set of complications, in that order.

memory.note: Your foster child took your surname at the frankpledge view.

choices.label: Tell them to keep their own

outcome.text: They give the name they were born with, in a clear voice, and the tithing writes it down as though it had never been in doubt.

events.title: THE UNEQUAL BOWLS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Say aloud that it is not fair

outcome.text: You agree, at volume, in front of everyone. The eldest puts down the bread and does not pick it up again that evening.

choices.label: Defend the custom of the manor

outcome.text: You point out that a divided holding feeds nobody. That is true. You then say it is why the thing has always been done, and that is a different argument wearing the same coat.

choices.label: Change the subject to the pig

outcome.text: You raise the matter of pannage in the lord’s wood. It works, for about a year.

events.title: THE CHRISTENING SPOON
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Search every chest in the house

outcome.text: You find no spoon, one hidden purse, and a letter nobody wanted read. The spoon turns up in June behind the salt.

choices.label: Buy a second spoon and say nothing (8g)

outcome.text: The silversmith asks no questions for an extra penny. Two spoons now exist and the family peace rests on nobody ever putting them side by side.

memory.note: You forged family peace with a duplicate christening spoon.

choices.label: Let the accusation lie where it fell

outcome.text: The blame settles on the sibling least able to argue back, which is why it settled there. Everyone is relieved and nobody says so.

events.title: A LINE IN A DIFFERENT HAND
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Sue in the church court (5g)

outcome.text: Probate belongs to the church and the church takes its time. Two years later a ruling arrives that pleases nobody and costs more than the land.

choices.label: Have a quiet word with the clerk

outcome.text: He is very frightened and very forthcoming. You leave with six shillings of his money and a permanent hold on him.

choices.label: Let the will stand as written

outcome.text: One line stays changed. The family stops shouting and starts keeping accounts of who owes whom, which lasts considerably longer.

events.title: AT THE LAMMAS ALE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A LINE IN A DIFFERENT HAND

choices.label: Say the grievance in the open

outcome.text: You lay it out in front of forty people and a barrel. It is true, it is satisfying, and the family will be explaining it at every ale for a decade.

choices.label: Toast the family and lie beautifully

outcome.text: You give a short speech about your parents that is almost entirely false and genuinely moving. Three people weep. The quarrel goes back under the table intact.

choices.label: Leave before the second barrel

outcome.text: You walk home in the light. Everything said after you go is worse than anything you would have said, and all of it is attributed to you.

events.title: WHAT THE DEAD ACTUALLY LEFT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Divide it evenly, whatever custom says

outcome.text: You split a holding that was never meant to be split. Each share feeds one household badly instead of one household well, and nobody has to leave.

memory.note: You split the family land against custom rather than turn kin out.

choices.label: Take what the custom gives you

outcome.text: You take the whole of it, lawfully, and two of your siblings are cottars by Michaelmas. The custom is on your side every single day of it.

memory.note: You took the whole inheritance by custom and left your siblings landless.

events.title: SICKNESS AT THE MILLRACE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Buy a sack in front of everyone

outcome.text: You carry it home on your shoulder past the whole market. Three households buy after you and one of them tells you it was foolish.

choices.label: Keep well clear of the mill

outcome.text: You grind by hand for a season and stay entirely well. The miller notices which neighbours crossed the lane to avoid his door.

choices.label: Fetch the herb-wife for them (2g)

outcome.text: She comes for tuppence and stays two nights. The fever breaks on the second, and she is honest enough to say she may have had nothing to do with it.

events.title: THE MILL HOUSE FALLS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Organise shared querns and shared labour

outcome.text: Six households, four hand-querns, and a rota you have to referee twice a week. Everyone eats and everyone complains about the rota.

choices.label: Grind your own and say nothing

outcome.text: Your household eats well and quietly. The smoke from your oven is visible from most of the lane.

choices.label: Argue for burning the mill’s stock

outcome.text: You get your way and a great deal of grain goes up in the yard. The sickness stops. So does the flour, three months before harvest.

events.title: THE CHARGE OF CONCEALMENT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Swear for the mill

outcome.text: You stand as an oath-helper and say the fortnight never happened. It probably did. The mill keeps its suit and you keep a debt you cannot name.

choices.label: Swear against it

outcome.text: You say what you saw. The mill is amerced two shillings, the customer buys you a drink, and the miller’s family stops speaking to yours entirely.

choices.label: Swear you saw nothing at all

outcome.text: The steward looks at you for slightly too long and writes it down anyway. Both sides now consider you unreliable, which is at least even-handed.

events.title: FORTY DAYS AND THE LAST GOOD GRAIN
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Shut the door and go hungry

outcome.text: The door is nailed and the grain sits behind it. Nobody else takes the fever and everybody else is thinner by Whitsun.

choices.label: Grind it out first, then shut the door

outcome.text: Two days of grinding with the sick upstairs. Swineford eats through the summer and two more households take the fever in June.

choices.label: Pay the physician to find them well (5g)

outcome.text: He writes what you paid for and rides out before dusk. The mill opens, the grain sells, and in August the parish clerk starts a longer burial list than usual.

memory.note: You paid a physician to certify a plagued house as sound.

events.title: THE WHEEL TURNS AGAIN
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: FORTY DAYS AND THE LAST GOOD GRAIN

choices.label: Buy the first sack of the new grinding (4g)

outcome.text: You take it at the old price in front of the market. The miller does not thank you, which is how you know it landed.

choices.label: Take your custom to the next village’s mill

outcome.text: It is a four-mile walk each way and a penny more a bushel. You make it every month for a decade and never once explain why.

events.title: A HAND ON THE WINTER ROAD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Take her in until it mends

outcome.text: She stays nine weeks and is a terrible guest. Every woman in the parish comes to your door to ask her things. It ruins your mornings and puts your household at the centre of the lane.

choices.label: Pay the barber-surgeon to set it (6g)

outcome.text: He sets it badly and charges well. The hand works, mostly, and neither of you says which two fingers do not.

choices.label: Send to the next parish for a midwife

outcome.text: One comes over for the worst of it and charges by the mile. It is sensible, it works, and {{other.name}} understands exactly what it means.

events.title: THE APPRENTICE ASKS FOR A HEARTH
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A HAND ON THE WINTER ROAD

choices.label: Give her the hearth

outcome.text: Your main room becomes the place Swineford is born for the better part of a decade. It costs you firewood, sleep and privacy, and the parish burial list for infants gets noticeably shorter.

choices.label: Refuse. A birth is not a lesson

outcome.text: You say it plainly and she does not argue. She just looks at the fire until you leave. She learns anyway, on kitchen floors, in the dark.

choices.label: Give it, and charge for it

outcome.text: A penny a birth, payable by the household concerned. It is entirely reasonable and the entire village finds it repulsive.

events.title: THE HAND THAT WILL NOT WAIT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE APPRENTICE ASKS FOR A HEARTH

choices.label: Say it aloud in front of the apprentice

outcome.text: You name it in the room, once. She does not forgive you for a long time, and she stops going out alone in January.

choices.label: Keep it between the two of you

outcome.text: You say nothing to anyone and she knows you saw. It holds until the winter she cannot hide it, and then it does not hold at all.

choices.label: Quietly take the heavy work off her

outcome.text: You start turning up at the right moments with the right excuses. It costs you sleep and she pretends not to notice for both your sakes.

events.title: A HARD BIRTH AT CANDLEMAS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE HAND THAT WILL NOT WAIT

choices.label: Back the master

outcome.text: Forty years of hands against two. It goes badly for an hour and then it does not, and nobody afterwards can say which of them turned it.

choices.label: Back the apprentice

outcome.text: She does the thing the master called proud, and it works. The master leaves before dawn and does not attend another birth in that house.

choices.label: Put both out and send for the physician (8g)

outcome.text: He arrives at first light, charges a mark, and does almost exactly what the apprentice had proposed at midnight.

events.title: WHOSE HANDS SWINEFORD SENDS FOR
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Speak for the old hands

outcome.text: They send for the master, as they always have. She is grateful, she is slower than she was, and everyone agrees not to mention the second thing.

choices.label: Speak for the new

outcome.text: They send for the apprentice. The master hears about it the same afternoon, from someone who enjoyed telling her.

events.title: THE MARKS ON THE MOULD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Read the marks aloud for them

outcome.text: You go down before the pour and call the numbers. It becomes a habit neither of you ever names, and it lasts five years.

choices.label: Tell the guild wardens

outcome.text: The wardens are correct, thorough and merciless. The workshop keeps its licence and loses its commissions, which amounts to the same thing more slowly.

choices.label: Say nothing to anyone

outcome.text: You leave it alone. Somebody else will see it eventually, and you will remember that you saw it first.

events.title: THE CORRECTIONS MADE AT NIGHT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Look away

outcome.text: You go home. The bells keep ringing true and the wrong name keeps going on them, and everyone concerned has agreed to this.

choices.label: Make the master see it

outcome.text: You put both of them in front of the same mould in daylight. It is a bad hour and the workshop is better run afterwards.

choices.label: Tell the apprentice to sign his own work

outcome.text: He starts cutting his mark into the crown of each bell where only the founder would look. Within two years the wardens have noticed.

events.title: THE BELL THAT CRACKED ON THE THIRD PEAL
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Produce the bill of metal

outcome.text: You read the weights out in the churchyard in front of the wardens. The guild pays for the recast and does not forget who made them.

memory.note: You proved a guild sold bad tin and made them pay for the recast.

choices.label: Let the old eyes take the blame

outcome.text: The wardens are relieved, the parish is satisfied, and the workshop is finished. You are paid a mark for a silence nobody names as such.

choices.label: Pay for the recast yourself (12g)

outcome.text: Twelve shillings and no explanation offered to anyone. The parish gets its bell and spends a decade guessing why.

events.title: THE DEED ON THE BENCH
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE BELL THAT CRACKED ON THE THIRD PEAL

choices.label: Read it plainly, clause by clause

outcome.text: You read every line including the one about the moulds. They sign anyway, but they sign knowing, which was the only thing you could give them.

choices.label: Buy the foundry yourself (30g)

outcome.text: Thirty shillings, the moulds, the debts and the apprentice. The name over the door is now yours and half the parish thinks you circled it for years.

memory.note: You bought a failing bell foundry from the man who built it.

choices.label: Tell them to sign and take the pension

outcome.text: They sign. There is a clause about a chair by the fire and the right to watch the pours, and it is honoured until the second winter.

events.title: WHOSE NAME GOES ROUND THE SHOULDER
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: The old master’s name

outcome.text: It goes up with his mark on it and he is helped out to hear the first peal. He says it is a little flat. It is not.

choices.label: The apprentice’s name

outcome.text: His mark, on the crown, in daylight, at last. The master does not come to the ringing and everyone notices the empty place.

choices.label: Yours, for paying for it

outcome.text: Your name, round the shoulder, in letters a hand high. It is entirely accurate and it sounds worse every time the bell rings.

memory.note: You put your own name on a bell somebody else spent a life learning to cast.

events.title: THE CHALICE IS GONE FROM THE AUMBRY
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Ask them yourself, first

outcome.text: They say it was a lamb they were hiding from the reeve, and produce a lamb. The lamb is real. The timing is not.

choices.label: Raise the hue and cry

outcome.text: The whole tithing turns out, as the law requires, and finds nothing. {{other.name}} spends the night in the reeve’s outhouse on the strength of your word.

choices.label: Keep what you saw to yourself

outcome.text: You go home. Six people saw them come out of that door and you are the only one who has decided to be no help whatsoever.

events.title: A SLIVER OF GILT IN THE MARKET
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE CHALICE IS GONE FROM THE AUMBRY

choices.label: Trace where the pedlar got it

outcome.text: Three days of asking ends at a tinker who bought it at Stourbridge fair from a man he cannot describe. It proves nothing and unproves nothing.

choices.label: Buy the scrap and pocket it (3g)

outcome.text: Threepence and no questions asked. You now own the only piece of evidence in the parish. It sits in your purse for a month before you understand what you are carrying.

choices.label: Take it straight to the reeve

outcome.text: He puts it in the box with the writs and thanks you formally. The pedlar is arrested and is very obviously not the man anyone is looking for.

events.title: A NEW ROOF AND SEVERAL FAT HENS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A SLIVER OF GILT IN THE MARKET

choices.label: Count the hens aloud at the hallmote

outcome.text: You do the arithmetic in public: a roof, nine hens, and a labourer’s wage. The steward strikes the testimony and the witness leaves the parish before Advent.

choices.label: Offer him more to change it back (10g)

outcome.text: He takes it, changes his story a third time, and is now worth precisely nothing as a witness to anybody at all, yourself included.

memory.note: You paid a witness to change his testimony back.

choices.label: Let the new roof stand

outcome.text: You say nothing about the hens. The case bends round the bribe the way water bends round a stone, and everyone can see the shape of it.

events.title: THE REEVE AND THE ARCHDEACON DISAGREE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A NEW ROOF AND SEVERAL FAT HENS

choices.label: Back the reeve and the manor court

outcome.text: Secular justice, and quickly. The archdeacon writes a letter about jurisdiction that is still being quoted in that parish forty years later.

choices.label: Back the archdeacon

outcome.text: It goes to the church court, where the penalty is penance and the object comes before the person. The reeve does not speak to you until Lady Day twice over.

choices.label: Tell {{other.name}} to claim sanctuary

outcome.text: Forty days in the chancel, then abjure the realm and walk to the coast barefoot carrying a cross. It is not mercy. It is not the gallows either.

events.title: THE CHALICE COMES BACK IN A MEAL SACK
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE REEVE AND THE ARCHDEACON DISAGREE

choices.label: Declare the matter closed

outcome.text: You say it loudly and often until it becomes true. Three households never speak again, and the parish is content to call that a resolution.

choices.label: Keep asking who carried the sack

outcome.text: You ask for twelve months and get an answer nobody wanted. By then the parish had stopped wanting one and rather resents being given it.

events.title: THE SILVERSMITH’S CONFESSION
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE CHALICE COMES BACK IN A MEAL SACK

choices.label: Have the confession read in church

outcome.text: The parish learns it nearly hanged a neighbour over pewter under gilt. The churchwarden’s tomb is in the chancel and cannot be asked about it.

choices.label: Pay him for his silence (8g)

outcome.text: Eight shillings for his trouble and his quiet. The parish keeps its relic, its story and its grudges, and every one of them is false.

events.title: THE ACCOUNT READ BEFORE THE PARISH
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Stand and say your own part in it

outcome.text: You give your account including the parts that do you no credit at all. Two others follow you up. It is the closest the parish comes to a reckoning.

memory.note: You gave a full public account of your part in the chalice affair.

choices.label: Stay on the bench

outcome.text: You keep your seat. The reading ends, everyone files out, and the whole business settles into the parish like damp into a wall.

events.title: VENISON IN THE WRONG HOUSES
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Want no part of it

outcome.text: You say so plainly and are not asked twice. You are also not told anything, by anybody, for a very long time afterwards.

choices.label: Take a share of the meat

outcome.text: A shoulder, wrapped in sacking, left in your byre before dawn. Your household eats, and you are now inside something with no obvious door out.

choices.label: Warn the forester there is a gang

outcome.text: You tell him there is a gang without telling him who. Patrols double, the poaching stops for six weeks, and somebody works out where the warning came from.

events.title: A SNARE TAKES A FORESTER’S LEG
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Carry him in and pay the herb-wife (4g)

outcome.text: You get him to the village on a hurdle and he keeps the leg. He remembers who took the front end, which turns out to matter enormously.

choices.label: Go out at night and clear the snares

outcome.text: Fourteen snares in one night by moonlight. Nobody thanks you, both sides suspect you, and no forester loses a leg in that wood again.

choices.label: Be somewhere else entirely

outcome.text: You are seen at the alehouse from noon to dark by nine reliable witnesses, which is the most suspicious alibi in the history of Swineford.

events.title: A SHARE OF THE SILVER
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A SNARE TAKES A FORESTER’S LEG

choices.label: Take the silver and move the patrol

outcome.text: You send them the long way on a story about a broken hurdle. Six shillings arrive wrapped in cloth two days later.

memory.note: You were paid to divert the village patrol for poachers.

choices.label: Refuse, and tell them why

outcome.text: You tell them a leg is already open and the next thing opened will be a neck. They call you soft. Two of them privately agree with you.

choices.label: Take the silver and send the patrol anyway

outcome.text: Three of them are taken on the coppice road with your six shillings still in your purse. It is the cleverest thing you have ever done and you sleep badly for a decade.

events.title: THE APPROVER’S PARDON
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Stand surety for {{other.name}}

outcome.text: You pledge your own goods against their appearance. If they run you are ruined, and every man in that court does the arithmetic while you are still speaking.

choices.label: Petition the lord for a common fine instead

outcome.text: You argue that hanging four tenants costs the manor four tenants. The steward finds this persuasive in a way that justice had not been.

choices.label: Let the approver name whoever he names

outcome.text: He names sixteen people, two of whom were nowhere near the wood. Three hang. His pardon is honoured in full and he is gone by spring.

events.title: THE WOOD GOES QUIET
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Keep the buried stores moving

outcome.text: You shift salt meat between four byres for another three winters. It is a small crime conducted with enormous administrative care.

choices.label: Dig it up and end it

outcome.text: You burn what has gone over and return the rest. Two households go hungry in March who did not have to, and they know which choice did it.

events.title: THE NEW FORESTER OFFERS AN AMNESTY
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Give him the one who has already fled

outcome.text: You name a man who took ship at Boston two winters back. The forester writes it down, everyone knows exactly what has happened, and the amnesty holds.

choices.label: Let the village name nobody

outcome.text: Michaelmas passes in total silence. The amnesty lapses, the patrols double, and Swineford holds together in a way that costs it a great deal.

choices.label: Name who actually did it

outcome.text: You say the name in the open. The amnesty holds for everybody else, and you are the man who said it for the rest of your life.

events.title: WHEN THE DEER COME BACK TO THE COPPICE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE NEW FORESTER OFFERS AN AMNESTY

choices.label: Say the law kept the wood

outcome.text: You make the case for forest law to people whose grandparents cleared that coppice. It is a sound argument and it persuades nobody who is hungry.

choices.label: Petition for a common right of pannage

outcome.text: Not deer. Pigs, in the wood, in autumn, by right. It is a smaller thing to ask for, it is granted, and it feeds Swineford every October after.

memory.note: You won Swineford a standing right of pannage in the lord’s wood.

events.title: AN ALIBI THAT IS PARTLY TRUE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Swear to the whole night

outcome.text: You give the oath entire and they walk free. The half you invented sits in the court roll in a clerk’s beautiful hand for good.

choices.label: Swear only to the hours you had them

outcome.text: You give the court exactly what you know: not enough to clear them, not enough to hang them. Both sides find you useless and entirely honest.

choices.label: Refuse the oath entirely

outcome.text: You will not stand up at all. They find two oath-helpers elsewhere inside a day, neither of whom was anywhere near your hearth.

events.title: THE SECOND WITNESS IS TOO TIDY
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: AN ALIBI THAT IS PARTLY TRUE

choices.label: Ask him what the rain did that night

outcome.text: You ask in front of the steward. He answers with total confidence and gets it wrong, and the court goes very quiet indeed.

choices.label: Produce a tidier witness of your own

outcome.text: You find somebody willing to be equally certain of the opposite. The court now holds two immaculate lies and no means of choosing between them.

choices.label: Let the clean story stand

outcome.text: It stands, and it wins. It was the best-told story in the room, and that is what the room was always going to decide on.

events.title: THE CLERK STILL HAS THE FIRST DRAFT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE SECOND WITNESS IS TOO TIDY

choices.label: Buy the original (9g)

outcome.text: Nine shillings for one sheet of parchment that says something quite different from the roll. You are now a man who buys evidence.

choices.label: Report the clerk to the steward

outcome.text: He is dismissed inside the week and the roll stands uncorrected, because correcting it would mean admitting it was wrong. Justice, administratively.

choices.label: Tell him to hide it and say nothing

outcome.text: It goes into the church chest under the tithe books. It will surface in fifteen years at the worst possible moment. Neither of you says so, and both of you are counting on it.

memory.note: A rewritten testimony still exists, hidden in the church chest.

events.title: THE LIE WAS FOR SOMEBODY ELSE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE CLERK STILL HAS THE FIRST DRAFT

choices.label: Name the third person

outcome.text: You say it and the whole shape of the case turns over. The damage is exactly as large as promised, and it lands on people who had done nothing.

choices.label: Carry the name yourself

outcome.text: You carry it. It is heavier than you expected and gets no lighter, and the wrong person stays under a shadow for years because you are decent.

choices.label: Make {{other.name}} say it themselves

outcome.text: You give them a month, then you stop giving them months. They say it badly, to the wrong people, and it costs them everything it would have cost you.

events.title: THE WRONGED HOUSEHOLD ASKS FOR THE RECORD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE LIE WAS FOR SOMEBODY ELSE

choices.label: Get the roll corrected (6g)

outcome.text: Nineteen months, two petitions and a fee. One line struck and one line added, and the family read it aloud to each other every evening for a week.

memory.note: You got a false judgment struck from the manor roll years after the fact.

choices.label: Pay them instead (15g)

outcome.text: Fifteen shillings, and the record stands. They take it because they need it, and both parties understand precisely what has been bought.

choices.label: Tell them it is too late

outcome.text: It is too late, factually. They knew that when they asked, and the asking was the whole of the point.

events.title: NO HERO IN THE CORRECTED ROLL
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE WRONGED HOUSEHOLD ASKS FOR THE RECORD

choices.label: Read it aloud at the view

outcome.text: You read every name, including your own. Nobody enjoys it. It is entered in the roll as read, which is the only monument the business ever gets.

choices.label: File it in the chest unread

outcome.text: It goes in with the writs and the tithe books, entirely accurate and entirely unread for the rest of the century.

events.title: THE COPE-CHEST COMMISSION
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Promise Michaelmas and worry later

outcome.text: You give them the date they wanted. The alderman’s son is furious, the wardens are delighted, and you have nine months to become somebody who can do this.

memory.note: You promised a masterpiece by a date no honest craftsman could meet.

choices.label: Give them the honest date

outcome.text: You say Candlemas and explain about seasoning oak. They take it to the alderman’s son, who promises Michaelmas within the hour.

choices.label: Ask to share it with another shop

outcome.text: Two shops, one mark, half the fee. The wardens dislike the arrangement and cannot fault the reasoning.

events.title: THE OAK ARRIVES SPLIT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Take him before the guild court

outcome.text: You bring the carter, the tally and the six hours. He replaces the boards and adds your shop to a list he keeps of difficult customers.

choices.label: Swallow it and buy more oak (12g)

outcome.text: Twelve shillings out of your own purse and no argument in front of the apprentices. The work stays on time and the supplier does it again in spring.

choices.label: Work round the splits and say nothing

outcome.text: You hide two splits inside the carcase where nobody will look for thirty years. Somebody will look in thirty years.

memory.note: There are split boards concealed inside your masterpiece.

events.title: THE APPRENTICE HAS A BETTER JOINT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Cut it his way and say whose it is

outcome.text: You use the joint and tell the wardens whose idea it was. Your standing with the guild improves, and {{other.name}} trusts you with the next suggestion.

choices.label: Cut it his way and say nothing

outcome.text: You take the payment and the credit. {{other.name}} knows where the joint came from and loses trust in you; no journey is needed to carry that grievance.

memory.note: The joint your masterpiece is famous for was your apprentice’s idea.

choices.label: Cut it the way it has always been cut

outcome.text: Five weeks longer, the old joint, no argument with the wardens. It is the safe decision and the apprentice stops offering things.

events.title: THE PATRON WANTS IT CHEAPER
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE APPRENTICE HAS A BETTER JOINT

choices.label: Refuse and finish it properly

outcome.text: You finish it in oak at your own cost. The patron pays the reduced fee, tells everyone he commissioned it, and you are thirteen shillings poorer and correct.

choices.label: Give him exactly what he is paying for

outcome.text: Elm, paint, and a bill that matches. It looks well from six feet and you make certain the wardens know which decisions were his.

choices.label: Take it to the wardens

outcome.text: The guild rules a master may not be made to put his mark on elm. The patron pays in full, loudly, and never commissions anything in this town again.

events.title: THE UNVEILING AT THE GUILD HALL
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Tell the whole history of it

outcome.text: The oak, the splits, the joint, the elm, the apprentice. It is a very strange speech for an unveiling. They are still repeating it in that hall forty years later, and getting the ending wrong.

memory.note: You gave a full public account of how your masterpiece was really made.

choices.label: Accept the praise and go home

outcome.text: You bow, you are admired, and you leave early. The chest is beautiful and everything anybody says about it is slightly wrong.

events.title: FOUR CARTS TO STOURBRIDGE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Put in a full share (20g)

outcome.text: Twenty shillings into a common purse held by a man you have known nine years. The others put in the same and everyone shakes on it in the alehouse.

choices.label: Put in a quarter share and keep the rest

outcome.text: You take a small stake and a small risk, and {{other.name}} notes exactly how small before agreeing very pleasantly.

choices.label: Lend them the money at interest instead

outcome.text: You are not a partner, you are a creditor, and the difference will matter enormously in about nine months.

events.title: ONE CART GONE IN THE NIGHT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Say the obvious thing aloud

outcome.text: You put it to them in front of the other partners. They have an answer for the bales and no answer at all for the timing.

choices.label: Insist the loss is shared four ways

outcome.text: You argue it through half a night and win. Everyone loses the same amount and the partnership survives, slightly bent.

choices.label: Say nothing and start keeping notes

outcome.text: You write down dates, bales and names in a little book. By Candlemas you have a very complete picture and nobody knows you have it.

events.title: THE DRIVER COMES BACK
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: ONE CART GONE IN THE NIGHT

choices.label: Believe him and pay his wages

outcome.text: You pay him for the weeks he was gone. He works for you for eighteen years and never once mentions it, which is either gratitude or discipline.

choices.label: Ride to Huntingdon and check it

outcome.text: Four days and a lame horse. Half the story is true. That is the worst answer he could have brought back, and you have to act on it anyway.

choices.label: Hand him to the constable

outcome.text: He is held six weeks and released without charge. He does not come back to Swineford and his family stops speaking to yours entirely.

events.title: SAFE PASSAGE, MINUS ONE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Refuse and travel unescorted

outcome.text: You go without the escort and nobody is dropped. It costs you two more losses that season and the partnership never once discusses breaking up.

choices.label: Take the escort

outcome.text: The poorest partner is out by Lady Day. The roads are safe, the season is excellent, and there is now an empty chair at every meeting.

memory.note: You traded a partner for safe passage on the Cambridge road.

choices.label: Buy the poor partner’s share yourself (14g)

outcome.text: You buy him out at a fair price, take the escort, and hold his stake in your own name. It is generous, it is profitable, and it is not the same as loyalty.

events.title: WHAT COMES BACK DOWN THE ROAD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Renew the partnership for another season

outcome.text: The same four names, or the three that are left. They sign again, which after this year is a considerably more serious thing than it was.

choices.label: Dissolve it and trade alone

outcome.text: You divide the purse on the table and shake hands. It is amicable, it is final, and you are considerably richer and slower for the next ten years.

events.title: HOURS BEYOND THE ORDINANCE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Back the apprentices openly

outcome.text: You put your name to their complaint. Two masters stop sending you work the same week and the apprentices remember it for thirty years.

choices.label: Read the ordinance to both sides

outcome.text: You find the clause, copy it, and nail it to three shop doors. Nobody can claim not to know now. That was the point, and it costs you three friendly shops by Whitsun.

choices.label: Keep out of it

outcome.text: It is not your shop and not your quarrel. It becomes your quarrel by Candlemas, on worse terms.

events.title: A CONTRACT OFFERED QUIETLY
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Take the contracts

outcome.text: The work is genuinely good and the silence is genuinely purchased. Both facts are true at once and only one of them is discussed.

memory.note: You were paid in commissions to stop speaking for the apprentices.

choices.label: Refuse, and say what was offered

outcome.text: You describe the offer word for word at the next guild meeting. The master denies it, everyone believes you, and nothing whatsoever is done about it.

choices.label: Take the contracts and speak anyway

outcome.text: You take the work and go on saying exactly what you said before. He cannot withdraw it without admitting what it was for, and you both know it.

events.title: TOOLS DOWN IN THREE SHOPS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Get both sides in one room

outcome.text: Four hours, one barrel, and a written agreement about bells. It holds because everybody had to say their terms out loud in front of the other side.

choices.label: Finish the urgent orders yourself

outcome.text: You work nine days straight and deliver the coffin on time. The masters are grateful and the apprentices watch you undercut the only pressure they had.

choices.label: Feed the apprentices out of your own stores

outcome.text: Bread and pottage for nine young men for three weeks. It empties your lardarium and it is the reason the strike lasts long enough to win anything.

events.title: ONE NAME OR ALL OF THEM
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Put your own name on it instead

outcome.text: You sign as the instigator. You are barred from guild work for two years and nine apprentices keep their indentures, and everybody in the trade knows why.

memory.note: You were struck off the guild register to save nine apprentices.

choices.label: Let {{other.name}} take it

outcome.text: They sign, they are expelled, and they leave for Bristol in April. The eight who stayed are careful never to say the name out loud again.

choices.label: Tell the guild to strike off all fifteen

outcome.text: You point out that nine expelled apprentices is nine shops without hands in July. The threat is quietly withdrawn and never referred to again.

events.title: THE NEW CHARTER READ ALOUD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: ONE NAME OR ALL OF THEM

choices.label: Put your seal to it

outcome.text: You seal it with the rest. It is worse than what was asked for and enormously better than what there was, and it outlives everyone in the room.

choices.label: Refuse to seal it

outcome.text: You say it gives back less than it took and decline. The charter passes without you, and in eight years somebody quotes your refusal in a very different argument.

events.title: THE BUSHEL THAT WEIGHS SHORT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Carry both measures to the market house

outcome.text: You set them side by side in front of thirty people. The rector’s bushel is short by better than a quart and there is nothing anybody can say about it.

choices.label: Have a quiet word with the rector

outcome.text: He is embarrassed, blames a servant, and the measure is corrected before Lady Day without one word said in public. Nobody is punished and everybody eats.

choices.label: Pay the tithe as measured

outcome.text: You give the tenth as demanded and say nothing. Four households follow your example. The rector had been waiting all morning for exactly that.

events.title: THE GRANARY OPENS, WITH CONDITIONS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Sign first and openly

outcome.text: You put your name at the head of the roll so that poorer households do not have to be the first to bend. It costs you nothing but the sight of your own signature.

choices.label: Refuse to sign and go hungry

outcome.text: You walk out past the grain. Nine households sign, two do not, and the parish spends the rest of the winter deciding which of you was the fool.

choices.label: Buy grain elsewhere and share it out (12g)

outcome.text: Twelve shillings of Cambridge wheat, distributed from your own yard with no roll and no clerk. The rector’s granary stays remarkably full.

events.title: THE BISHOP’S CLERK COMES TO COUNT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Give him the accounts, all of them

outcome.text: You hand over every roll including the ones that embarrass the parish. He reads for two days and writes down four names, none of them about arithmetic.

choices.label: Coach the parish on what to say

outcome.text: You spend an evening in the alehouse making sure everybody tells the same true story. He finds nothing and reports the parish sullen. A parish with nothing to hide does not close ranks.

choices.label: Give him the name he came for

outcome.text: You name the churchwarden who has been selling tithe hay on the side. It is entirely true, it satisfies the clerk completely, and it ends a family in this parish.

events.title: THE NEXT COLLECTION REFUSED
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE BISHOP’S CLERK COMES TO COUNT

choices.label: Broker a modus: a fixed sum in place of the tenth

outcome.text: A money payment, fixed by agreement, entered in the book. Both sides lose the argument and gain a number, which is what a settlement is.

memory.note: You settled the tithe dispute with a fixed money payment.

choices.label: Hold the refusal

outcome.text: The refusal hardens religious tension and lowers public order. Your standing with the Commons rises, while the rector’s authority remains a matter for the church rather than a victory you can announce.

choices.label: Pay in full and break the refusal

outcome.text: You pay the whole tenth on the first day. The refusal collapses within a week and the parish is very clear about who collapsed it.

events.title: THE TITHE AS IT IS NOW TAKEN
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Have the terms read out every year

outcome.text: You get it entered that the modus is to be read aloud each Lady Day. It is read for a hundred and forty years, long after nobody remembers why.

choices.label: Let it lie in the book

outcome.text: It goes into the parish chest. Within a generation both sides are quoting it inaccurately and with total confidence.

events.title: THE COMMISSION OF ARRAY
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Draw up an honest assessment

outcome.text: You go house by house with the tax roll and set what each can actually bear. It takes nine days and everybody hates the number and pays it.

choices.label: Plead the village down

outcome.text: You take the murrain, the flood and the burial list to the commissioners in person. They cut the assessment by a third and mark Swineford as difficult.

choices.label: Offer money instead of men (20g)

outcome.text: You raise twenty shillings and buy the village out of the array. No Swineford man marches, and the money is gone in a way the grain would not have been.

events.title: NAMES OFF THE MUSTER ROLL
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Put the four names back

outcome.text: You write them in again in front of the constable. Two of the five never speak to you again and the roll is honest for the first time in nineteen years.

choices.label: Take a payment to leave your own name off (10g)

outcome.text: Ten shillings changes hands and your name is not read out. It is precisely what the five households did, and you were a great deal angrier about it in March.

memory.note: You paid to keep your own name off the muster roll.

choices.label: Read the roll as it stands

outcome.text: You read out what is written. Five men who should be marching are at home, and the rest of the column noticed exactly which five.

events.title: LOTS DRAWN IN FRONT OF THE HALL
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Hold the drawing, and draw first

outcome.text: You put your own hand in the bag before anybody else. You draw a short straw and it is the single most useful thing you do all year.

memory.note: You drew a lot for the levy before anyone else and lost.

choices.label: Let the steward choose the men

outcome.text: He picks twelve and the retainers stay against the wall. The fourteen are the sixteen you would have expected, and the hall empties in complete silence.

choices.label: Take the place of a man with children

outcome.text: You march in place of a father of four. His wife brings your household bread for six years and never explains why to anybody who asks.

events.title: THE ESCHEATOR ASKS ABOUT THE NUMBERS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: LOTS DRAWN IN FRONT OF THE HALL

choices.label: Give him the true figures

outcome.text: You lay out what the village actually has. The assessment goes up by a fifth, permanently, and no one is ever hanged for it.

choices.label: Stand by the returns as filed

outcome.text: Every man in the village tells him the same figure. He does not believe a word of it and cannot prove otherwise, and he says so in writing.

choices.label: Blame the dead reeve

outcome.text: You put it all on a man buried three years ago who cannot argue. The officer accepts it because it is convenient, and his widow hears about it by Friday.

events.title: THE LEVY MARCHES OUT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE ESCHEATOR ASKS ABOUT THE NUMBERS

choices.label: Say plainly how it was shared

outcome.text: You give the full account at the view: who paid, who marched, who bought their way clear. It is entered in the roll and read at every array afterwards.

choices.label: Let the village forget it

outcome.text: Nobody says anything. By the next array the story has quietly rearranged itself so that everyone behaved rather better than they did.

events.title: TWO SEALS, ONE MATRIX
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Seize the matrix and lock it in the chest

outcome.text: You take it, put it under three keys held by three men, and no order goes out for twenty days. The town is furious and the forgery stops dead.

choices.label: Recognise one officer and ignore the other

outcome.text: You pick the one who is more likely to win and start honouring his orders. Half the guild does the same and the other half does the opposite.

choices.label: Take orders from whichever suits you

outcome.text: For a season you have written authority for absolutely anything you care to do. It is extremely profitable and it cannot possibly last.

events.title: THE MERCHANTS STOP TAKING SWINEFORD PAPER
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Ride to Lynn and vouch for the wool yourself

outcome.text: You stand surety in person for three carts on nothing but your own name. It works, it takes nine days, and your name is worth more at Lynn afterwards than it is at home.

choices.label: Sell the wool at whatever it fetches

outcome.text: It goes for two-thirds and the charges eat a third of that. Everybody is paid something and nobody is paid enough.

choices.label: Leave it on the wharf and wait them out

outcome.text: Eight weeks of charges and the wool is worth less than the storage. The dispute is settled the following spring, far too late for that wool.

events.title: A CHARTER FRAGMENT IN A FAMILY CHEST
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE MERCHANTS STOP TAKING SWINEFORD PAPER

choices.label: Produce it before both councils

outcome.text: It is read out and it changes the argument completely. Both factions immediately begin claiming they always knew about it.

choices.label: Sell it to the borough (25g)

outcome.text: The borough pays well for a document that ceases to exist the moment it is paid for. You are twenty-five shillings richer and the guild is smaller forever.

memory.note: You sold a guild charter to the borough and it was never seen again.

choices.label: Go looking for the other half

outcome.text: Two years of chests, priories and one very unhelpful archdeacon. You never find it, and everybody now knows there is half a charter somewhere.

events.title: THE CROWN OFFERS RECOGNITION
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A CHARTER FRAGMENT IN A FAMILY CHEST

choices.label: Take the recognition and the debt

outcome.text: Sealed by Whitsun. The guild is lawful, undisputed, and paying the Crown eight marks a year in 1390 for a quarrel settled in 1352.

choices.label: Refuse and settle it yourselves

outcome.text: Four more years of argument, two ruined merchants, and a settlement written by the guild for the guild that costs it nothing annually forever.

choices.label: Go to the borough instead

outcome.text: The borough will recognise the guild for less money and considerably more interference. It is a smaller collar and it is a collar.

events.title: ONE SEAL RETURNS TO THE HALL
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Have the whole history written into the book

outcome.text: Four pages, both factions, the wool on the wharf, the charter. It is read to every new warden at their swearing-in for two hundred years.

choices.label: Turn the key and get back to trade

outcome.text: Nobody writes it down. Inside a generation the guild is confidently telling a version in which nothing much went wrong at all.

events.title: THE THATCH WILL NOT SEE ANOTHER WINTER
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Pay the thatcher properly (9g)

outcome.text: Nine shillings, three days, and new reed over the whole hearth end. It is the correct decision and it empties the purse before winter.

choices.label: Patch it yourself with what you have

outcome.text: Two days on the roof with old reed and borrowed spars. It will hold. It will hold in the way that things hold when you are the one who fixed them.

choices.label: Move the bed and leave it

outcome.text: You shift the beds to the dry end and put a pot under the wet one. Everybody sleeps in one room until March and nobody says a word about it.

events.title: ROT UNDER A RECENT REPAIR
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE THATCH WILL NOT SEE ANOTHER WINTER

choices.label: Find out who did it and make him pay

outcome.text: It was the man who is now the churchwarden. He pays for the beam rather than have it discussed, and he is never civil to you again.

choices.label: Buy the beam and say nothing (16g)

outcome.text: Sixteen shillings for oak and two men to raise it. The house will stand for two hundred years and nobody will ever know why it needed to.

choices.label: Prop it and hope

outcome.text: A post under the beam and a prayer. It holds for thirteen years. Nobody who signed it expected five.

memory.note: The main beam of your house is rotten and propped.

events.title: RAIN IN THE BEDDING
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Give up your own place by the fire

outcome.text: You sleep by the door for six weeks and take a cough that lasts into April. The other household never forgets which side of the room you chose.

choices.label: Draw lots for it each week

outcome.text: A rota, drawn publicly, changed every Sunday. It is fair, everybody grumbles about it, and there is not one serious quarrel all winter.

choices.label: Keep your place; it is your roof

outcome.text: It is your roof, factually. You are warm all winter and the arrangement is discussed in the lane for considerably longer than the winter lasts.

events.title: THE TIMBER GOES TO THE LORD’S GRANARY
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Petition the steward at the hallmote

outcome.text: You cite the custom of the manor on timber-right for repairs. It is real, and he had plainly assumed nobody in Swineford could quote it. Half the oak comes back.

memory.note: You quoted manorial custom at the steward and got your timber back.

choices.label: Buy timber from the next parish (18g)

outcome.text: Eighteen shillings and a two-day haul. The roof is finished a fortnight before Martinmas and the purse is emptier than it has been in years.

choices.label: Take what you need off the granary pile at night

outcome.text: Three spars, moved after dark, from a pile of forty. Nobody counts them and you spend the next five years expecting somebody to.

events.title: THE SACKS COME UP LIGHT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Set traps and count every sack weekly

outcome.text: You catch nine rats and establish, by arithmetic, that the rats account for about a third of it. The other two-thirds have a key.

choices.label: Blame the rats and get a better cat

outcome.text: A good mouser from the mill, fed on scraps, worth every one of them. The loss halves and the half that remains keeps quietly happening.

choices.label: Sit in the granary all night

outcome.text: Four nights in the cold before you see who has the key. You know, now, and knowing turns out to be considerably harder than not knowing was.

events.title: A CHILD CARRYING FLOUR AT DUSK
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Fill the coat properly and send them on

outcome.text: You put a full measure in and walk them to the door yourself. Four households know by morning and two of them start doing the same.

choices.label: Take the child to the reeve

outcome.text: The reeve is obliged to record it and does so with visible reluctance. The child is amerced twopence their family cannot pay, and everyone involved feels precisely as bad as they should.

choices.label: Take the flour back and say nothing

outcome.text: The child goes home with an empty coat. Nothing is recorded, nothing is said, and nothing is eaten in that house until Friday.

events.title: DAMP GRAIN BEHIND A NEW WALL
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A CHILD CARRYING FLOUR AT DUSK

choices.label: Break the wall out and salvage what is sound

outcome.text: Two days of shovelling and sorting in a stench that gets into your clothes. You save rather more than anyone expected and lose the rest.

choices.label: Sell the doubtful sacks at market

outcome.text: It goes at a good price to a buyer three villages off who does not open the sacks in your presence. You are paid and you are not proud of it.
