memory.note: You sold spoiled grain at market to a buyer three villages away.

choices.label: Burn the lot in the yard

outcome.text: A quarter of the winter store, on a fire, in front of the household. Nobody in Swineford is poisoned that year and nobody in your house forgives you until March.

events.title: THE RECKONING AT WINTER’S END
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: DAMP GRAIN BEHIND A NEW WALL

choices.label: Say all four numbers out loud

outcome.text: You read the whole account to the household including the sharing and the theft. It is a difficult evening and the granary is never short again.

choices.label: Say the two that are easy

outcome.text: Eaten and spoiled. The other two numbers stay in your head, where they go on being true and go on being expensive.

events.title: SPARKS ON YOUR OWN THATCH
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Wet your own roof first

outcome.text: Every bucket in the house onto your own thatch. Your roof survives, theirs does not, and both of those facts are noted in the lane.

choices.label: Pull the burning roof down with hooks

outcome.text: You get the fire-hooks off the church wall and drag the whole roof into the lane. It is the right answer, it saves the row, and it takes the skin off your hands.

choices.label: Get the people out and let it burn

outcome.text: Three children and an old man out through the smoke, and the row goes up behind you. Everyone lives. Nothing else does.

events.title: THREE HOUSEHOLDS, TWO ROOMS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Take a household into your own room

outcome.text: Six people where six lived. The food goes twice as fast, nobody sleeps well, and not one of them is out of doors when the frost comes.

choices.label: Let out your byre at a fair rent

outcome.text: A penny a week for the byre, which is honest, sheltered and cold. They take it and they pay it and something between you never quite comes back.

choices.label: Get the church house opened for them

outcome.text: You badger the churchwardens until they open the church house, which has stood empty for six years for no reason anybody can defend.

events.title: A STRONGBOX IN THE ASHES
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Have it cried in church three Sundays

outcome.text: Three Sundays and no claimant. It goes to the parish chest for the rebuilding, lawfully, and everybody knows you could have kept it.

choices.label: Keep it

outcome.text: Nine shillings and a ring you never wear. Whoever it belonged to knows it was in that row, and one day may work out who did the raking.

choices.label: Split it between the three households

outcome.text: Three shillings and eightpence each and the ring drawn for. It is not lawful and nobody in that lane ever raises the point.

events.title: WHO GETS A ROOF FIRST
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: The poorest family first

outcome.text: They are under a roof by Martinmas. The other two wait until spring and say, mostly, that it was right, and mean it, mostly.

memory.note: You had the poorest burnt-out family roofed before the others.

choices.label: Whoever can pay toward the timber

outcome.text: The family that can find twelve shillings is roofed first, which is how it is normally done and is the reason the poorest family is the poorest family.

choices.label: Split the timber three ways and rough-roof all three

outcome.text: Three bad roofs instead of one good one. All three leak, all three stand, and nobody spends the winter in somebody else’s byre.

events.title: A RAIN-SOAKED MAP FOR FOURPENCE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Dry it out and read it properly

outcome.text: Three days over a low fire and most of it comes back. It is a genuine survey, badly copied, of something under the mere field.

choices.label: Buy it off {{other.name}} for a shilling

outcome.text: A shilling for fourpence of vellum. They take it happily and tell nine people about the profit. By Sunday the whole village knows there is a map.

choices.label: Tell them to burn it

outcome.text: Maps of things under boundary stones have a way of becoming inquests. They do not burn it. They put it somewhere you cannot find it.

events.title: BONES, TOOLS, AND A NEWER FOOTPRINT
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Seal it up again and tell the priest

outcome.text: The priest has it consecrated and blessed and firmly closed. He also asks, twice, who else had been down there, and you do not have an answer.

choices.label: Take the tools

outcome.text: Five iron pieces of a make no smith in the shire recognises. They are worth money to the right person and questions to everybody else.

choices.label: Go looking for whose boot it was

outcome.text: You measure it against every man in Swineford over the next month, entirely without explaining why. You find the match and you very much wish you had not.

events.title: THE MISSING CORNER IN THE REEVE’S ARCHIVE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: BONES, TOOLS, AND A NEWER FOOTPRINT

choices.label: Ask the reeve about it directly

outcome.text: He goes grey, says it was there when he came, and is entirely honest about that. He is much less honest about why he never mentioned it.

choices.label: Take the corner out of the chest

outcome.text: You now have the whole map and a theft from the manor archive on your conscience and, potentially, on the record.

choices.label: Trace the family that stopped existing

outcome.text: Ninety years of rolls and one very reluctant priory. They did not die out. They were dispossessed, and there are descendants, and they are three miles away.

memory.note: You found living descendants of a family dispossessed ninety years ago.

events.title: THE PATH ENDS UNDER A LIVING HOUSE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE MISSING CORNER IN THE REEVE’S ARCHIVE

choices.label: Tell the family what is under their floor

outcome.text: You tell them everything and let them decide. They decide to do nothing at all, and they sleep on it for another forty years, and they are grateful you asked.

choices.label: Dig at night from the byre side

outcome.text: Ten nights of quiet digging under somebody else’s floor. You find it. Whatever it is worth, you can never once explain how you came by it.

memory.note: You dug treasure out from under a sleeping family’s house.

choices.label: Declare it as treasure trove

outcome.text: You report it to the coroner as the law requires. The Crown takes the whole of it, you are thanked in writing, and the family gets the hole in their floor filled in.

events.title: A RELIQUARY AND A LARGE CLAIM
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Look at the reliquary rather than the bone

outcome.text: The enamel is Limoges work and eighty years old at least. Whatever is inside it, the box is real and the box is worth more than the parish makes in a year.

choices.label: Take it to the rector at once

outcome.text: He is cautious, delighted, and writing to the bishop before you are out of the door. It is out of your hands inside a week.

choices.label: Tell them to keep it in a box and say nothing

outcome.text: It goes under a floorboard. It stays there for nine years and then somebody’s child finds it, at the worst possible moment, in front of a visiting archdeacon.

events.title: PILGRIMS ON THE SWINEFORD ROAD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A RELIQUARY AND A LARGE CLAIM

choices.label: Sell them beds, bread and badges

outcome.text: Swineford makes more in one summer than in the four years before it. It also buries nine people in August who came in already coughing.

choices.label: Limit them to the churchyard and the well

outcome.text: You organise where they sleep, where they wash and where they do not go. It makes half the money and buries nobody, and the alehouse never forgives you.

choices.label: Ask the miracle-witnesses some questions

outcome.text: Of six miracles, eight are weather, two are recovery from things people recover from, and one is genuinely unaccountable. You write all seven down anyway.

events.title: THE SCHOLAR WILL NOT SPEAK OF THE BONE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Follow him to the gate and press him

outcome.text: He tells you, quietly, that it is a sheep’s. He also tells you he will deny having said so, and that he is not the first man to have found this out.

memory.note: A scholar told you privately that the parish relic is a sheep bone.

choices.label: Let him go and publish the certificate

outcome.text: The certificate says the reliquary is genuine. That is true, and it is not what anybody who reads it will think it says.

choices.label: Ask him the question in front of the parish

outcome.text: He gives a beautiful eight-minute answer about the limits of scholarly method that says nothing whatsoever, and the parish is entirely satisfied by it.

events.title: TWO CHURCHES AND AN ARMED GUARD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE SCHOLAR WILL NOT SPEAK OF THE BONE

choices.label: Give it to whichever house will take it furthest away

outcome.text: It goes to the cathedral with an escort. The pilgrims follow it inside a twelvemonth and Swineford goes back to being a village with a wet field.

choices.label: Fight to keep it in the parish

outcome.text: Two years of proctors and letters and one shoving match in the nave. Swineford keeps it, keeps the trade, and keeps the armed men in the porch indefinitely.

choices.label: Put the offerings to the poor and say so loudly

outcome.text: Every penny in the box goes to the burnt-out and the widowed, published at the church door each quarter. Both claimant houses lose interest remarkably quickly.

memory.note: You put every penny of the relic offerings to Swineford’s poor, publicly.

events.title: THE CHILD WHO DESCRIBED THE FLOOD
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Write down exactly what was said and when

outcome.text: You take it in the child’s own words with the date and two witnesses. It is either the most valuable page in the parish or a piece of paper.

choices.label: Tell the priest at once

outcome.text: He is far more worried than impressed and says three things about discernment of spirits that the family does not understand and does not like.

choices.label: Call it a coincidence, loudly

outcome.text: You say the obvious thing about a wet spring and a low causeway. Half the lane agrees with you and the other half remembers, in detail, that you said it.

events.title: A SECOND DREAM NAMES SOMETHING PRIVATE
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: THE CHILD WHO DESCRIBED THE FLOOD

choices.label: Get the child out of the lane for a while

outcome.text: You send them to kin at Barton for the summer. The household concerned calms down, and the two who are protecting the secret work out exactly who moved the child.

choices.label: Ask the child how they knew

outcome.text: They say a woman told them, and describe somebody who has been dead since before they were born, accurately, including the limp.

choices.label: Use what the child said

outcome.text: You go to the household concerned and let them understand that you know. They are extremely accommodating from that day and they hate you for the rest of their lives.

memory.note: You used a child’s vision to blackmail a household.

events.title: CROWDS AT THE DOOR ASKING ABOUT HARVESTS
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: A SECOND DREAM NAMES SOMETHING PRIVATE

choices.label: Shut the door and stand in front of it

outcome.text: You turn away sixty people in a month, some of them angry and more of them desperate. The child sleeps properly for the first time since Lady Day.

choices.label: Let them come, but on your terms

outcome.text: You limit the questioning to one morning a week and refuse payment. Religious tension still rises a little; the smaller gathering is a boundary, not proof that the child is no longer frightened.

choices.label: Charge a penny a question

outcome.text: You collect twenty gold and increase household wealth. Existing debts are not erased by the takings, and {{other.name}} trusts you less for pricing the frightened child’s answers.

events.title: A DREAM THAT SUITS NOBODY
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

hasWorldMemoryType: CROWDS AT THE DOOR ASKING ABOUT HARVESTS

choices.label: Say you believe the child

outcome.text: You say it in the nave with both of them present. It costs you the rector’s goodwill, the steward’s goodwill, and absolutely nothing that you needed.

choices.label: Say the child is ill and needs quiet

outcome.text: It is the answer that ends the matter without anybody being burned or believed. The child is left alone and grows up ordinary, which was possibly the point.

choices.label: Side with the rector

outcome.text: You say what the rector needs said. The dream is condemned from the pulpit, the family leaves the parish by spring, and you are on very good terms with the church.

events.title: THE DREAMER COMES BACK GROWN
events.text: state=>render(state,beat.text)

choices.label: Tell them what actually happened

outcome.text: The flood, the secret, the crowds, the penny a question, what you did about each. They listen the whole way through and thank you, and they do not stay.

choices.label: Tell them the version the parish tells

outcome.text: It is a better story than the truth and considerably kinder to everybody in it, including you. They know it is not right and do not press.

events.title: THE COMMON HEDGE
events.text: {{other.name}} moves a boundary hedge while you organise the village work. By dusk two households are shouting over a strip of common ground and everyone expects you to decide whether this was theft or a mistake.

choices.label: Measure the old boundary

outcome.text: You find the old stones beneath the nettles and put the hedge back where memory and mud agree it belongs.

choices.label: Back {{other.name}}

outcome.text: You declare the moved hedge reasonable. {{other.name}} remembers the loyalty; the other household remembers everything else.

choices.label: Put it before the reeve

outcome.text: The reeve restores the boundary, fines both households for wasting his morning, and thanks you by assigning next month’s ditch work.

events.title: THE MASTERS’ PRICE
events.text: {{other.name}} closes the guild-room door and lays out a simple proposal: every workshop will raise its prices together, and anyone who refuses will find supplies strangely unavailable.

choices.label: Refuse the pact

outcome.text: You keep your prices honest. Customers crowd your door, while three suppliers suddenly forget the road to your workshop.

choices.label: Join them

outcome.text: The new prices hold. Your purse grows heavier and the poorest customers begin repairing old things instead of buying yours.

choices.label: Demand a poor rate

outcome.text: You secure one price for noble orders and another for neighbours who arrive with mended sleeves. Nobody loves it, which is how you know it is a bargain.

events.title: WHAT WAS SAID IN DARKNESS
events.text: The voice behind the screen is {{other.name}}’s. The confession concerns a plan that may hurt innocent people, but repeating it would break the seal that made the truth possible.

choices.label: Keep the seal

outcome.text: You say nothing. {{other.name}} leaves knowing the secret is safe, while you spend the night wondering who may pay for that safety.

choices.label: Warn the threatened household
choices.hint: Prevent harm without naming the source

outcome.text: You deliver a warning wrapped in enough scripture to conceal its origin. The household prepares, and {{other.name}} watches you more carefully afterward.

choices.label: Report it openly

outcome.text: You name the danger and its source. The plan dies immediately, along with every honest confession likely to reach you for years.

events.title: THE FORBIDDEN GLOSS
events.text: {{other.name}} recognises the hand in a censored margin: a respected scholar condemned years ago. The erased argument is persuasive, useful, and dangerous to possess.

choices.label: Copy it in secret

outcome.text: You hide the argument inside an innocent commentary where a careful reader may recover it. Knowledge survives by learning to whisper.

memory.note: You preserved a forbidden argument inside an innocent manuscript.

choices.label: Finish the erasure
choices.hint: Protect the house; destroy the passage

outcome.text: Fresh scraping removes the last readable words. The manuscript is safe, the scriptorium is safe, and the thought exists only in your memory.

choices.label: Put it before the prior

outcome.text: The prior reads the passage twice, locks the book away, and orders that no punishment follow. Half the house calls that mercy and half calls it fear.

events.title: ONE SPEAR MISSING
events.text: At roll call {{other.name}} is absent. You find them behind the tithe barn, shaking, with a widowed parent at home and no intention of marching toward a war they do not understand.

choices.label: Mark them sick

outcome.text: A fever appears in the roll beside {{other.name}}’s name. Their household keeps its last able pair of hands and your captain begins counting more carefully.

choices.label: Talk them back into line

outcome.text: You promise to place them in the rear rank and bring them home if promises survive battle. They return because you asked, not because the levy did.

choices.label: Make an example of them

outcome.text: {{other.name}} is bound before the whole levy. Nobody else deserts, and nobody meets your eye during the march.

events.title: TWO CLAIMS, ONE MEADOW
events.text: {{other.name}} arrives with a charter, while another household arrives with three generations of grazing and no parchment at all. Both claims are convincing. The meadow is not large enough to satisfy either.

choices.label: Uphold the old custom

outcome.text: The grazing continues as it always has. {{other.name}} folds the charter very carefully and begins asking who else doubts written law.

choices.label: Uphold the charter

outcome.text: The seal wins. The meadow changes hands before sunset, and an old household begins selling the animals it can no longer graze.

choices.label: Divide the grazing rights

outcome.text: You mark alternate grazing weeks. Both sides call it impossible and both follow the schedule once they think nobody is watching.

events.title: THE EMPTY GRANARIES
events.text: The council’s figures agree on one fact: there is not enough grain for the army, the towns, and the winter poor. {{other.name}} asks which promise should be broken first.

choices.label: Feed the poorest first

outcome.text: Army stores are opened at the church doors. The hungry eat, the captains protest, and every mother in the queue learns whose order did it.

choices.label: Keep the army supplied

outcome.text: The military granaries remain sealed. The levy will march well-fed past villages that are not.

choices.label: Buy foreign grain

outcome.text: Merchants empty your treasury and fill the quays. It is an undignified solution to hunger, which remains preferable to a dignified famine.

events.title: THE MISSING SHARE
events.text: The gang’s purse is light by twelve gold. {{other.name}} had the key, denies taking it, and offers three different explanations before anyone asks for one.

choices.label: Recover it quietly

outcome.text: You find six gold beneath a floorboard and accept that the other six purchased silence. The gang survives with a new lock and an old suspicion.

choices.label: Expel {{other.name}}

outcome.text: {{other.name}} leaves without the purse and with every name, route, and hiding place the gang has used this year.

choices.label: Forgive the debt once

outcome.text: You name the theft, forgive it, and make {{other.name}} earn the money back beside you. Half the gang calls it weakness; the other half would now follow you anywhere.

events.title: THE WRONG SEAT
events.text: Before the first loaf is cut, {{other.name}} objects to where you have seated them. The complaint is supposedly about precedence and unmistakably about an insult from twelve years ago.

choices.label: Move the whole table

outcome.text: Benches scrape, children carry trenchers, and everyone moves one place. The ancient insult survives but tonight’s supper does too.

choices.label: Give {{other.name}} the high seat
choices.hint: Win one ally; slight the rest

outcome.text: {{other.name}} receives the high seat and becomes gracious at once. Three other guests become historians.

choices.label: Make the quarrel ridiculous

success.text: You retell the old insult until even its victim laughs. By pudding, the rival households are correcting your version together.

failure.text: Your joke lands like a brick in a baptismal font. {{other.name}} leaves before supper and takes two cousins with them.

events.title: THE PARISH HEARS A NAME
events.text: Your sermon against hidden sin is still echoing when someone in the nave points at {{other.name}}. The congregation turns as one body and waits for you to confirm an accusation you never made.

choices.label: Preach mercy immediately

outcome.text: You turn the next half-hour toward mercy until pointing fingers lower. {{other.name}} remains shaken, but the parish leaves with nobody to punish.

choices.label: Let the accusation stand

outcome.text: You do not speak the name, but you do not deny it. By evening {{other.name}}’s door bears a mark in chalk and the collection plate is unusually heavy.

choices.label: Admit the sermon went too far

outcome.text: You say plainly that zeal outran wisdom. A few parishioners sneer, more look relieved, and {{other.name}} stays to help extinguish the candles.

events.title: JUDGMENT BEFORE SWINEFORD
events.text: function hearingText(s){const charges=hearingCharges(s),l=s.world.characters[s.playerCharacterId].legalState;if(!charges.length)return"No unresolved charge remains in this sitting. Earlier findings stay on record; there is no new offence to punish.";const first=charges[0],witnesses=[...new Set(charges.flatMap(c=>c.witnessIds))].map(id=>s.world.characters[id]).filter(Boolean);const victims=[...new Set(charges.flatMap(c=>c.victimIds))].map(id=>s.world.characters[id]?.name).filter(Boolean);return`${CASE_OPENINGS[offenceKind(first.offence)]} The sitting covers ${charges.map(c=>c.offence).join("; ")}. Evidence: ${Math.max(...charges.map(c=>c.evidence))}/100.${victims.length?` Injured households: ${victims.join(", ")}.`:""}${witnesses.length?` Witnesses: ${witnesses.map(c=>`${c.name}${c.alive?"":" (recorded testimony)"}`).join(", ")}.`:" No named witness is recorded."} ${l?.charges.filter(c=>c.verdict==="convicted").length??0} prior convictions are on record. Each charge will receive a finding; this sitting imposes one combined sentence.`}

choices.label: Answer every charge

success.text: The reeve dismisses the charges and reminds the spectators that their certainty is not evidence. Several look annoyed at having been so certain for nothing.

failure.text: The reeve gives sentence. The spectators stop offering advice now that none of them has to serve it.

choices.label: Confess and seek mercy (restitution up to 12g)

outcome.text: You admit the acts without the grand explanation. The reeve reduces the sentence; the neighbours look disappointed to have come so far for such a short performance.

choices.label: Purchase favourable testimony (20g; bribery risk)

success.text: The purchased testimony changes the finding. The witness leaves before gratitude can become another negotiation.

failure.text: The witness repeats your offer instead. For once, everyone in court agrees on exactly what you said.

annual.text: Your joints announce the weather before the sky does. They offer no useful advice about what to do with it.
You choose a seat by how easy it will be to stand up again. There are forms of wisdom nobody puts in books.
You wake before the bell and remember a time when waking was somebody else’s responsibility.
You find a ribbon you meant to throw away years ago. It returns to its box without any firmer decision.
A familiar lane is full of unfamiliar children. You know which of their parents once broke the same fence.
Your oldest coat fits differently now. You blame the mending, which has no voice with which to object.
A young person explains how the world works. You recognise several of your own former errors and let them finish.
A tavern proverb named you wise. By dawn nobody remembered the proverb, only the ale.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'alehouse_proverb', tag: 'ALE', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: 3, health: -1 }, requires: { minAge: 14 } }

annual.text: You take three determined steps towards a stool. {{carer}} catches you before you discover the fourth is missing.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'baby_first_steps', tag: 'INFANCY', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: 2 }, requires: { maxAge: 3 } }

annual.text: Your first clear word is “more.” {{carer}} looks pleased until you begin applying it to everything.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'baby_first_word', tag: 'INFANCY', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: 2, kinRel: { id: 'mother', delta: 3 } }, requires: { maxAge: 3 } }

annual.text: Sir Quackbeard inspects your cradle with the severity of a constable. He objects to the blanket and loses the argument.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'baby_goose_guard', tag: 'INFANCY', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { kinRel: { id: 'goose', delta: 5 } }, requires: { maxAge: 3 } }

annual.text: A winter cough keeps you awake. {{carer}} warms your blanket by the hearth and stays until your breathing settles.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'baby_winter_fever', tag: 'INFANCY', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: -5, kinRel: { id: 'mother', delta: 3 } }, requires: { maxAge: 3 } }

annual.text: A relic seller passed through with Saint Nobody's elbow. It bent suspiciously.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'bad_relic_rumor', tag: 'RELIC', tagColor: C.purpleDark, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { wits: 2 }, requires: { minAge: 10 } }

annual.text: The church bell rang at the wrong hour. Everyone arrived tired and morally early.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'bell_wrong_hour', tag: 'BELLS', tagColor: C.blue, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { faith: 2, health: -1 }, requires: { minAge: 4 } }

annual.text: You lit a candle at the chapel. You feel holier and slightly singed.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'blessing_candle', tag: 'BLESSING', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { faith: 7, path: { church: 1 } }, requires: { minAge: 5 } }

annual.text: Your borrowed boots reach the puddle before you do and leave considerably later.
Your first clay cup leaks. {{carer}} calls it a fine sieve and uses it anyway.
The children play at holding court. The judge is chosen because she owns the stool; the prisoner owns the biscuits.
Sir Quackbeard lets you sit nearby while he preens. It is a quiet friendship with rather strict terms of admission.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'child_goose', tag: 'CHILDHOOD', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { kinRel: { id: 'goose', delta: 4 } }, requires: { maxAge: 10 } }

annual.text: {{carer}} pretends not to notice the crust you save for later. At bedtime there is a second one beside it.
You practise your letters on a broken roof tile. The first good letter is so large that there is no room for the rest of your name.
{{carer}} teaches you a knot that holds under strain. The explanation includes an unflattering account of a cousin’s wedding.
You build a miniature house in the mud and give it a very small door. Visitors will have to be polite enough to shrink.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'child_mud', tag: 'CHILDHOOD', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: 2 }, requires: { maxAge: 8 } }

annual.text: You herd a flock of stones across the yard. They are obedient sheep until someone tries to put one in a pocket.
Your snowman has the reeve’s enormous nose. When the reeve comes past, you hastily add a moustache.
A noble introduces himself by five titles. His creditor waits patiently to use the shortest name.
A courtier recognises you warmly, then checks who is watching before deciding how warmly.
A herald draws a family tree so broad that several disputed ancestors have to stand in the margin.
A petitioner spends half a page calling himself insignificant. The remaining half explains why his neighbour matters even less.
A lord describes his hunt without mentioning the groom who found his horse or the ditch that found his boot.
A councillor calls his support unwavering. The ink is still wet where he altered the recipient’s name.
A portrait improves its subject’s chin. The painter waits to see whether courage or flattery earns the larger fee.
An envoy arrives with a dove embroidered on his sleeve and enough armed men to protect it.
Two dignitaries reach a narrow door together. A useful discussion waits while neither becomes the lesser man.
Your council agrees that the throne needs a cushion. Agreement on anything else is postponed while the cushion is discussed.
annual.mechanics: line('court_royal_chair', 'royal_duties', <TEXT>, { minAge: 16, custom: s => s.world.court?.rulerId === s.playerCharacterId })

annual.text: Your crown makes the same place itch throughout the audience. Nobody has devised a dignified way to scratch beneath a kingdom.
annual.mechanics: line('court_royal_itch', 'royal_duties', <TEXT>, { minAge: 16, custom: s => s.world.court?.rulerId === s.playerCharacterId })

annual.text: The silk cord on a decree costs more than the matter it settles. The councillors discuss the cord first.
A servant brings water before you ask. Among so many people waiting to be noticed, you notice the one who was watching.
A lord calls thirty guests a small supper. The people carrying it do not dispute the adjective until they reach the kitchen.
A food taster asks whether he may object to the cooking on ordinary grounds.
The baker stamps every loaf with his initials. Nobody has asked to sign the small ones.
The well rope catches on a sleeve. A vigorous argument follows about which of the two is supposed to go down.
A cat walks over a freshly copied page. Its contribution is darker, clearer and much less expensive than the scribe’s.
A stool gives way under the only person who had just called the meeting to order.
A cobbler promises shoes that will outlast their owner. An elderly customer asks for a more cheerful recommendation.
You count what you owe instead of sheep. The sheep would at least have had the decency to jump away.
annual.mechanics: line('daily_debt_sleep', 'household_accounts', <TEXT>, { minAge: 16, custom: s => s.debts.some(d => d.principal > 0) })

annual.text: A neighbour hangs washing in a rare patch of sun. Half the lane turns to watch it, as though warmth were a public performance.
The bowls are the same size as last year. Everyone eats more slowly, as though that could fill them.
Frost draws a finer window than the glazier ever managed. You admire it until someone reminds you it is on the inside.
Someone leaves a glowing coal ready for your cold hearth. You never learn who; the room warms anyway.
The last sheaf comes in before the rain. People stand under cover listening to the work they no longer have to do.
The locksmith locks his own stall to demonstrate a new bolt. His apprentice has the key and the afternoon off.
A rope seller demonstrates the strength of his wares by tying up his assistant. The assistant negotiates his wages from there.
A tally stick splits neatly into two matching accounts. You wish every disagreement could be settled by breaking a stick correctly.
Fresh rushes make the floor look respectable. The missing spoon is still under the old respectability.
You can afford the good thread this year. It feels extravagant until you remember what the cheap thread cost in mending.
The soap seller’s hands are cleaner than anyone’s in the square. He keeps dropping the money.
The soup bone is being used for a second day. It has begun to look less like an ingredient than a guest.
For once the soup is thick enough to hold a spoon upright. You eat before anyone mistakes it for building material.
You take a familiar uneven step without looking. Your foot remembers a street your head was too busy to notice.
A sundial gives a precise answer until a cloud arrives. You appreciate an instrument willing to admit it does not know.
A cartwheel returns to the same rut so faithfully that the driver accuses it of having relatives there.
You found dice under a chapel pew. Someone has been praying for sixes.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'dice_under_pew', tag: 'VICE', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { gold: 2, faith: -1 }, requires: { minAge: 10 } }

annual.text: The bell rope wears smooth where generations of hands have pulled it. You hold the same place for a moment.
The sacristan straightens a candle after every prayer. Disorder is the one sin he can reliably put right.
The chapel door whistles through the sermon. It is the only interruption the priest cannot ask to leave.
A friar consults three calendars before deciding whether today requires him to refuse the cheese.
A dispute over a saint’s feast ends when both sides discover that the cook has already served it.
A hermit complains that visitors interrupt his solitude, then asks whether anyone mentioned his new cave.
Someone carries a lantern to a sick neighbour after the chapel closes. There is no audience for the walk home.
A monk draws a tiny sleeping clerk beside a solemn passage on vigilance. You wonder who the book was meant for.
An old hymn brings back a voice you had almost forgotten. You lose the next verse trying to hear it again.
The procession for rain ends in a downpour. The priest claims success from beneath the only dry canopy.
The relic’s case is polished so brightly that nobody can see the bone. The keeper thinks this has improved attendance.
A stranger leaves bread beside the poor box and goes before anyone can praise the gift.
{{child}} adopts your most irritating habit. You defend it much less confidently from the other side of the table.
{{child}} asks why grown people need so many witnesses if they tell the truth. You suddenly remember a pressing chore.
{{child}} falls asleep against your shoulder halfway through a complaint. You stay where you are until your arm goes numb.
You still leave room at the table for someone who will not be coming. This year you notice the space before setting out the bowl.
annual.mechanics: line('family_empty_chair', 'remembrance', <TEXT>, { minAge: 18, custom: s => s.world.characters[s.playerCharacterId].parentIds?.some(id => s.world.characters[id]?.alive === false) === true })

annual.text: A household recipe says “as much as seems right.” Whoever wrote it took the quantity with them.
{{carer}} mends your torn sleeve without asking how it happened. That is how you know the story has already arrived.
There is less bread at supper and more time spent cutting it. Nobody mentions the arithmetic.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'famine', tag: 'FAMINE', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: -7, gold: -1 }, requires: { minAge: 10 } }

annual.text: {{father}} predicts rain from an aching knee. You carry a cloak out of affection and are dry by good fortune.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'father_weather_knee', tag: 'WEATHER', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { wits: 2, kinRel: { id: 'father', delta: 2 } }, requires: { minAge: 6 } }

annual.text: Found a shiny coin in the mud. It is mostly mud, but it spends.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'fortune_coin', tag: 'FORTUNE', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { gold: 3 }, requires: { minAge: 4 } }

annual.text: A merchant counts out six gold too many and rides away. You close your purse before anyone asks you to check it.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'fortune_merchant', tag: 'FORTUNE', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { gold: 6, faith: -2 }, requires: { minAge: 8 } }

annual.text: A friar preached fasting while smelling powerfully of pudding. The village noticed.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'friar_pudding_smell', tag: 'GOSSIP', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { wits: 2, faith: -1 }, requires: { minAge: 8 } }

annual.text: A travelling clerk sketches Sir Quackbeard in the margin of an account. For once the most forceful opinion on the page needs no signature.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'goose_court_news', tag: 'COURT', tagColor: C.blue, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: 2, kinRel: { id: 'goose', delta: 3 } }, requires: { minAge: 8 } }

annual.text: The clerk reads marriage banns so softly that only the objections can be heard.
A bard fits your name into a song by adding two syllables and a crime you have never committed.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'gossip_bard', tag: 'GOSSIP', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: -2 }, requires: { minAge: 6 } }

annual.text: Two courting neighbours speak through a fence. Their chaperone listens from the gate, complaining that the acoustics are poor.
A love letter circulates without a name. Three people blush at the same description of their teeth.
The matchmaker judges a prospect by the state of their shoes. “Love walks,” she says. “Debt sends a messenger.”
The chapel echoes a groom’s promise to obey. His family looks alarmed at having heard it twice.
A lover recites a moving poem. The minstrel listening behind him remembers writing it for someone else.
A suitor praises someone’s fine judgement, then spends an hour explaining why they should choose him.
The jeweller explains that a wedding ring can be made smaller. The listening couples look briefly hopeful.
A bride’s veil catches on the chapel door. Her aunt calls it an omen; the carpenter calls it a nail.
A widow moves her bench into the sun. Three men offer to carry it; she asks the one who brought a cushion.
A clean bowl of water arrives beside your bed. You are too tired to ask who carried it, and less alone for seeing it.
The market sounds very far away while you rest. You promise yourself not to complain about its noise quite so readily.
You sit by an open window long enough to feel the air change. Recovery is less dramatic than anyone’s account of being ill.
A passing knight explains that the dent in his helm saved his life. His squire says the doorway was never in much danger.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'knight_dented_pride', tag: 'MARTIAL', tagColor: C.blue, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { rankProgress: 4, charm: 2 }, requires: { minAge: 12 } }

annual.text: The bailiff’s new hat is too tall for the courthouse door. He makes everyone wait while authority enters sideways.
An official says his hands are clean. The new gloves are quite fine.
The court dog sleeps through an argument over ownership. Both claimants lower their voices rather than wake it.
A strip of sunlight moves across the cell wall. You have learned to tell the hour without asking anyone for anything.
The gaoler calls the soup substantial. You spend the meal looking for the substance.
A cutpurse takes one look at your empty purse and moves along with professional disappointment.
You notice how often people glance at a chest after insisting there is nothing in it.
An official explains that there is a fee for recording a fee. You begin to understand why parchment is dear.
{{rival}} greets you by your full name in public. No friendly person has ever needed quite so much of it.
A clerk refuses an unsigned complaint that the official seal has been stolen.
Every traveller reports a larger army than the last. By supper the enemy has more horses than there are fields to feed them.
Someone has put a cushion in the stocks. The gaoler removes it, on the grounds that punishment should not attract regulars.
The clerk corrects a spelling in a warrant with more care than he gives the accusation beneath it.
The watch changes its password. By dusk everybody knows it except the man who chose it.
A witness clears his throat every time the clerk reaches the useful part. The testimony is eventually adjourned for water.
Someone sold hats for goats. No one agreed whether the hats were for goats or from goats.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'market_goat_hat', tag: 'MARKET', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: 2, wits: 1 }, requires: { minAge: 8 } }

annual.text: {{spouse}} insists you steal the blanket in your sleep. Your waking defence is weakened by possession of the blanket.
{{spouse}} saves you the last pear and says it was too bruised to eat. The bruise is no larger than a thumbnail.
You and {{spouse}} walk home without speaking. It is a comfortable silence, and neither of you spoils it by saying so.
{{spouse}} starts laughing before you reach the end of an old story. You tell it anyway, because that is part of the pleasure.
{{spouse}} repairs your stockings with red thread. You are now easy to identify fleeing a puddle.
You and {{spouse}} tell the story of your wedding differently. Both versions contain an innocent person who looks remarkably like the teller.
The miller measured your flour with a scoop that looked hungry.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'miller_short_measure', tag: 'MILL', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { gold: -2, wits: 2 }, requires: { minAge: 10, minGold: 2 } }

annual.text: A tethered goat loops its rope around your ankle. It watches you untie the knot as though reviewing your work.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'mishap_goat', tag: 'MISHAP', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: -6, charm: -2 }, requires: { minAge: 4 } }

annual.text: You slip beside the watering trough and come up with duckweed in your hair. A bystander turns away to cough very noisily into a sleeve.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'mishap_trough', tag: 'MISHAP', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: -4 }, requires: { minAge: 3 } }

annual.text: A monk explains division with three apples. The lesson becomes subtraction when somebody eats the example.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'monk_bad_sum', tag: 'WISDOM', tagColor: C.blue, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { wits: 4, faith: -1 }, requires: { minAge: 8 } }

annual.text: You wore your best shoes to chapel. The mud wore them better.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'muddy_sabbath', tag: 'SABBATH', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { faith: 3, charm: -1 }, requires: { minAge: 4 } }

annual.text: A poet praises your noble bearing in a verse whose longest word is your title. The short lines cost just as much.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'noble_bad_poem', tag: 'STATION', tagColor: C.purpleDark, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: 2, reputation: 1 }, requires: { rankAtLeast: 2 } }

annual.text: A servant waits for you to finish speaking before retrieving the bowl you are blocking. Rank has made people patient in inconvenient ways.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'noble_envy', tag: 'STATION', tagColor: C.purpleDark, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: 2, reputation: 1 }, requires: { rankAtLeast: 2 } }

annual.text: {{carer}} softens a crust for you, blows on it, and tests it twice. The second test is mostly hunger.
You spend a morning laughing at a ceiling beam. Nobody else can make it perform.
{{carer}} forgets the end of your lullaby and hums instead. You know the missing part and fall asleep waiting.
{{carer}} marks your height on the doorpost. You stand on tiptoe and wait to see whether it counts.
{{carer}} sews a bell to your sleeve to hear where you crawl. You learn to crawl very slowly.
You try to fit an enormous bite into your mouth. Half reaches your chin. You pat it back up with both hands.
{{mother}} finds an old family warning against trusting smiling millers. The warning is written on the back of an unpaid milling bill.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'old_oath_found', tag: 'FAMILY', tagColor: C.purpleDark, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { wits: 3, kinRel: { id: 'mother', delta: 2 } }, requires: { minAge: 8 } }

annual.text: You catch a rough cough during the market sickness scare. Several nights pass without good sleep; even the haggling outside sounds distant.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'plague_cough', tag: 'PLAGUE', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: -9 }, requires: { minAge: 5 } }

annual.text: A sickness scare packed the chapel. The coughs harmonized terribly.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'plague_crowded_prayer', tag: 'PLAGUE', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: -5, faith: 3 }, requires: { minAge: 14 } }

annual.text: The sun darkens briefly. Someone bangs a pan at it. When daylight returns, he looks unbearable.
A traveller teaches you a greeting in a distant tongue. You repeat it until it sounds like a place you might reach.
Ice stills the little bell above a shop. Customers discover how loudly they have been relying on it to announce their honesty.
A glass bead catches the sun and puts a small blue kingdom on your palm. For once nobody asks rent for it.
An old bowl is mended with neat metal staples. Someone decided it was worth keeping, cracks and all.
A rope walker crosses the square above your heads. The crowd holds its breath; his wife holds the collecting bowl steady.
A travelling clockmaker shows a machine that marks each hour. Everyone spends half the afternoon waiting to be told they have wasted it.
A traveller displays a sea creature’s enormous rib. The butcher asks after the rest before believing the story.
The reeve banned suspicious whistling. You whistled innocently and learned nothing.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'reeve_new_rule', tag: 'LAW', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'plain', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: -1, path: { outlaw: 1 } }, requires: { minAge: 12 } }

annual.text: {{rival}} wishes you excellent health with the expression of someone cancelling a small celebration.
You try a knowing smile across the square and receive a puzzled one in return. The misunderstanding is mercifully brief.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'romance_wink', tag: 'ROMANCE', tagColor: C.healthDark, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: 3 }, requires: { minAge: 14 } }

annual.text: You check that a certain chest is locked. It is. You check again, discovering that secrecy is mostly unpaid work.
A loose thread undid half your tunic in the market. The tailor called it ventilation.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'tailor_loose_thread', tag: 'MISHAP', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { charm: -4 }, requires: { minAge: 10 } }

annual.text: The collector takes three gold and gives you a receipt large enough to wrap a much more valuable payment.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'taxman', tag: 'TAXES', tagColor: C.bad, tone: 'bad', text: <TEXT>, effects: { gold: -3 }, requires: { minAge: 12, minGold: 4 } }

annual.text: A turnip grew as large as a helmet. The village called it a sign and then ate it.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'turnip_giant', tag: 'HARVEST', tagColor: C.good, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: 4, faith: 1 } }

annual.text: Full granaries lower the price of bread. You buy a little extra and need no better reason to enjoy it.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'weather_harvest', tag: 'WEATHER', tagColor: C.amber, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { health: 4, gold: 2 }, requires: { minAge: 4 } }

annual.text: A hermit teaches you the words on a milestone. His complaints about visitors become easier to understand.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'wisdom_hermit', tag: 'WISDOM', tagColor: C.blue, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { wits: 6 }, requires: { minAge: 5 } }

annual.text: A monk leaves a space in his sums to show you how nothing can have a place. You think about that on the way home.
annual.mechanics: { id: 'wisdom_zero', tag: 'WISDOM', tagColor: C.blue, tone: 'good', text: <TEXT>, effects: { wits: 5 }, requires: { minAge: 5 } }

annual.text: An apprentice sweeps the workshop into two piles: dirt, and pieces he hopes nobody needs.
There is clean linen ready when you need it. Someone who will never be thanked has done the important part first.
You find an error copied so faithfully that three witnesses have sworn to it. Truth has acquired an untidy margin.
You reach the field before the shouting begins. For a little while it belongs to birds and your own breathing.
The plough catches an old horseshoe. Everyone agrees it is lucky except the person who must straighten the blade.
The guild spends an hour deciding who sits nearest the fire. No trade is conducted, but the importance of rank is kept warm.
A company horse receives better oats than its rider receives bread. Only one of them is allowed to object by biting.
Your ink freezes before your fingers do. For a short time the records are safe from everybody.
The wardens inspect a master’s mark more closely than the object carrying it. Fortunately the mark is excellent.
The forest goes quiet as you approach. Even the hares have learned that discretion is a useful trade.
A companion explains how to leave no tracks while standing in the deepest mud you have seen all week.
Two parishioners quarrel over the draughtiest pew. The cold is bearable; sitting behind the other household is not.
A patient keeps his hat on while describing an ailment of the foot. People guard whatever dignity is still within reach.
A patron asks for a rhyme for his own name. You charge for the difficulty without explaining what it is.
You shake sawdust out of your sleeve after supper. The bench has followed you home in instalments.
A merchant warms his seal so carefully that he stamps the table instead of the deed. The table is now exceptionally well attested.
A cloth buyer produces his own measuring rod. It is noticeably longer when he buys than when he sells.
You learn exactly where an audience coughs when it wants a song to end. The rhythm is unusually consistent.
A patched sheet of vellum makes you write around a hole. The sermon improves when given something it cannot say.
The watch changes in heavy rain. Both guards salute with the enthusiasm of men trading a bad bargain.

lines.text: {{other}} asks you to carry a handsome pie to a juror
{{guardian.intro}} asks you to carry the old charter
{{guardian}} asks you to carry the family record
Hire a clerk to trace the sales Your clerk traces the bales through every sale
Hire a clerk to verify their names Your hired clerk verifies the names and records the exchange
Hire a clerk to survey the ports Your hired clerk surveys the ports and stays in service
Ask {{mentor}} to check the tally {{mentor}} runs a thumb along the fresh mark and shows you where to compare it
Ask {{mentor}} to check the relic list {{mentor}} lays the old list beside yours
Ask {{mentor}} to check the surviving lines {{mentor}} helps you recover the measurements from the unburnt corner
Ask {{mentor}} to check the suspicious names {{mentor}} removes the false entries while you copy the corrected ration order
Ask {{mentor}} to check the disputed arms {{mentor}} helps you trace the descent, then moves the cousins away from the sharp cutlery
Ask {{mentor}} to check the stores with you You count the grain beside {{mentor}} instead of guessing from the tenant’s manners
Ask {{mentor}} to check what can be spared {{mentor}} keeps the seed grain separate while you and {{classmate}} work out the payment
Ask {{mentor}} to check the symptoms with you You work through the diary beside {{mentor}}, marking the actual symptoms before discussing the old explanation
Ask {{mentor}} to check the relief you propose {{mentor}} counts the grain with you before you promise it
